author: Alison Avigayil Ramer
title: After October 7, I learned that movements need grief spaces
content:
This article

After October 7, I learned that movements need grief spaces

 was originally published by

Waging Nonviolence

.


Since the massacres on Oct. 7, now three years ago, the news has brought a steady stream of horror and broken promises. The ceasefire in Gaza has been broken thousands of times; the ceasefire with Iran only holds until the next strike. Many of us have responded by going numb or turning away. Over these three years, I’ve come to believe that collective mourning can help movements build sturdier organizing infrastructure, move through paralysis and numbness, and get back to the long-term work of creating systemic change.


I’ve spent nearly two decades living and working as a human rights defender, mostly in Palestine and Israel. For years, I responded to atrocities the way much of the dominant organizing culture did at the time: strategically. I prepared statements, launched campaigns and mobilized our base. I worked through several wars and the ongoing ethnic cleansing and genocide. Even though my colleagues and I were often physically together, we rarely had the opportunity to collectively mourn. In fact, mourning was often seen as something only the privileged could afford. As organizers and solidarity activists, we were the ones who needed to push past the pain and keep mobilizing.


And then, after each war, large swaths of colleagues and organizers would burn out, and our movement would suffer a setback. Movement researchers Paul Gorski and Cher Chen, studying U.S. human rights and social justice activists, found that an estimated 50 to 60 percent of organizers eventually walk away from movement work and never return, burned out by a culture that treats overwork and self-sacrifice as necessary. That culture also leaves no room to mourn and process the secondary trauma that accumulates, hastening burnout. These kinds of cycles make it especially hard for movements seeking systemic change to sustain themselves.


Sign Up for our Newsletter


We’ll send you a weekly email with the latest articles.


When Hamas attacked Israel in October 2023 and I was waiting in anticipation of the retaliation against Gaza, I knew I couldn’t respond with the same kind of organizing strategy that we usually use: preparation of advocacy statements, social media campaigns and fundraising appeals. I knew that while some people should and would continue that work, there also needed to be spaces for organizers and our base to mourn. And so, on Oct. 8, I opened a space for collective mourning online, sharing it in the many community, political and religious groups I was a part of, for anyone who needed somewhere to process what they were witnessing and feeling. Dozens of people joined: primarily my Jewish community at first, and then people from many faiths and chapters of my life, from Palestine to Palo Alto. 


As the assault on Gaza and the genocide continued, the room stayed open. More colleagues, including community organizers, artists, chaplains and psychologists, joined me in facilitating, and we held space for hundreds of people from across our communities to mourn together. We formed a collective called the

Social Change Sanctuary

 and developed a format that included facilitation and participation from attendees. Over time, we were invited to hold spaces for other communities in mourning. We’ve held spaces to grieve the ongoing genocide; climate catastrophes like the fires in Los Angeles; ICE raids, arrests and murders; and the war on Iran.


The Social Change Sanctuary hosts an Interdependence Day circle in 2025. (Alison Avigayil Ramer)


Participants repeatedly shared the difference it made in their lives to know they had a consistent space to mourn.


“In daily life, when something hurts, I turn away, I distract myself,” one participant told us. “But the collective mourning practice helped me move through the frozenness that constant news induced — helped me stop doomscrolling — and I’m able to return to my work.”


That participant went on to organize her community and raised $20,000 for refugees in Gaza. 


Another participant returned to their role as a chaplain, and extended her work to include “movement chaplaincy” holding one-on-one spaces for people doing solidarity work. 


Many participants also shared how witnessing the news with others enabled them to feel the emotions provoked by the headlines, leaving them feeling less isolated and more connected. That is co-regulation happening at …

author: Sara Fayyazi
title: Addressing the Economic Costs of Sexual Violence: The Survivors’ Rights Restitution Act
content:
On September 15, 2026, Rep. Ayanna Pressley (MA-07), Rep. Teresa Leger Fernandez (NM-03), and Rep. Deborah Ross (NC-02) introduced the Survivors Rights Restitution Act. This legislation would establish a federal restitution program for survivors of sexual violence whose rights were violated by the federal government. The bill would include survivors of abuse by Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell while addressing the financial burden that can occur from sexual violence.

The bill focuses on the economic consequences that survivors can face long after an assault. The estimated lifetime cost of rape at $122,461 per victim, including the expenses of medical care, loss of income, housing instability and mental health support. These expenses can become an additional burden for survivors as they recover from trauma. The proposed restitution program would provide compensation for certain economic and non-economic harms and losses.

Under the legislation, an independent Office of Special Adjudicators for Survivors Restitution would be established within the US Court of Federal Claims. The office would review petitions from survivors and determine awards through what the bill describes as a streamlined, non-adversarial and trauma-informed process. The legislation would also establish a Survivors Rights Restitution Fund within the Department of the Treasury. The funds would be financed through federal forfeiture proceeds connected to trafficking and sexual exploitation offenses, voluntary contributions, and authorized appropriations.

The legislation is also intended to address the gaps in the enforcement of survivors’ existing legal rights. Under the Crime Victims’ Rights Act, survivors have certain protections when they report crimes, including the right to receive timely and accurate notice of an accused person’s release. The bill’s sponsors point to the handling of Jeffrey Epstein’s 2008 plea agreement as an example of these rights not being adequately enforced. The sponsors argue that current law does not provide a specific avenue for financial relief when victims’ rights are violated.

Although the bill is closely connected to the Epstein case, its protections would extend to other survivors of sexual violence more broadly. Rape and sexual assault victimizations occur annually, while approximately two out of three sexual assaults go unreported, the legislation argues that when survivors do come forward, there should be a helpful and easy path towards restitution.

Pressley has experience working with survivors of sexual violence and the Epstein investigation. In May 2026, Pressley and House Oversight Committee Democrats held a field hearing in Palm Beach focused on the Epstein investigation and the long-term economic and emotional harms experienced by survivors.

The legislation has received endorsements from several survivor and women’s rights organizations like World Without Exploitation, me too. International, the National Alliance to End Sexual Violence, and many others.

Financial compensation cannot erase the trauma of sexual violence. However, supporters of the legislation argue that financial restitution can help survivors address some of the costs associated with recovery while providing a mechanism for accountability when the federal government fails to protect their rights.

The Survivors’ Rights Restitution Act would create a process for survivors to seek financial restitution when their rights have been violated by the federal government. The bill addresses not only the immediate consequences of sexual violence but also some of the long-term financial burdens survivors can carry. The legislation now faces the congressional process where it will be considered before any potential action is taken.

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: NTI names Navarana Beveridge its new CEO
content:
This story was updated Tuesday, Oct. 6, 2026, at 5:09 p.m. ET.


Nunavut Tunngavik Inc. has named Navarana Beveridge its new chief executive officer.


The Inuit rights-holding organization in Nunavut announced the appointment Monday in a news release.


Beveridge’s hiring fills a vacancy left by Kilikvak Kabloona, who left in June,

one week after

 beneficiaries elected Gloria Uluqsi as the the organization’s new president on May 27.


“Gloria has just gotten on as NTI’s new president,” Beveridge said in an interview Tuesday. “I met her while she was campaigning and thought she was a very interesting, grounded leader, very genuine in her wanting to make a difference in the communities and working for Inuit. And that really appealed to me.”


“Navarana understands our organizations, our communities and the issues that matter to Nunavut Inuit,” Uluqsi said in the release. “She brings strong leadership experience, but just as importantly, she understands that our work must remain grounded in the people we serve.”


Beveridge said she wanted to join NTI’s leadership because she’s optimistic about Nunavut’s future.


“I think NTI is at a very exciting point in time, where there’s a lot of opportunities and possibilities to do good things,” the she said.


Beveridge was born and raised in Greenland and spent 17 years working at the Qikiqtani Inuit Association, most recently as their senior director of strategic planning. In 2021, the Kingdom of Denmark appointed her as its

honorary consul

 in Nunavut.


She speaks four languages — Inuktitut, English, Kalaallisut and Danish. Throughout her career, she helped negotiate the Mary River iron mine’s Inuit Impact Benefit Agreement and also oversaw the creation of the Qikiqtani Inuit Association’s research and training centre in Pond Inlet, which had its grand opening at the end of September.


Uluqsi said in a news release on Monday that the new CEO “brings strong leadership experience, but just as importantly, she understands that our work must remain grounded in the people we serve.”


Beveridge is expected to officially begin on Oct. 13.


Correction:

This article has been updated to correct information about Kabloona’s departure from NTI.

author: Admin101
title: ATX Solidarity Network is Fighting Wage Theft, La Migra, and Apathy
content:
AK, a founding member of ATX Solidarity Network, discusses their experience organizing immigrant workers to confront wage theft and other issues in right-to-work Texas.


Increased ICE enforcement has raised fears about fighting back, turning many to seek services in a field dominated by


nonprofits. In this interview we explore the tensions organizing for direct action amid these conditions.


Black Rose/Rosa Negra (BRRN): We understand that you all in Austin, Texas have begun to build a solidarity network. What is that? How is it structured?


AK:

 A solidarity network is basically made up of workers and tenants from all over the city (or, in some cases, parts of a city) who have or may have issues with their bosses and landlords. Instead of organizing with our immediate coworkers or neighbors, we are individuals from different workplaces and living in different areas of town who fight for each other where we are at. Solidarity networks are meant to fill the void where workplace unions and tenant unions don’t exist. Since Texas is a “right to work” state, capital strategically undermines workers from building fighting organizations like unions. Solidarity networks are flexible enough to meet one or a few workers at one workplace or tenants at a complex, and temporarily bypass the immediate need for longstanding organizations.  


When you meet someone with a workplace or tenant issue, the whole solidarity network takes on the demands of the case, with those with the grievance–the issue(s) they want to fight around that directly affects them–being core organizers of their own campaign. We use direct action tactics, which means we don’t go through the courts or ask the cops or nonprofits to take care of the situation for us; we rely on just us to get the demand met by putting pressure on the boss or landlord until it becomes so unbearable they have no choice but to give in.


Like most solidarity networks there is a small group of core organizers who respond to the day- to-day needs of the organization. The people with the demands must be a part of this group. Then, there is a larger membership which is involved in many of the functions of the organization, but not all of its functions. They may pass out flyers with us, make phone calls, or research campaign targets, for example. Then there is a much larger network of people who will come out to actions when called on.


BRRN: Walk us through how you started it. Why this kind of organization, and what kinds of fights do you take on?


AK:

 Our specific solidarity network wanted to take on wage theft campaigns as our main, but not exclusive, area of struggle. We began working with another organization here that works in immigrant communities around stopping deportations. They were getting a lot of calls about wage theft, and helped us start the solidarity network to meet this need. Most of our initial calls came directly from them, and our first campaign came out of one of these calls. We also understand that the immigrant community, especially here in Texas, is very vulnerable to wage theft, and they often feel they do not have a lot of options for getting back stolen wages. We want to change that! Eventually, we want to create a citywide network of people who can respond to wage theft grievances, and other workplace and housing issues. We want to make bosses and landlords scared to even think about messing with us! 


In ATX, we have a small and unorganized left with a larger activist scene. A solidarity network is one form of organization that can work well under these conditions because you really only need a handful of core organizers and access to lots of people to show up to actions. We also see this form of organization being one in which committed leftists can develop relationships with other members of the working class. We see a lot of the left in ATX being very insular and removed from other everyday people. We feel it is important to be organizing in working-class communities since it is us as a class that are capable of transforming society. 


We also want to help normalize direct action tactics to push our collective ability to struggle even further. Ultimately, we would like to see more working-class organizations in our neighborhoods, workplaces, schools, and more. The solidarity network isn’t meant to be

the form

 of organization for widespread worker rebellion, but it is one form of organization that can respond to specific conditions that …

title: French Youth Take the Streets against a Bleak Future : A Report
content:
This past week, thousands of teenagers have taken the streets of France, clashing with police as they demonstrate against the deplorable conditions in their high schools and a rapidly collapsing future. This is a promising sign, shifting attention from the seemingly unstoppable rise of the extreme right to the question of what people can do on a grassroots basis to defend themselves. Our correspondents in Paris explore the situation in detail.


Another unprecedented summer of record

heatwaves

,

droughts

, and

wildfires

 throughout Europe underlines the desperate situation we are all facing today, while politicians of all stripes and their techno-industrial sponsors continue to turn a blind eye, forcing us down the path to catastrophe in the name of progress.


Hoping to turn the page on these environmental disasters, the French government has hurriedly shifted focus to other priorities. The coming months represent a crucial transition for Emmanuel Macron and his government, as they will bring Macron’s second term to a close, opening a new political era in France. Candidates are already battling to succeed Macron in power at the beginning of May 2027.


In the midst of this political spectacle, during an increasingly

menacing surge

 in the popularity of the National Rally (formerly, the National Front), the extreme-right party, it is especially meaningful that teenagers have started to organize at a grassroots level to defend themselves. This organizing gained momentum last week, when blockades of high schools, demonstrations, and riots erupted across France, taking everyone by surprise.


Students clash with police forces in Montpellier on October 2, 2026.


Licensed to Kill?


Since Macron was elected President for the first time in May 2017, the political discourse in France has been even more dominated by an emphasis on authoritarian and far-right ideologies in terms of security, immigration, and economic and social issues.


This political shift towards an even more aggressive form of governance has led to increasing state violence targeting the social movements and uprisings that have emerged since. From the eviction of the

ZAD

 at Notre-Dame-des-Landes in 2017 to the

riots

 following the murder of Nahel in 2023, not forgetting the

Yellow Vest

 sequence and the COVID-19 pandemic lockdown experimental

doctrines

, we have experienced a headlong plunge into a world of surveillance, repression, and loss of individual freedoms. This has become today’s new normal.


It was in this already suffocating context that last July, the French government decided to vote on a new bill giving police officers more latitude to use their firearms without consequences—a demand that the far right has promoted for years. If voted through, this legislation could set a

dangerous precedent

, as it would establish “a presumption of ‘legitimate use of arms’ by police and gendarmes ‘in the exercise of their duty’.”


Police arrest a student in Lyons on October 1, 2026.


In other words, not only will police officers be able to freely use their weapons if in any situation they claim to fear for their lives or the lives of others, but authorities will no longer have to prove that the officers acted within the framework of the law, as they are required to do today. It will be up to the victims and their families to provide evidence that the use of firearms was not justified. We can already see how this new law represents a legislative tool enabling law enforcement agents, and therefore, the state, to cover up future murders.


Unwilling to let such a law pass without resistance, political opponents and radicals, who had rightly rebranded this law the “license to kill,” decided to organize massive demonstrations and events throughout France on the weekend of September 18 to 20.

Thousands

 of people took part in these protests in different major cities alongside traditional leftist politicians, rights groups such as Amnesty International and the League of Human Rights, and various lawyers and magistrates’ unions.

author: Valerie Anne
title: Horror Comedy ‘The Blood Countess’ Imagines Elizabeth Báthory as a Lesbian Vampire
content:
If I had a nickel for every piece of queer media about 17th century Hungarian countess Elizabeth Báthory released this year, I’d have two nickels. Which isn’t a lot, but it’s weird that it happened twice. After her strange appearance in Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story, she also appears in the vampire horror comedy The Blood Countess directed and co-written by lesbian filmmaker Ulrike Ottinger. In the film, Báthory (played by Isabelle Huppert) wakes from a long slumber and finds herself in modern-day Vienna, searching for a book that could cure her vampirism.

I find two things interesting about the fact that the countess has appeared in two queer adaptations this year. The first is that Lizzie Borden actually never really portrayed her as a lesbian, even though she was set up parallel to Lizzie and lesbian serial killer Aileen Wuornos and was played by the same actress who played Lizzie’s lover. Before the much-later rumors that Elizabeth Báthory bathed in the blood of virgin girls, the crimes she was accused of were more along the lines of torture and cannibalism. So it’s interesting that was then interpreted as lesbianism. Then again, she was luring young women to her castle with three of her closest gal pals, so, who knows I guess. It is just fascinating to me that despite the fact that she has been in folklore for centuries, no new media has come out about her in years, and now these two instances pop up in the same year. Three, if you count the experimental film Báthory by Carlos Atanes. Something seems to be in the (bloody) water.

Unfortunately, it seems like perhaps The Blood Countess isn’t quite as gay as it could be. Then again, apparently Ottinger wrote the screenplay in 1998, almost 30 years ago, so that could potentially account for that. But still, I won’t say no to a lesbian vampire film so I’ll probably still check it out when it makes its North American theatrical release in spring 2027.

author: Taina Da Silva
title: Near Grassy Narrows, an Elder shows us how using the land also protects it
content:
Anishinaabe Elder Gwawich’s Land Back Garden on the outskirts of the Grassy Narrows First Nation. Photo by Taina Da Silva


I’m thinking about the power of my treaty rights as I drive to meet with Anishinaabe Elder Gwawich — Roberta Keesick — on a late summer day on the outskirts of Grassy Narrows.


Gwawich is an activist and trapper who has substantial experience of being on the land and creating land-based learning systems for our community. She grew up in our territory with a traditional Anishinaabek family, and she works to restore our traditional ways. 


As I pull into the site, Gwawich offers me some ripe vegetables — a squash, green beans and tomatoes — that she’s harvested from an extensive garden nearby. 


Gwawich and I are ten minutes outside of the reserve line of Grassy Narrows First Nation, a small and semi-remote community in northwestern Ontario. We sit at an off-grid campsite and community garden which Gwawich started by herself to host her Seven Grandfathers Teachings Program.


The Seven Grandfather Teachings — love, respect, bravery, truth, honesty, humility, and wisdom — are what Gwawich’s social program follows, and she hopes her program will impact Grassy in a way that will bring us Anishinaabek back to the land and culture. 


“Colonization has changed our ways of thinking,” she says. 


A lake in the traditional homelands of Grassy Narrows First Nation. Photo by Taina Da Silva


As the lake glistens in the background, Gwawich talks about how she is determined to decolonize our community from decades of learned behaviour — stemming from the reserve system that relocated people in our community, to the residential “school” system and

devastating mercury pollution

, which have all been an upheaval to our traditional ways.


Her campsite is available for any band members who want to get away from the reserve, and the garden is another free resource where members are often invited to pick fresh food.


“Land Back Garden” is painted on a wooden sign and it sits front-and-centre of the garden. Another sign near the campsite greets visitors to the “Seven Grandfather Teachings Program — Land Based Family Healing Initiative.”

This program is how families from Grassy are now able to access different opportunities designed to bring land based learning to the community, and it is what our aboriginal land title permits us to do in our territories. 


Anishinaabe Elder Gwawich’s program is helping Grassy Narrows members return to their traditional ways. Photo by Taina Da Silva


What started as a community-wide gardening initiative in 2020 has grown into the off-grid garden and campsite, a monthly food program in the community, and a small sewing building right in the reserve — all operating through outside funding.


Children from the reserve are able to experience what it might have been like for the older generations to gather traditionally, share food, and play games like the old days — and with some contemporary additions.


Today, there are community events with bungee trampolines, rock climbing, horse rides and even a zipline, Gwawich tells me with true pride. 


Gwawich speaks excitedly about a farmers’ market coming up, where she will be taking vegetables from the Land Back Garden to give away to Grassy families. 


She reminds me that “being out on the land makes our rights stronger,” and that running the site is a way to protect the land — and our rights under Treaty 3.


This is an area of land which I mistakenly used to associate as a settler hunting camp on so-called “Crown land,” before I learned about traditional land use areas and our history of ancient rock paintings, burial grounds and artifacts found across our territory. 


It takes community members like Gwawich to figure out ways to navigate the colonial systems that have been imposed on us, and decolonize our ways of thinking.


Gwawich remembers a time when the entirety of Grassy Narrows spoke our language and lived off trapping and fishing incomes when she was a child in the 1960s and 70s. 


“Even my siblings were helping with trapping and fishing when they were nine and ten years old,” she said, and we laughed at the idea of that happening now — because that is a lost tradition for Anishinaabek families.


Residential “schools” — an intentional violation of our human rights — and the resulting language and culture loss are not easily forgotten about in our communities. Repairing the losses and devastation is not a simple …

author: Chad Nelson
title: နိုင်ငံရေးသမားတွေရဲ့ ရွှေ့ပြောင်းအခြေချသူတွေအပေါ် တိုက်ခိုက်မှုဟာ တကယ်တော့ အာရုံလွှဲတာပါပဲ
content:
Chad Nelson

.

The Political Class’s War on Immigrants is a Diversion

, January 30, 2015. Translated into Burmese by Hein Htet Kyaw.


ဂျန်နဝါရီ ၂၈ ရက်နေ့မှာ လော်ရက်တာ လင်းချ် (Loretta Lynch) ကို အစိုးရရှေ့နေချုပ် အဖြစ် ခန့်အပ်ဖို့ အမေရိကန် ဆီးနက်စစ်ဆေးမေးမြန်းခြင်း စတင်ချိန်မှာ၊ ရီပတ်ဘလစ်ကန်တွေဟာ အစိုးရက “တရားမဝင် ခိုးဝင်သူတွေ” လို့ သတ်မှတ်ထားတဲ့ လူတန်းစားအပေါ် သူမ ဘယ်လောက်အထိ အလိုက်သင့် ပေါင်းသင်းမလဲဆိုတာ မေးဖို့ အရမ်းစိတ်အားထက်သန်နေကြတာပါ။ ရွှေ့ပြောင်းအခြေချသူတွေအပေါ် တင်းကြပ်တဲ့ ဂျက်ဖ် ဆက်ရှင်နိစ် (Jeff Sessions – R-AL) နဲ့ အပြန်အလှန် မေးမြန်းမှုတစ်ခုမှာ၊ ဆက်ရှင်နိစ်က အမေရိကမှာ အလုပ်လုပ်ပိုင်ခွင့် ဘယ်သူ့မှာ ရှိလဲဆိုတာ လင်းချ် ဘယ်လိုယုံကြည်လဲ မေးခဲ့ပါတယ်။ သီးသန့်အနေနဲ့ပြောရရင်၊ “ဘယ်သူက ပိုပြီး လုပ်ပိုင်ခွင့်ရှိသလဲ – တရားဝင်လာတဲ့ ရွှေ့ပြောင်းအခြေချသူလား၊ နိုင်ငံသားလား၊ ဒါမှမဟုတ် တိုင်းပြည်ထဲ တရားမဝင် ဝင်လာတဲ့သူလား” လို့ သူက မေးခဲ့တာပါ။ လင်းချ်ကတော့ ဆက်ရှင်နိစ်ရဲ့ မေးခွန်းအတုအယောင်ကို လိမ္မာပါးနပ်စွာ ရှောင်လွှဲခဲ့ပြီး၊ လူတစ်ယောက်ဟာ ဒီမှာ တရားမဝင် ရှိနေရင်တောင် အမေရိကရဲ့ လုပ်သားအင်အားထဲမှာ ပါဝင်သူတစ်ယောက်အနေနဲ့ ရှိနေတာကိုပဲ ပိုသဘောကျတယ်လို့ ပြန်ဖြေခဲ့ပါတယ်။


ဆက်ရှင်နိစ်ရဲ့ မေးခွန်းထုတ်ပုံနည်းလမ်းနဲ့ သူလိုချင်နေတဲ့ အဖြေ ဟာ နိုင်ငံရေးသမားတွေရဲ့ လိမ်ညီနေတဲ့ အတွေးအခေါ်ကို အများကြီး ဖော်ပြနေပါတယ်။ ဝါရှင်တန်က နှစ်ပါတီစလုံးမှာပါတဲ့ ရွှေ့ပြောင်းအခြေချသူတွေကို တိုက်ခိုက်တဲ့အုပ်စုက ရှယ်လ်ဒွန် ရစ်ချ်မန်း (Sheldon Richman) မှတ်ချက်ပြုသလိုပဲ “အလုပ်လုပ်ခွင့် ပေးပိုင်ခွင့်ဆိုတာ သူတို့ပေးမှ ရတာ” လို့ ယုံကြည်ထားကြတာပါ။ ဝမ်းနည်းစရာက အဲဒီယုံကြည်ချက်ဟာ ဒီတိုင်းပြည်ရဲ့ ဥပဒေဖြစ်နေတာပါပဲ။ ဒီနေ့ခေတ်မှာ ဘယ်သူအလုပ်လုပ်ခွင့်ရှိလဲဆိုတဲ့ မေးခွန်းကို ဝါရှင်တန်က ဗျူရိုကရက်တွေနဲ့ သူတို့ဆီကနေ လုပ်ပိုင်ခွင့် လက်ဝါးကြီးအုပ်ခွင့် လာဝယ်နေတဲ့ အကျိုးစီးပွားကာကွယ်ရေး အုပ်စုတွေကပဲ အဓိက ဆုံးဖြတ်နေကြတာပါ။ မင်းအနေနဲ့ ကိုယ်ကြိုက်တဲ့ အလုပ်ကို လွတ်လပ်စွာ လုပ်ပိုင်ခွင့်ရှိတယ်လို့ ထင်ချင်ထင်နေလိမ့်မယ်၊ ဒါပေမဲ့ အစိုးရက စည်းကမ်းချက်တွေ အမျိုးမျိုး ထုတ်ပြန်ပြီး မင်းရဲ့ ရွေးချယ်ခွင့်တွေကို အများကြီး ကျဉ်းမြောင်းအောင် လုပ်ပစ်လိုက်တာပါ။ အဲဒီအတားအဆီးတွေကို ကျော်လွှားနိုင်ခဲ့ရင်တောင် အစိုးရ သတ်မှတ်ထားတဲ့ စည်းမျဉ်းစည်းကမ်း နွံထဲမှာ ရုန်းကန်နေရတာနဲ့တင် မင်းရဲ့ ကျွမ်းကျင်မှုကို အပြည့်အဝ ထုတ်မသုံးနိုင်တော့ဘဲ ဖြစ်နေရပါတယ်။


နိုင်ငံရေးသမားတွေဟာ သူတို့ရဲ့ ပြည်သူတွေအပေါ် လွှမ်းမိုးချုပ်ကိုင်ထားနိုင်ဖို့ ဒီလိုမျိုး အရမ်းအရေးပါတဲ့ လုပ်ပိုင်ခွင့်ကို မှီခိုနေကြတာပါ။ ပြည်သူတွေကို အလုပ်လုပ်ခွင့် ပေးပိုင်ခွင့်ရှိနေတာ၊ နဲ့ အဲဒီခွင့်ပြုချက်နဲ့အတူ ပါလာတဲ့ စည်းကမ်းသတ်မှတ်ချက်တွေ အားလုံးက ကပ်ပါး နိုင်ငံရေးသမားတွေကို သူတို့အိတ်ကပ်ထဲ အထိရောက်ဆုံး နည်းလမ်းနဲ့ ပိုက်ဆံထည့်နိုင်အောင် ကူညီပေးထားပါတယ်။ အလုပ်တစ်ခုဟာ တရားမဝင် ရွှေ့ပြောင်းအခြေချသူရဲ့ အလုပ်ဖြစ်ဖြစ်၊ အမေရိကန် မှောင်ခိုဈေးကွက်က အလုပ်သမားရဲ့ အလုပ်ဖြစ်ဖြစ် စည်းမျဉ်းမရှိတဲ့ ဈေးကွက်တွေဆီ လမ်းကြောင်းပြောင်းသွားရင် နိုင်ငံရေးသမားတွေအနေနဲ့ အဲဒါကို စောင့်ကြည့်ဖို့နဲ့ ဆက်ကြေးတောင်းဖို့ ခက်သွားပါတယ်။ သူတို့ရဲ့ ရှုပ်ထွေးလှတဲ့ အခွန်၊ လုပ်အား၊ နဲ့ အုပ်ချုပ်ရေး ဥပဒေတွေကို မလိုက်နာရင်၊ သက်ဆိုင်ရာ အသက်မွေးဝမ်းကျောင်း လုပ်ငန်းတစ်ခုလုံးပေါ်မှာ လိုင်စင်စနစ်တွေ အထပ်ထပ် တင်ထားတာကို မလိုက်နာရင် မင်းရဲ့ အသက်မွေးဝမ်းကျောင်းလုပ်ငန်းပါ ရုတ်တရက် ဖျက်ဆီးခံရနိုင်ခြေ ရှိပါတယ်။ ဒီစနစ်တစ်ခုလုံးကို ထုတ်လုပ်သူတွေနဲ့ စားသုံးသူတွေကို ကာကွယ်ပေးနေပါတယ်ဆိုပြီး အတုအယောင် လိမ်ညာရောင်းချထားတာပါ။


တရားမဝင် ရွှေ့ပြောင်းအခြေချမှု သက်သက်က ဗျူရိုကရက်တွေကို ခြိမ်းခြောက်နေတာ မဟုတ်ပါဘူး။ သူတို့ အမှန်တကယ် ကြောက်တာက ထိန်းချုပ်မထားတဲ့ ရွှေ့ပြောင်းလုပ်သားတွေဆီကရတဲ့ ဝင်ငွေလမ်းကြောင်းတွေကို ချုပ်ကိုင်ခွင့် ဆုံးရှုံးသွားမှာကိုပါ။ ဆက်ရှင်နိစ်နဲ့ ကွန်ဂရက်ထဲက သူ့လို နယ်စပ်စောင့် စိစစ်ရေးသမားတွေဟာ သူတို့ကြောက်ရွံ့မှုကို “ငါတို့ နဲ့ သူတို့” ဆိုတဲ့ စကားလုံးတွေနဲ့ ဖုံးကွယ်ပြီး ရေးကြီးခွင်ကျယ် စကားလုံးအလှတွေ သုံးနေကြတာပါ၊ ဒါဟာ အရေးပါတဲ့ နိုင်ငံရေး ရည်ရွယ်ချက်အတွက် ပြုလုပ်ထားတဲ့ ပြဇာတ်တစ်ခုပါပဲ။ ဒီလို လှည့်ကွက်မျိုးနဲ့ နိုင်ငံရေးသမားတွေက မင်းတို့ကို လှည့်စားထားတာပါ။ သူတို့ ကြောက်နေတာဟာ အခွန်ဘဏ္ဍာ ဆုံးရှုံးမှာကို မဟုတ်ဘဲ၊ “မင်းတို့ရဲ့” အလုပ်တွေ၊ “မင်းတို့ရဲ့” ကျန်းမာရေးစောင့်ရှောက်ခွင့်တွေ၊ နဲ့ “မင်းတို့ရဲ့” လူမှုဖူလုံရေးတွေ ဆုံးရှုံးမှာကို ကြောက်နေရတာပါဆိုပြီး ယုံအောင် လှည့်စားထားတာပါ။ တရားဝင် ရှိနေပြီး အလုပ်လုပ်နေသူတွေ (အခွန်ဆောင်နေသူတွေ) ကိုတော့ မျိုးချစ်စိတ်ရှိသူတွေအဖြစ် သတ်မှတ်ပေးထားပါတယ်။ အစိုးရက သူတို့ရဲ့ လစာထဲက ဖြတ်တောက်ယူနေတာကို မုန်းတီးစရာလို့ မမြင်ဘဲ အားလုံးရဲ့ ကောင်းဖက်အတွက် အရေးပါတဲ့ ပါဝင်ဆောင်ရွက်မှုအဖြစ် ကြိုဆိုကြရပါတယ်။ ခွင့်ပြုချက်မရှိဘဲ အလုပ်လုပ်သူတွေကိုတော့ ရန်သူတွေ၊ တရားဝင် အလုပ်လုပ်နေသူတွေရဲ့ မွန်မြတ်တဲ့ အလုပ်ကို ဖျက်ဆီးနေသူတွေအဖြစ် ပုံဖော်ကြပါတယ်။ “မင်းတို့” က လူကောင်း၊ “သူတို့” က လူဆိုး ပေါ့။ နိုင်ငံရေးအရ အင်အားမရှိတဲ့ တရားမဝင် ရွှေ့ပြောင်းအခြေချသူတွေဟာ ဝါရှင်တန်အတွက် တိုက်ခိုက်ရ အလွယ်ဆုံး ပစ်မှတ်ဖြစ်နေပြီး နိုင်ငံရေးသမားတွေရဲ့ စိတ်ကူးယဉ် ပြဿနာရှာမှုတွေအတွက် လွယ်လွယ်ကူကူ …

author: Elizabeth Weill-Greenberg
title: Activists Are Pushing Cities and Companies to Cancel Parking Contracts With ICE
content:
The Trump administration’s abduction and deportation machine is multifaceted. There are clear-cut components — agents, shackles, and jails — and less obvious, although no less essential, ones — cars and parking spaces.


In an effort to impede the attacks on immigrants, mayors of some of the country’s largest cities, including

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani

,

Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson

, and

Boston Mayor Michelle Wu

, have issued executive orders

banning Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)

 from using city-owned parking lots and properties.


But even in cities where mayors have banned ICE from using government-owned properties, ICE still has free reign to contract with private companies. After the federal agency

posted a notice

 seeking “Surge Parking” in 14 cities, including Boston, Wu

released a public letter

 to

local parking garage and lot owners

, warning them that if ICE were “to procure such resources, it would constitute an unprovoked and unwarranted escalation, creating potentially significant risks to public safety and halting economic activity across our entire region.”


“Today, I ask you to join us: Reject any proposition by ICE to facilitate an attack on the people of Boston,”

she wrote

. “In the face of escalating attacks on cities across the country, we have repeatedly seen that the strongest defense is solidarity.”


In the Boston suburb of Burlington, Massachusetts, Bearing Witness New England has been holding weekly protests outside ICE’s Boston Field Office, where people are

held for days

 in inhumane conditions. Activists say ICE has been keeping its vehicles in a nearby parking lot owned by local developer National Development.


According to a report by

NPR

 affiliate

WBUR

, the company sent a letter to local activists in February, stating that ICE vehicles were being “improperly parked” in its parking spaces, and that it had “reached an arrangement with ICE that they would no longer park their vehicles on our property.”


However, the company also said that the government agency, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), has

rights to use the garage

 and the company does not have authority over how the FAA parcels out parking spaces to other federal agencies, according to

WBUR

’s report.


Nathan Phillips, a Boston University professor who organizes with the Burlington-area coalition

Building Up Resilience Networks (B.U.R.N.)

, says ICE has continued to park in sections of lots National Development leases to the FAA that exceed what the lease allows.


Protests that target parking garages are “throwing sand in the gears” of ICE’s deportation and abduction machine, he says.


“So much of their operation depends on logistics of transport and travel,” Phillips told

Truthout

. “It’s human trafficking, and so if we can go after the trafficking, the means by which they’re doing this, that can have a really effective impact.”


The Appeal in Your Inbox


Subscribe to our newsletters for regular updates, analysis and context straight to your email.


          Sign Up


Fellow B.U.R.N. activist Josh Model says National Development’s recent actions contradict its public image as a

philanthropic company

 committed to improving communities.


“National Development Corporation, which, as a local developer, likes to promote that they’re cognizant of community needs and give to charity and all these nice things,” but they’re “letting ICE stage kidnappings” from their property, said Model.


While the government spending website,

usaspending.gov

, only lists 12 active contracts for parking spaces, as of September 28, the true number of parking lots that ICE uses is likely much higher, said Model. It’s difficult to untangle where ICE is parking, in part, because many of the contracts are not with ICE, but through another federal agency, the

General Services Administration

 (GSA), he said. The GSA manages government buildings and real estate, and owns or leases space in more than 8,300 buildings, according to an

explainer

 on the agency published by the Congressional Research Service.


In the case of National Development, ICE is using parking leased by the GSA for the FAA, according to Model.

PPA website

 states that, among other responsibilities, it coordinates “the efforts of public agencies concerning parking” and establishes and operates public …

author: Thiago Domenici
title: Processo da Advocacia da União contra bets tem 14 empresas que passaram impunes por CPI
content:
Em junho de 2025, a CPI das Bets terminou em pizza – como se diz quando uma investigação acaba sem punir ninguém. Mas agora, mais de um ano depois, as empresas que passaram impunes pela comissão estão de volta, desta vez como alvos de uma ação civil pública na Justiça.


No dia 28 de setembro, a Advocacia-Geral da União (AGU)

entrou

 na Justiça Federal em Pernambuco contra 17 empresas ligadas a 20 marcas de apostas online, pedindo ressarcimento de gastos pela União.

A

Agência Pública

 cruzou essa lista com a documentação reunida pelos senadores da CPI e descobriu que ao menos 14 delas estavam nos documentos da comissão como remetentes ou beneficiárias de transferências financeiras. Dessas, 12 foram citadas no relatório final.

 Esse documento, da então senadora Soraya Thronicke (Podemos-MS) – que não foi reeleita neste ano -, foi rejeitado por 4 votos a 3.


Na ação da AGU, o órgão pede que as empresas de apostas ressarcem o Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS) pelo tratamento de apostadores adoecidos, custo que o Ministério da Saúde (MS) estima em, no mínimo, R$ 2,6 bilhões. Pede também R$ 1 bilhão por danos morais coletivos e a devolução em dobro do que as pessoas diagnosticadas com ludopatia apostaram.


Aparecer nos papéis da CPI não indica, por si só, irregularidade. Nem todas as empresas aparecem como suspeitas. A Superbet, por exemplo, surge como titular legítima de uma autorização que outra plataforma teria usado indevidamente. Duas, a OIG e a Ventmear (Sportingbet), estão ligadas a pedidos de indiciamento, todos contra pessoas, não contra as empresas. Seis delas, OIG, Esportes Gaming, NSX, Ventmear, BPX e Foggo (Blaze), somam cerca de 31% do mercado, segundo as contas da própria AGU, e ocupam lugar de destaque nas 541 páginas deixadas por Thronicke.


Muitas siglas: Bets, CPI, MP de Lula e Fux no STF


A ação da AGU veio três dias depois da

Medida Provisória 1.394

, assinada pelo presidente Lula, que

proíbe

 as apostas de quota fixa, tira as plataformas do ar até 6 de outubro e extingue as autorizações em 30 dias, sem devolver o que as empresas pagaram pelas outorgas.

Se o Congresso não aprovar a MP em até 120 dias de tramitação, prazo suspenso durante o recesso parlamentar, ela perde a validade.

 A CPI já havia ido nessa direção: entre as vinte medidas do relatório derrubado estava a proibição de cassinos on-line, como o Tigrinho.


A Associação Nacional de Jogos e Loterias (ANJL) e o Instituto Brasileiro de Jogo Responsável (IBJR) já apresentaram pedido a Luiz Fux, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), para suspensão dos efeitos da medida provisória.


Nesta segunda-feira, 5 de outubro, a AGU pediu que o STF rejeite a suspensão da Medida Provisória. Na manifestação, assinada pelo advogado-geral Jorge Messias, a AGU sustenta que o marco legal das bets, formado pelas leis 13.756/2018 e 14.790/2023, era “extensamente falho” e falhava em autorização, fiscalização, publicidade e prevenção à lavagem de dinheiro. Para concluir, a peça diz que “o ‘dragão’ era indomável”. O órgão cita dados oficiais segundo os quais os registros no SUS ligados ao jogo patológico cresceram 140% entre 2018 e 2025, e as apostas retiraram R$ 62,5 bilhões dos orçamentos familiares só em 2025. A AGU também pediu que o procurador-geral da República seja ouvido em 72 horas e sugeriu uma nova audiência pública sobre o tema, atualizando a realizada em novembro de 2024.


Como a CPI terminou em pizza


Em 26 de novembro de 2024, Fernando Oliveira Lima, o Fernandim OIG, sentou-se diante dos senadores da CPI das Bets amparado por um habeas corpus. Tinha 33 anos, disse ter estudado até o primeiro ano do ensino médio e se apresentou como empresário de tecnologia, criador de jogos para o Facebook que teriam alcançado 250 milhões de usuários durante a pandemia. Os senadores exibiram dois vídeos e perguntaram se ele conhecia os sites 7Games, R7Games e Betão. Ele conhecia e disse que pertenciam à OIG Gaming Brazil, da qual é sócio. Perguntaram se era dono do “jogo do tigrinho”, mas ele negou. Respondeu que a OIG pagava para oferecê-lo. O empresário contou ainda que, naquela mesma semana, a empresa havia sido uma das primeiras a obter a aprovação completa do Ministério da Fazenda para operar.


A CPI das bets a fez audiência com depoimentos de três representantes de casas de apostas, entre eles Fernando Oliveira Lima, CEO da OIG Group


Fernando não era o único convocado do dia. A pauta listava também João Studart, dono da Betnacional, e Marcus …

author: Esperanza
title: Dúo Kosa presenta Quién es quién: investigación escénica de terror y danza contemporánea
content:
El colectivo de investigación y creación en artes escénicas, Dúo Kosa, presentará su obra de danza contemporánea “Quién es quién” los días 8, 9 y 10 de octubre a las 20:00 horas en Teatro Trashumantes, Temuco. Una exploración por las posibilidades del horror como lenguaje corporal, a partir de intersecciones entre coreografía, terror y niñez.


Desde 2021, Dúo Kosa desarrolla una práctica de danza contemporánea centrada en la investigación coreográfica y en la creación de imágenes corporales que emergen desde lo inestable, lo desplazado y lo ambiguo. “Nuestro trabajo entiende la composición como un campo de experimentación situado y abierto a la anomalía, donde la escena se convierte en un espacio de estudio y de urgencia poética”, comenta Alex Sanzana, artista escénica de Temuco.


En

Quién es quién

, esa búsqueda se encuentra con una pregunta: ¿cómo se coreografía el terror? El proyecto comenzó desde una aproximación audiovisual y fotográfica, a partir de la imagen de dos cuerpos unidos por camisas cosidas, formando una especie de cuerpo transversal y alargado. “Aquella imagen, al mismo tiempo tenebrosa, viscosa y tierna, fue desplazando la investigación hacia la práctica coreográfica y abrió la pregunta que sostiene actualmente la obra”, recuerda Pipi Villadangos, artista escénico de Buenos Aires, integrante de Dúo Kosa.


Aunque el terror ha sido ampliamente explorado por el cine y la literatura, su presencia en la danza aparece aquí como una oportunidad para tensionar los imaginarios del horror en lugar de reproducir sus clichés. En

Quién es quién

, el miedo no se construye únicamente desde aquello que se representa, sino desde aquello que ocurre en el cuerpo: una textura, una vibración, un ritmo dislocado, un gesto suspendido o una oscilación permanente entre ternura y amenaza.


La niñez ocupa un lugar central en esta investigación. Duo Kosa recurre al llamado “tiempo niño”, entendido como ese estado de imaginación absorbente en que el juego puede suspender la lógica cotidiana, para aproximarse al miedo desde una dimensión sensorial y afectiva. Así, la escena se sitúa en un territorio ambiguo entre lo real y lo fantasmático: un cuerpo que juega mientras imagina que algo acecha detrás de la puerta.


La obra se estructura en cuatro cuadros y presenta una ficción campesina protagonizada por tres figuras ambiguas: dos niños que juegan en el bosque y un espantapájaros que parece marcar el camino hacia una trampa. Entre presencias invisibles, mutaciones entre lo humano y lo animal y ensoñaciones lúgubres, la escena construye un paisaje donde la imaginación infantil convive con lo inquietante. Juegos, embestidas, sospechas, alegrías y misterios atraviesan una danza en la que fuerzas extrañas parecen transformar permanentemente el territorio.


Quién es quién

 es también el resultado de un proceso de investigación sostenido en el tiempo. La obra comenzó con un laboratorio en Espacio Kom de Temuco en 2023, y continuó con una residencia de investigación en Teatro Puerto de La Serena, durante el 2024. En 2026, el proceso llegó nuevamente a Temuco para una residencia técnica y una apertura de proceso en Teatro Trashumantes.


De esta manera, la presentación en Teatro Trashumantes da continuidad a un proceso que ha transitado por distintos espacios de investigación y creación, consolidando una propuesta que utiliza la danza para explorar aquello que resulta difícil de nombrar: el miedo, la imaginación, la amenaza y esa zona incierta donde lo tierno puede volverse inquietante.


Sinopsis:

 La danza, la comedia y el terror se encuentran en este montaje para desatar anomalías en las líneas discursivas, a partir de una serie de acontecimientos atemporales que van llevando a los personajes por juegos, embestidas, sospechas, alegrías y misterios. Tal como sucedería en un cuento de fantasía, fuerzas externas o extrañas provocan texturas y escalofríos en el baile de dos niños que juegan compenetrados mientras un monstruo acecha tras los árboles.


Las entradas se compran mediante la web

 y tienen un valor mínimo de 4500 pesos. Clasificación para mayores de 14 años. Pueden entrar menores de edad con un adulto acompañante.

 Teatro Trashumantes, Temuco.

author: Andrés
title: Cuerpos que piensan, cuerpos que resisten: la danza tomó el Centro Cultural Universitario Paco Urondo
content:
Iara Pavanello, Dulcinea Segura Rattagan y Carolina Bergero, el equipo del IAE encargado de la curaduría del encuentro


Durante dos intensas jornadas, el Instituto de Artes del Espectáculo de la UBA reunió a decenas de investigadoras, bailarinas, creadores y docentes de distintos puntos del país y de Latinoamérica para pensar una pregunta urgente: ¿qué hacen los cuerpos cuando los poderes fácticos tienen tanto interés de desmaterializarlos? El VI Encuentro de Pensamiento sobre Danza y Prácticas Somáticas, titulado «Cuerpos en estado de resistencia» combinó ponencias académicas, talleres participativos, funciones y proyecciones de videodanza en un formato mixto que permitió seguir las actividades de manera presencial, y virtualmente. El Centro Cultural Universitario Paco Urondo fue el escenario para el despliegue artístico. Su arquitectura de estilo academicista funcionó como el cuerpo receptor del 6° enc

uentro de prácticas somáticas.

Por ANRed.


El 1 y 2 de octubre, el Área de danza y artes del movimiento del IAE-UBA,

que coordina la investigadora especialista en danza Dulcinea Segura Rattagan, junto al equipo que componen Iara Pavanello y Carolina Bergero

, organizó una nueva edición de su encuentro anual, que desde hace seis años viene consolidándose como uno de los espacios de reflexión sobre el cuerpo más importantes del ámbito académico porteño.


La convocatoria superó el formato de jornada universitaria tradicional:

43 ponencias distribuidas en dos días reunieron a más de cincuenta expositores/ as

, con una variedad de voces que incluyó a estudiantes de grado y posgrado, investigadores del CONICET, docentes de conservatorios, trabajadores de la salud y representantes de escuelas de formación artística.


Taller exploratorio de investigación corporal, por Soledad Manrique


Lo federal

fue una

 marca del encuentro

. A la participación de universidades porteñas y bonaerenses —la UBA, la UNA y la Universidad Nacional de Río Negro— se sumaron

expositoras de Chaco, Rosario, Córdoba y Neuquén

, además de la presencia internacional: Brasil, Chile, Colombia, Uruguay y España representados a través de ponencias que pusieron en diálogo tradiciones corporales y de la danza de muy variada procedencia. Del ballet barroco al zaar sudanés; desde la danza gawazi egipcia hasta las memorias somáticas de comunidades indígenas del Chaco argentino. La amplitud geográfica se tradujo en una conversación rica, donde

la pregunta por la resistencia se formuló desde contextos culturales y políticos diferentes

, sin perder nunca el hilo común.


«Estamos volviendo a casa» obra del grupo Bailarines toda la vida, del grupo de Danza Comunitaria dirigido por Aurelia Chimelli


La dinámica de trabajo favoreció esa multiplicidad. Las mesas temáticas, organizadas en bloques de entre cuatro y seis exposiciones breves, permitieron que cada jornada avanzara a ritmo ágil, con un diálogo rico de temas, que permitieron tender puentes entre un trabajo sobre eutonía y una reflexión sobre psicodrama, o con una investigación sobre danza y salud mental.

El tema: la resistencia

, sumada a la cuidadosa curaduría

fue un acierto.


La jornada del jueves tuvo una fuerte impronta práctica y artística.

 Por la tarde, en el Paco Urondo, se desarrolló un

taller exploratorio de investigación corporal a cargo de la Doctora e investigadora Soledad Manrique

, abierto a todo público. Allí se propuso indagar modos de habitar la crisis desde la sensopercepción y el vínculo grupal. Luego llegó el turno de la

videodanza

, bajo la curaduría de

Ladys González

, integrante del Circuito Argentino de Videodanza, y a cargo del Festival Internacional Corporalidad Expandida (FICE). Se seleccionaron:

R.E.D., de Oscar Martínez

, un trabajo que indaga el vínculo entre el sonido y la ciudad, entre el ser humano y el espacio público urbano.

DES(ARCHIVADAS), de Anahí Mariluan

, distinguida en el Festival Internacional Cámara Corporizada, y

LONA, de Malena Martínez

, homenaje en stop-motion a los 194 muertos y más de 1400 heridos que dejó la tragedia de Cromagnon, en clave amorosa. Todos los videos pusieron en diálogo el archivo, la memoria y la resistencia a través del movimiento, y fueron seguidos de un conversatorio con sus directorxs. La jornada cerró con la función de

«Todas las cosas que somos», de Alina Marinelli

, a cargo del Grupo de Experimentación en Artes del Movimiento de la UNA (GEAM) que dirige Valeria Martínez.

title: Organizaciones sociales marchan a Capital Humano contra el ajuste y a la Corte Suprema por la recuperación de la Ley de Tierras
content:
Más de 70 organizaciones sociales, territoriales y piqueteras se movilizarán este martes 6 de octubre contra las políticas de ajuste del gobierno de Javier Milei y en rechazo al fallo de la Corte Suprema que dejó vigente la derogación de la Ley de Tierras Rurales. La jornada comenzará a las 13.30 con una conferencia de prensa frente al histórico edificio del Ministerio de Capital Humano (ex Desarrollo Social), a cargo de Sandra Pettovello, donde denunciarán el ajuste, la pérdida de ingresos y el desmantelamiento de políticas destinadas a los sectores populares. Luego, movilizarán al Palacio de Justicia, donde confluirán con una amplio marco de organizaciones que repudiarán el fallo de la Corte Suprema de Justicia de la semana pasada, que eliminó los límites para la adquisición de campos argentinos por parte de extranjeros. La jornada de lucha de los movimientos sociales busca también preparar nuevas acciones para el jueves 15 de octubre, cuando la Cámara de Diputados tiene prevista una sesión especial para tratar el DNU 70/23.


Más de 70 organizaciones sociales, territoriales y piqueteras se movilizarán este martes 6 de octubre contra las políticas de ajuste del gobierno de Javier Milei y en rechazo al fallo de la Corte Suprema que dejó vigente la derogación de la Ley N° 279 de Tierras Rurales. La jornada comenzará a las 13.30 con una conferencia de prensa frente al histórico edificio del Ministerio de Capital Humano (ex Desarrollo Social), a cargo de Sandra Pettovello, y continuará con una movilización hacia el Palacio de Justicia.


Imagen: CTA Autónoma.


“Más de 70 organizaciones territoriales, sociales y piqueteras que venimos luchando en los barrios contra la destrucción y el ataque sistemático a las condiciones de vida de la enorme mayoría de las y los trabajadores, nos convocamos este martes 6 de octubre a las 13 en el histórico edificio del Ministerio de Desarrollo Social para realizar una conferencia de prensa”, señalan en la convocatoria.


Concentración de la UTEP frente al Ministerio de Capital Humano contra el hambre.


“Esta situación se da en un cuadro de crecimiento de la desocupación y la precarización laboral, caída del consumo y cierre de empresas, mientras la mayoría de las familias se encuentra endeudada a niveles insostenibles para poder llegar a fin de mes”, sostienen las organizaciones. En ese mismo sentido, un informe del Instituto de Investigación Social Económica y Política Ciudadana (ISEPCI) calculó que la eliminación del programa Volver al Trabajo, efectiva desde abril de 2026, dejó sin ese ingreso a cerca de 950.000 trabajadores informales y afectó a más de tres millones de personas al considerar a sus grupos familiares.


Otro de los ejes está puesto en la asistencia alimentaria: «venimos, además, de sufrir el corte abrupto e injustificado de la entrega de alimentos a más de 45.000 comedores populares, situación por la cual la ministra Sandra Pettovello ha sido llevada a juicio». El reclamo contra la política social se articula además con la eliminación del programa Volver al Trabajo: “Milei eliminó el programa Volver al Trabajo, dejando a casi un millón de trabajadores sociales, cocineras, recicladores y otros trabajadores de la economía popular sin el único ingreso que percibían por trabajar”. La medida efectivamente alcanzó a cientos de miles de titulares y, según un informe del ISEPCI, implicó el retiro de unos $74.100 millones mensuales del circuito de consumo popular.


Foto: David Briasco.


Luego de la conferencia de prensa, anuncian: “marcharemos al Palacio de Justicia en repudio al infame y cipayo fallo de la Corte Suprema, que sostiene la extranjerización de la tierra mediante la ratificación del inconstitucional Decreto 70/23”.


Para las organizaciones convocantes, la cuestión territorial forma parte de una ofensiva más amplia: “este decreto no solo habilita la entrega del territorio nacional al capital extranjero, sino que agrava la situación de tenencia precaria que padecen los pueblos originarios y la población trabajadora, amenazada permanentemente por desalojos en terrenos recuperados mediante enormes luchas para defender un pedazo de tierra donde vivir y producir”. El reclamo se produce, además, después de una jornada federal el pasado 6 de agosto en la que organizaciones indígenas, campesinas, ambientales, sociales y sindicales se movilizaron contra la extranjerización de la tierra y denunciaron el proyecto de Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada.

title: Worte des Subcomandante Insurgente Moisés,  beim Treffen am  3. Oktober 2026, 11:00, im CIDECI-Unitierra.
content:
Worte des Subcomandante Insurgente Moisés beim Treffen am 3. Oktober 2026, 11:00, im CIDECI-Unitierra.

.- Das hauptsächliche Ziel: das Treffen-die Umarmung mit den Sucherinnen. Es ist wichtig, dass dies gut verstanden wird und klipp und klar bleibt. Denn wir werden ein Treffen oder eine Aktivität mit den Sucherinnen nicht wegen anderer Sachen absagen.

Viele Jahre warten wir schon auf den Moment, uns mit ihnen zu treffen.

Somit sind die Versammlungen/ Treffen und Aktivitäten mit den Sucherinnen, die Priorität oder das Wichtigste in unserer Agenda oder Organisierung des Programms; Tag und Uhrzeit legen sie fest.

Jeglicher andere Vorschlag zu Aktivität oder Versammlung wird dann sein müssen, wenn es keine Versammlung oder Aktivität mit den Sucherinnen gibt.

Ebenso wird auch unsere Feier des Jahrestags des Aufstands von der Umarmung mit den Sucherinnen abhängen.

.- Das Geld für die Busse der Delegation ist bereits zusammen. Es gelang, dank der Unterstützung des widerständigen Europas, welches das spendete, was zusammengebracht wurde für das Kapitel Europa der Reise für das Leben und nicht vollkommen aufgebraucht wurde. Diese Compañeras, Compañeros und Compañeroas haben uns seit Zeiten gesagt, dieses Geld ist Geld der Zapatistas. Es muss jedoch gesagt werden, es ist Produkt ihrer Arbeit, ihrer Anstrengung und Hingabe; diese bedingungslose Solidarität muss anerkannt werden. Wir hoffen, dieses Beispiel wird nachher bei den folgenden Kapiteln der Reise für das Leben nachgebildet – so dass jedes Kapitel die Umsetzung des folgenden Kapitels unterstützt.

Unterdessen erkennen wir hier die uneigennützige Arbeit aller Personen, Gruppen, Kollektive, Organisationen und Bewegungen des Europas von unten und links an.

Auch war die Unterstützungsarbeit des Kollektivs der Sexta Mexiko: Mujeres y la Sexta [Frauen und die Sexta] fundamental, um die Busse zu bekommen.

Danke, Compañeras, Compañeros und Compañeroas. Wir werden die Sucherinnen über Eure Unterstützung informieren.

.- Deswegen wird jetzt die gesamte ökonomische Kampagne dazu da sein, um den Transport aller möglichen Gruppen, Kollektive und Organisationen nach Mexiko-Stadt zu unterstützen – zu den Daten, die ihnen am passendsten scheinen, innerhalb des Monats Dezember 2026 bis zur ersten Januar-Woche 2027.

Im Falle von Drohungen und Gefahren wird versucht, dass ihr Hin- und Rück-Transport per Flugzeug sein wird, sodass sie nicht beim Über-Land-Transport Gefahr laufen.

.- Es wird Euch schlecht ergehen, denn wir kommen nicht mit 1.111, sondern bis jetzt sind es 1.509, die kommen. Plus denen, die im letzten Moment dazukommen. Es gibt jedoch Platz für das Frayba, falls sie uns begleiten möchten.

.- Das zweite Ziel besteht darin, uns mit einigen Gruppen, Kollektiven, Organisationen und Bewegungen der Sexta zu treffen, um zusammen und gemeinsam, das zu planen, was für die Zweite Etappe der Reise für das Leben – Kapitel Mexiko möglich ist.

Dies bedeutet: Wenn wir kommen, um Euch zuzuhören, was Ihr seid und was Ihr macht, und zu Euch sprechen, was wir sind und was wir machen, das heißt: vom Gemeinschaftlichen.

.- Wenn es Zeit und Modus gibt, können wir uns zu Orten bewegen, die geographisch nahe an Mexiko-Stadt liegen.

Jedoch nur wenn es die entsprechenden Bedingungen gibt und wir eingeladen sind. Bis jetzt haben wir Einladungen in Oaxaca, Bundesstaat Oaxaca, Querétaro, Bundesstaat Querétaro, und es wird gerade geschaut, ob nach Puebla, Bundesstaat Puebla. Falls es an anderen Orten möglich ist, muss sich organisiert und ein Vorschlag gemacht werden.

Die Compañeras aus Oaxaca haben begonnen, sich zu organisieren, seit die Fahrt nach Mexiko-Stadt angekündigt wurde. Sie haben bereits [das Problem der] Unterkunft und Verpflegung für einen Teil der zapatistischen Delegation gelöst.

.- Wir sind in Equipen organisiert und können somit gut das abdecken, was im Valle de México veranstaltet wird und können so in nahegelegenen Geographien präsent sein. Dezentralisiert könnten wir zur gleichen Zeit verschiedene Orte und Themen abdecken.

author: Maríangeles Guerrero
title: Sastre sin fumigaciones: “Lo que debería venir es la agroecología para las futuras generaciones”
content:
Por Mariángeles Guerrero


Desde Santa Fe


Siete líneas en una hoja membretada de la Corte Suprema de la Nación pusieron punto final a la batalla judicial que emprendieron, en 2018, vecinas y vecinos de la localidad de Sastre y Ortíz (Santa Fe). Los jueces Horacio Rosatti y Carlos Rosenkrantz desestimaron un reclamo de la municipalidad y convalidaron la decisión que ya había tomado la Corte santafesina: se deben establecer mil metros de distancia para las fumigaciones terrestres en relación a toda esa ciudad. El ministro Ricardo Lorenzetti se excusó de intervenir. Tras conocer el fallo, Sonia González, una de las impulsoras de la causa, pide: “Que no se dude ante la salud”. Asegura que ahora irán por la reforma de la ordenanza local, de acuerdo a lo establecido en los sucesivos fallos favorables que tuvo el expediente.


Sastre y Ortiz es una ciudad de 6.000 habitantes ubicada en el sudoeste santafesino, zona núcleo del agronegocio. A lo largo de la provincia, pueblos y ciudades conviven a diario con las avionetas y los mosquitos. Santa Fe cuenta con una ley obsoleta, que data de 1995, cuando aún no se había aprobado la soja transgénica en Argentina. La soja modificada genéticamente implicó un mayor avance de la frontera agrícola y un mayor uso de herbicidas, principalmente el glifosato. Pese a urgir una actualización, la Legislatura provincial cajoneó varios proyectos de reforma impulsados desde 2010 por organizaciones socioambientales.


En 2018, Zoe Giraudo tenía dos años y un diagnóstico: linfoma linfoblástico tipo T. Estaba internada en Rosario pero, al momento de poder regresar a su casa para continuar los tratamientos de quimioterapia desde allí, los médicos advirtieron a la familia: no podía estar cerca de los venenos. En la localidad ya se venían reuniendo vecinos para intentar que el Concejo local y de que la intendenta, María del Carme Amero, tome alguna medida preventiva ante los mosquitos que fumigaban a menos de cien metros de las viviendas. A fin de ese año se presentó el amparo colectivo que ahora concluyó en la última etapa procesal posible con una nueva sentencia a favor.


La demanda se presentó contra la Municipalidad tras varios intentos de diálogo con el Ejecutivo y el Concejo para que se reformara la Ordenanza Municipal 951/2004, que fijaba el límite de fumigación a solo cien metros a partir de la finalización del área urbana. En el juicio se presentaron como terceros interesados la provincia y una decena de productores. Si bien en 2020 el juez Francisco Hail, de Rafaela, dio la razón a los vecinos, la municipalidad apeló. Y siguió apelando hasta llegar a la Corte Nacional.


Desde la Capital Federal se puso fin al litigio alegando que el último recurso de queja presentado por la Municipalidad de Sastre carece de “fundamentación autónoma”. Cuando refiere a esta falencia, el máximo tribunal indica que una queja determinada no cuenta con un relato prolijo de los hechos y una crítica ordenada al fallo que se busca impugnar. En este caso, el de la Corte de Santa Fe.


El fruto de la lucha colectiva


En el contexto de una provincia donde se plantea la tensión entre salud y modelo productivo y se priorizan los intereses de los grupos concentrados que están detrás del glifosato, de los transgénicos y del monocultivo de commodities, vecinas y vecinos iniciaron un camino que no abandonaron. Y lograron un fallo que ahora implica un precedente relevante para las localidades de Santa Fe y para otros pueblos fumigados del país. Hoy Zoe Giraudo tiene 10 años y su mamá siente que, con esta resolución, deja de cargar una mochila que llevó por años. “Estamos orgullosos como grupo y yo como mamá, porque siento que hice un montón por mi hija”, dice González.


—¿Cómo comenzó la movilización en Sastre?

—La lucha de los vecinos empezó hace muchísimo tiempo, porque había muy pocos vecinos que estaban tratando de alejar estos venenos que ya se sabía que hacían mal. En 2018, una vecina que vive a una cuadra vio un mosquito que estaba fumigando a 70 metros de su casa. Y coincidió con el tiempo en que yo tenía a Zoe, mi nena, internada en Rosario. Esa vecina empezó a buscar soluciones: yendo a la municipalidad, a juntar firmas, a levantar publicaciones en las redes. Zoe se estaba atendiendo con los mejores médicos, pero al final no tenía resguardo con respecto a los venenos. Ellos se juntaron como vecinos, juntaron firmas, fueron al Concejo Municipal y nada. No hubo soluciones. Eso pasó en marzo. Los vecinos …

author: La Zarzamora
title: Comunicado público ppm Caso Grollmus
content:
Frente a las exuberantes condenas y tras un viciado proceso declaramos:

Mari mari pu machi, pu lonko, pu werken, kom pu che. El día de hoy nos dirigimos a la sociedad en general, a todos y todas quienes nos han brindado su apoyo y respaldo en este proceso denominado “Caso Grollmus”.

Actualmente a nosotros como comuneros mapuche se nos ha condenado a penas que marcarán un precedente como obscenamente políticas, se nos condena por decisión política, por ser mapuche que vivimos y recuperamos nuestro territorio.

Tras el gigantesco despliegue comunicacional, y tras el espectáculo montado por el Ministerio Público y la PDI, la familia Grollmus demanda al estado en busca de indemnizaciones y reparaciones.

La fiscalía con el aval del tribunal logró su objetivo: condenar a una pena que ponderada resulta en 1055 años de prisión contra nosotros. La prensa vociferó la sentencia y el poder político respaldo, claridad absoluta.

Les decimos, su ocupación contra nuestro pueblo y su territorio apenas tiene 143 años. Nuestro pueblo resistió al imperio español casi 300 años.

Hoy Chile soberbio y republicano nos condena a más de 1000 años. Por el único motivo de luchar por nuestra soberanía, por nuestro buen vivir y dignidad. Lo anterior tendrá la más necesaria respuesta: continuar con el legado de nuestro pueblo, luchar por nuestra dignidad y libertad.

Los Grupos de Tarea y la BIPE de la PDI recorren los penales de forma morbosa buscando testigos a quienes poner corbata de protegido y sin rostro. Sólo por cuatro relatos de estos “testigos” se dictó sentencia y veredicto. Nuestro territorio se militariza y vuelven a saquear nuestros recursos naturales, vuelven las concesiones mineras, CMPC y Mininco cual mecenas entregan dinero y donaciones a Postas y Escuelas.

Queremos manifestar nuestro agradecimiento por todo el respaldo de nuestros hermanos y hermanas en otros territorios y ciudades. No renunciaremos jamás a la lucha por un debido y objetivo proceso.

Nos movilizaremos por nuestra libertad y juicio justo.

PRESENTACION


¿Qué relación existe entre la Comuna como forma política de la emancipación social y la clase, entendida ésta no como categoría positivizada y sociológica, sino en su carácter dual y contradictorio? ¿Es la Comuna una manera de entender la clase y la lucha de clases en clave no identitaria, no positivizada? ¿La oposición entre Comuna y clase es algo derivado de una concepción anti-dialéctica de la lucha de clases? En ese campo ¿a qué dialéctica nos referimos? ¿A la dialéctica hegeliana orientada a la síntesis estatal como forma política de la identidad? ¿A la dialéctica negativa que la cuestiona? ¿La lucha de clases, entendida en clave dialéctica no-identitaria, permite entender la Comuna como proceso contradictorio de disolución de la clase? ¿Implica esto un desafío a nuestro concepto de proletariado y a la idea de revolución calcada en el canon leninista?

author: Aline Melo
title: Plataformas mantêm anúncios e recomendações políticas irregulares no dia da votação
content:
Investigamos o que importa para os brasileiros além do que passa na campanha eleitoral. Leia mais reportagens como essa clicando

aqui

.


Em meio às acusações sobre a interferência das Big Techs na integridade eleitoral brasileira,

plataformas digitais continuaram veiculando anúncios políticos irregulares e recomendando conteúdos de candidatos durante o período de resguardo do primeiro turno das

eleições de 2026.


O período de resguardo para a circulação paga ou impulsionada de propaganda eleitoral na internet compreende as 48 horas anteriores e as 24 horas posteriores à votação, conforme previsto no

art. 29, § 11, da Resolução TSE nº 23.610/2019.

 A norma também define, nos artigos 28 e 29, as formas de propaganda eleitoral na internet e as regras para o impulsionamento de conteúdo. 


O monitoramento identificou 568 anúncios irregulares na Meta, 18 anúncios ativos no Kwai e um no Google Ads, além de ao menos seis campanhas fraudulentas que imitavam o Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE).

 O levantamento também encontrou recomendações orgânicas de conteúdos publicados por contas oficiais de candidatos no TikTok e no YouTube durante o dia da votação. Os dados são do Observatório das Big Techs, realizado pelo NetLab UFRJ, laboratório de pesquisa sobre internet e redes sociais vinculado à Escola de Comunicação da Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ). 


O monitoramento foi dividido em duas frentes: o Observatório da Publicidade Política, voltado aos anúncios pagos, e o Observatório da Recomendação Algorítmica, que analisou os conteúdos sugeridos organicamente por TikTok, YouTube e Instagram.


Anúncios de TSE falso dizem que eleitor poderia votar pela internet


Na frente de publicidade política, foram identificados os 568 anúncios veiculados irregularmente na Meta relacionados a 15 candidatos, além de 18 anúncios ativos no Kwai e um anúncio ativo no Google Ads durante o período de resguardo. No Kwai, os pesquisadores também encontraram 45 anúncios de 10 páginas de candidaturas cuja data-limite de circulação havia sido alterada para permitir que continuassem ativos no dia da votação.


Entre os casos identificados na Meta estão ao menos seis campanhas fraudulentas que se passavam pelo Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) ou pela Justiça Eleitoral.

 Segundo o NetLab, os anúncios eram veiculados tanto por perfis que imitavam contas oficiais, utilizando a marca da Corte e nomes como “TSE Informa”, quanto por contas aparentemente pertencentes a usuários comuns.


As campanhas promoviam a falsa ideia de que o TSE teria criado uma modalidade oficial de “voto digital”, que permitiria ao eleitor votar remotamente, de casa ou pelo celular.

 Para dar credibilidade à fraude, os anúncios exploravam situações que poderiam dificultar o comparecimento presencial às urnas, como fortes chuvas, problemas de saúde e dificuldades de locomoção.


Ao clicar nas peças, o usuário era direcionado para sites externos que solicitavam o CPF para supostamente iniciar a votação. Uma das mensagens identificadas no monitoramento dizia: “Você não precisa de fila para votar. O TSE criou o voto digital para que você participe desta eleição pelo celular, com total segurança e praticidade”. O NetLab aponta que esse tipo de conteúdo poderia induzir eleitores a acreditar que não precisariam comparecer presencialmente às suas seções eleitorais, além de criar riscos relacionados à coleta de dados pessoais.


O monitoramento também identificou anúncios da loja Vinho B II Mito, que promoviam produtos como vinhos, facas e bonés utilizando imagens de figuras políticas e manifestações explícitas de apoio a candidaturas.


O boletim aponta problemas de transparência nas próprias ferramentas utilizadas para fiscalizar a publicidade. Na Meta, os pesquisadores encontraram inconsistências entre os anúncios classificados como “inativos” e aqueles que permaneciam disponíveis como ativos na biblioteca da plataforma. No Kwai, foram identificados rótulos como “em pausa”, sem documentação clara sobre o significado desses status, além de divergências entre os dados exibidos na plataforma e os dados que poderiam ser exportados para análise.


TikTok “para você” recomenda conteúdos políticos no dia de votação


Na segunda frente, o Observatório da Recomendação Algorítmica analisou como as plataformas recomendaram conteúdos políticos e de candidatos no dia da votação. Segundo o NetLab, a Resolução TSE nº 23.732/2024 estabelece regras sobre sistemas de recomendação …

content:
Artist Cesim Başboğa was prosecuted over songs he performed at the Culture and Arts Festival held in Tatvan (Tetwan), Bitlis (Bedlîs), in 2025.


The songs Serhildan Jiyan e, Lê Amedê and Zana û Andok, which Başboğa performed at the festival, were cited as evidence in the case brought against him on allegations of “making propaganda for an organization.”


At the second hearing of the case, held today at the Bitlis 2nd High Criminal Court, the court sentenced Başboğa to 10 months in prison.


Başboğa said in his defence that, at a time when peace is being discussed, imposing sentences on artists who perform music in their mother tongue harms the process.

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Leyte farmer files harassment complaint vs military
content:
By Veronika Barbosa TACLOBAN CITY – A farmer filed a complaint on September 22 with the Commission on Human Rights Regional Office 8 against the Philippine Army’s 93rd Infantry Battalion (IB) due to intimidation against her and her family.

Accompanied by the National Union of People’s Lawyers Eastern Visayas and Katungod Sinirangan Bisayas, Brenda Lagado said that the first incident happened on July 28 in their house in Jaro, Leyte. “We were visited by elements of the Armed Forces of the Philippines. At first, they were just checking in on us but they eventually pressured us to confess that we have connections with the New People’s Army even if we have none.”

In the same month, Lagado said that her 16-year-old cousin was also interrogated by soldiers and alleged military assets.

“He [my cousin] was tending to farm animal when he was approached by seven soldiers and seven other individuals. At first, he was told to wait for a certain Basas who was supposed to talk to him but the latter did not arrive. He was instead confronted by a certain Simon who later grabbed him by the collar, hit him with a piece of chopped wood, and threatened that he will be hanged or electrocuted if he does not cooperate with them.”

Lagado said that his cousin was coerced by at least 14 men to divulge information about certain individuals that the victim does not know about.

She said that in August, a certain Sgt. Andres visited their house and compelled her to go to the barangay hall to purportedly “clear her name” which she refused to do. “We already went to the barangay before but the harassment still continued.”

In the same month, Lagado said that a child development worker of the Daycare Center where her child 3-year-old child was enrolled in, also experienced interrogation. “The teacher told us that a certain Cris Edison Rivera, who we later found out was from the 93rd IB, asked for the name and even live birth of my child. He also interrogated the teacher and asked information about our family.”

On September 11, Lagado received a letter from an unknown sender via express delivery. The letter included an unknown number and contained statements maligning Brenda and her family. “The letter pressured me to cooperate and call the number written on the letter within 24 hours or else they would let my entire family and my husband know that I have a relationship with an NPA rebel.”

“I am scared for my family and worried about my children’s safety. I am scared because the military have pictures of my family and even my children,” Lagado said. In a statement, Katungod SB condemned the 93rd IB’s series of harassment targeted against the Lagado family and their intimidation tactics involving innocent children.

“Children are not the tools of war…they should never be used, threatened, or assaulted to serve the military’s agenda. The 93rd IB, the entire AFP, and the NTF-ELCAC should all be held accountable for using a child and physically assaulting a minor to force the family to surrender or report to the 93rd IB.” Katungod SB called on the Commission on Human Rights to swiftly investigate and to protect the Lagado family against further intimidation and harassment. (DAA)

title: Dubious China ties of Sara, Manases
content:
The Chinese Embassy may protest to high heavens that the P150-million it “donated” to a foundation headed by Sara Zimmerman Duterte Carpio was meant to “help” build classrooms in Davao City, but the Chinese corporations in Hong Kong and Southern China will be hard put proving that they were just buying banana chips from Cale 88, which appears to a small enterprise with a work force that is not even a dozen but scored a huge windfall of P1.25-billion from 2022 to 2025. This cannot be consistent with a business that paid an annual income tax that is a tad higher than P10,000. Moreover, Manases Carpio mysteriously disappeared as a stockholder with 47% equity when Sara was investigated and impeached. It turned out that another company also owned by the Dutertes “bought” Carpio’s interest.


Surely, Cale 88 Foods could not have shipped boatloads of banana chips to China with the few workers that it had. Most likely, and this is assuming that Cale 88 Foods were a legitimate food manufacturer, the venture could have bought huge volumes of banana chips from other companies in Tagum, Panabo (where prison labor can be exploited to the hilt) and other areas still free from the ravages of *fusarium wilt, particularly Tropical Race 4, and sent them to China. Stranger still, Philippine bananas had to go through the eye of a needle to enter the China market. China now produces bananas after claiming for years that Philippine bananas harbor pests.


Even then, the documents showed that the total sales of Cale 88 were only P208-million but inward remittances were P319.33-million. Curiously, the revenues were not reflected in the Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN) of Sara and her husband from 2019 to 2025. They had no cash on hand and cash in banks despite the fact that their transactions from 2009 to 2013 amounted to P2.7 billion, or between 70% and 80% of the total P3.3 billion flagged for that period. Sara became a public official only on 2007 and got married to Carpio in the same year. From where did she accumulate such enormous wealth?


On this basis alone, one could surmise that the Duterte political warlord family amassed their huge stash since the 1980s, when Rodrigo Duterte entered politics and emerged as the warlord of Davao City. But why are state-owned companies buying banana chips from Carpio rather than the thousands of family enterprises engaged in the same business? This question was raised at the Senate and the logical justification was that the Chinese were also into some hanky-panky, “buying” access and “cooperation” with Sara and Carpio. Before Sara broke with her Team Unity partners in 2023, the Chinese Embassy was cocksure that she was a shoo-in for the presidency in 2028. Yet, political conditions in the Philippines defy categorization by Confucius or Sun Tzu, and the more they believed in the theory of Sara’s invincibility, the more the Chinese would invest in the Duterte dynasty.


Nevertheless, the Chinese, who invented the word patience, could not purchase wisdom, and they failed to understand the calculus of chaos that underpins botched ambitions and tactical alliances among members of the political class. The linear thinking exhibited by the Chinese mission and the coterie of pro-China propagandists is their own folly. No one would wish to be drawn, quartered and their remains stuck in some pikes to champion the Duterte dynasty’s interest. Neither would anyone suffer lingzhi to protect Sara, Manases, Pulong, Baste, Kitty and, of course, the patriarch now awaiting trial before the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague.


Witnesses testified on Oct. 6, 2026 that Sara and her beloved husband have 30 active accounts in eight banks, surely an indication that they trust the banking system, and Sara also has joint accounts with her father Rodrigo, with P193.7-million flitting from one account to another as the crow flies in 2014. There were seven inter-account transfers on March 28, 2014, involved the Duterte father and daughter. The transfers, each bearing a separate reference number, totaled P193.7 million. The largest was P55.13 million, followed by P41.72 million, four P20-million transfers and P16.85 million. Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) executive director Atty. Ronel Buenaventura said these were movements of funds from one account to another within the same bank and were treated separately because they had different reference numbers.
