author: Ishita Chakrabarty
title: Hindus for Human Rights: ‘Racism is not just about violence, it manifests through misinformation’
content:
To all those who have come from far off-lands and continents; who have made it here despite the monumental barriers that passport privilege poses for some over others — the intense questioning as to motivation; the demand for return tickets; the visa costs that keep escalating year on year; the bank statements and medical reports to prove you will not become a burden onto the system, I am one among you.

To those who have lived here for generations and are yet still told to “Go back where you came from”.

To those who hold a sacred relationship to this land — whose belonging to this land can never be severed by the operation of an unjust, extractive and foreign imposed law.

And to all those who join us here in solidarity, who believe in the idea of an inclusive, egalitarian and multicultural Australia.

I come from Bengal in India. I am representing Hindus for Human Rights, a voice for progressive Hindus and Indians working for inter-faith and inter-community respect and understanding and advocating against all kinds of discrimination and bigotry.

Coming from India, I know all too well what hate, bigotry and the belief of the superiority of some over the other looks like, and how the destruction of the very fabric of society is tantamount to the destruction of the human within us.

It is because of the love I hold towards my home country and the appreciation for being here that I believe we must join hands in the fight against racism and bigotry, whether it comes from the far right politics of One Nation, or from the Hindutva ideology that considers Dalits, Muslims, Christians and other minorities inferior and less than human.

As I speak, Muslims are being lynched, evicted, legally stripped of their citizenship through complicit state institutions. Christians are being hounded, their prayer services are being stopped mid-worship on allegations of forced conversions. Dalits and other caste minorities remain trapped in a system where the so-called upper castes get offended by someone for sporting a moustache, or a Dalit man “daring” to attend their own wedding on horseback.

As a person bearing a majoritarian identity, I feel even more compelled to not only speak of racism emanating from a certain and distant political entity, but also the hatred, transpiring within our own South Asian community, including in Australia.

Identities, beliefs and practices travel alongside communities and are often seen through acts such as questioning one’s food preferences, tasking that one Indian student whose identity is given away by their surname to undertake the menial tasks in the house, through casual bullying. They perpetrate through closed social groups and in marriage alliances.

Hindus for Human Rights along with allies have worked hard and successfully to have caste discrimination included as a form of racism in city councils and universities.

When we speak of racism and bigotry it is also important to speak about these internal exclusions that we have created. For the same hatred that I mentioned earlier is then taken and twisted to justify that the far right is not against all immigrants — only the “bad ones” who refuse to “assimilate”, for example, the hijab- or turban-wearing student of Indian origin.

It is used to legitimise the exclusion of our fellow community members, as when One Nation leader Pauline Hanson keeps speaking of how Indians are the “good, hardworking migrants”.

It is seen when platforms show her attending Diwali festivals and being warmly received by diasporic Indians, represented through associations like the Hindu Council of Australia, or when she visits that one Indian migrant-run shop in Townsville, posing with the owner while eating fish and chips.

When I speak of racism, I speak of the overt acts: The people who called 22-year-old Harmanpreet Singh “a dog”, and physically assaulted him, leaving him with a broken nose in February in Corio. Or when they called 26-year-old Nayonika a “curry muncher”, “smelly Indian”, and a “Mrs. 7/11 driver” in Sydney’s CBD.

But racism also manifests through misinformation such as caricatures portraying Indians, and other immigrants, as being responsible for the housing crisis.

It co-exists in the digital world where desk warriors feel confident to call Greens Senator Mehreen Faruqi “a filthy Australian hating racist pig”.

It does not stop at that. Racism and bigotry also acts through constant daily acts of micro-aggression; through people staring you …

author: Frenny Jowi
title: Congo in Kenya: Why Xenophobia is a Racist Ideal
content:
Thirty-three-year-old Emmanuel is a freelance hairdresser in Nairobi. He is a refugee from the Democratic Republic of Congo and has lived in Kenya for six years.


The young man is chic, dressed in designer brands, with a gentle demeanour that reflects his customer-care style in the city’s beauty industry. His calm, collected appearance belies a history of strife, struggle, and an ongoing effort to recover from the decades of armed conflict he witnessed as a child in North Kivu.


‘I will never forget the night when rebels attacked our village in North Kivu. I must have been seven years old at that time. Some people were killed, and there was fire burning everywhere around us.’


Emmanuel narrated his story as he swung around in his styling chair in front of a large mirror that is popularly called a ‘station’ in Nairobi’s hairdressing and beauty salons.


I had visited Emmanuel at the salon where he works. Renting business premises in Nairobi is a significant cost for many young business owners, whether citizen or foreigner. In the beauty industry, most professionals can only afford to rent a mirror and a styling chair as a workstation – hence the name ‘station’.


While occasionally glancing at his WhatsApp notifications for customer bookings, Emmanuel continued to share his story with me.


‘The attack happened many years ago. I still remember how my mother stopped to pack her pot of fish stew and cassava leaves and rice. My father asked her to hurry up, leave the food, and run for safety, but she insisted she would not leave her delicious food. As we all escaped in the dim light of the moon, I recall our neighbours’ comments about my mother’s weird sense of what to salvage. She insisted the food would also save us and she would not leave it behind despite the gunfire. Now I find that funny.’


Emmanuel laughed, trying to find humour in a devastating story.


I knew that talking about traumatic childhood experiences from war would be difficult, so I did not press Emmanuel further about the night armed fighters attacked their village, killing many people and setting houses on fire.


The events Emmanuel witnessed as a child in 2000 were part of the Second Congo War, dubbed Africa’s World War. According to

Amnesty International

, the DRC’s current conflict has been ongoing since the 1990s, particularly in the eastern part of the country, which borders South Sudan, Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, and Tanzania.


This armed conflict escalated in August 1998 when President Laurent Kabila fell out with the Ugandan and Rwandan allies who had helped him seize power.


Emmanuel narrated how the fighting between the Lendu-Ngiti and the opposing Hema began as communal land disputes involving farmers and pastoralists. Locals believe politicians and those with mining interests took advantage of these seemingly solvable disputes to fuel the ongoing war. He added that their radio broadcasts often mentioned various fighting groups such as the UPDF (Uganda People’s Defence Forces) and the UPC (United Congolese Patriots).


‘In the news, when we heard that Bosco Ntaganda was in court and wanted to defend himself in Kinyarwanda, we were all shocked, because locally, we knew him as one of us. We never thought he was from Rwanda. He lived here for so long, spoke our language, looked like one of us, and was always involved in Congolese affairs,’ Emmanuel said.


Decades of conflict have been fuelled by ethnic tensions, political rivalries, corruption, and fighting for control of valuable natural resources.


Over time, the war drew in nine African nations, making it one of the largest wars in African history. The 2017 Kivu Security Tracker Report by Jason Stearns and Christoph Vogel listed 132 armed fighter groups operating in North and South Kivu alone.


Today, Emmanuel is one of the over 100 million citizens of the DRC affected by incessant wars. The DRC is the fourth most populous country in Africa and the 14th in the world. Despite decades of war and pandemics such as Ebola, its population has continued to grow steadily. 


In 2025,

Human Rights Watch

 reported that the Congolese military and a coalition of armed fighters have continued to attack civilians. The report adds that throughout 2024, the

Rwandan

 army and the M23 armed group indiscriminately shelled displacement camps and other densely populated areas near Goma in eastern Congo.


Emmanuel arrived in Kenya in 2019, just before the COVID-19 pandemic. Earlier, in 2017 …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Tormenta Negra 2: “no son políticas de prevención del delito, es racismo”
content:
El gobierno de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires realizó el jueves 24 un nuevo operativo “Tormenta Negra” en 15 barrios populares con violencia policial, detenciones arbitrarias y el retiro de pertenencias y herramientas de trabajo. Jorge Macri “consolida una política que identifica pobreza con inseguridad” e insiste en violentar la vida en los barrios populares y atemorizar a quienes viven en ellos, denunciaron desde el Centro de Estudios Legales y Sociales (CELS). “No existen operativos de este tipo en los otros barrios de la Ciudad” como Palermo, Caballito o Núñez, señalaron.


Compartimos el comunicado del CELS:


Tormenta Negra 2: el gobierno de CABA entiende a los barrios populares como zonas de ocupación


El gobierno de Jorge Macri volvió a desplegar más de 1500 policías y agentes de control en 15 villas y barrios populares de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires. Registramos episodios de violencia policial, detenciones arbitrarias y el retiro de pertenencias y herramientas de trabajo. La CABA consolida una política que identifica pobreza con inseguridad, no con ausencia de derechos.


El jueves 24 de septiembre, el gobierno de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires realizó un nuevo operativo Tormenta Negra en 15 villas y barrios populares. Más de 1500 policías y agentes de control de Espacio Público ingresaron de manera simultánea a los barrios para realizar controles de personas y vehículos, inspeccionar comercios y retirar del espacio público objetos de las personas que viven allí. Es la segunda vez que el gobierno porteño organiza un despliegue de estas características, después del de mayo de este año. Jorge Macri insiste en violentar la vida en los barrios populares y atemorizar a quienes viven en ellos.


Se trata de un modo de entender la ciudad y el derecho a la ciudad con un abordaje racializante y con límites de clase. Es una política que decide qué cuerpos van a ser controlados por la policía, qué familias van a ser desalojadas sin garantías, qué personas deberán demostrar una y otra vez que tienen derecho a quedarse y cuáles tienen que mostrar su documentación en las estaciones de trenes y subtes. La política porteña naturaliza que la principal y primera intervención del Estado en los barrios populares va a ser la policial. Uno de los jóvenes detenidos estaba en situación de calle dentro de la Villa 21. El gobierno llegó con patrulleros, efectivos armados y agentes de control, en lugar de organizar una intervención a partir de las necesidades de quienes viven allí o para garantizar los derechos sobre los que el mismo Estado está en deuda. No hubo presencia de áreas de desarrollo social, sino el despliegue de dispositivos de estigmatización de quienes viven allí, para convertirlos en sujetos de sospecha. El gobierno de la Ciudad abandonó las políticas de integración sociourbana. Ahora se enfoca en una política que niega la ciudadanía de las personas que viven en estos barrios. No existen operativos de este tipo en los otros barrios de la Ciudad, que los invadan a la pesca de ver qué delitos se identifican, que sin duda los hay en Palermo, Caballito o Núñez.


La vara en la Ciudad de Buenos Aires está tan baja que tenemos que reiterar lo obvio: en los barrios populares viven personas que trabajan, estudian, crían a sus hijos que van a la escuela y sostienen redes comunitarias. Tienen derecho a tener políticas que integren las villas con la ciudad en términos de derechos garantizados: a la vivienda, a la salud, a la educación, al trabajo y no estar sujeto a control poblacional permanente. La guerra contra los pobres habla de la pobreza en políticas públicas de la gestión actual de la ciudad. Y del solapamiento de un abordaje que se anuncia como control de actividades delictivas con la persecución de las estrategias de supervivencia. De este modo, la ciudad se fragmenta cada vez más. Los operativos espasmódicos y violentos no llevan orden a estos barrios, sino incertidumbre, abusos y show para las redes sociales. Cuando terminan los operativos y la policía se retira de estos barrios, no permanecen otras políticas públicas.


Durante el operativo del jueves registramos situaciones de violencia policial, uso de gases lacrimógenos y disparos de balas de goma. En la Villa 21-24, los registros audiovisuales que hicieron los mismos vecinos muestran intervenciones contra personas en situación de calle que intentaban resguardar sus colchones y pertenencias. También denunciaron que la policía les sacó herramientas de trabajo. El Ministerio …

author: Wildcat #116
title: 1976 – 1991: Das Albartus-Papier der Revolutionären Zellen
content:
Die Jahre 1976 und 1991 markieren zwei deutliche Abstürze in der Geschichte der radikalen Linken in der BRD. Bezeichnenderweise kam Ende 1991 das Albartus-Papier der Revolutionären Zellen auf 1976 zu sprechen: die Flugzeugentführung von Entebbe. Anlässlich des 50. Jahrestags haben wir in der aktuellen Wildcat einen langen Artikel, der diese Verbindungen aufzudröseln versucht: »Entebbe und die Folgen«. Hier eine Kürzestfassung plus update:


Im Juni und Juli 1976 herrschte in Europa eine Hitzewelle. Die Temperaturen in Deutschland stiegen wochenlang regelmäßig über 30 Grad auf Spitzenwerte bis 36 und 37 Grad.


Politisch endete vor 50 Jahren das »rote Jahrzehnt«: 24. März 1976 Militärputsch in Argentinien. Am 9. Mai 1976 starb Ulrike Meinhof. Anfang Juni brach auf dem »Pfingstkongress« ein breiter Teil der radikalen Linken mit der Militanz und machte sich auf in die Institutionen. Am 10. Juli begann die Chemiekatastrophe in Seveso. Im August das Massaker von Tel al-Zaatar. Am 6. Oktober der Militärputsch in Thailand.


Auch kulturell war 1976 schlimm: ABBA »Dancing Queen«, Jürgen Drews »Ein Bett im Kornfeld«, Boney M. »Daddy Cool«. Kurz danach kamen dann die BeeGees »Stayin’ Alive« – der Sound zum Deutschen Herbst!


Für die deutschen Maoisten der diversen K-Gruppen lag 1976 zwischen dem Besuch von Franz Josef Strauß bei Mao (Januar 1975) einerseits, dem Krieg Vietnams gegen Kambodscha und den »Reformen« von Deng Xiao Ping (beides im Dezember 1978) andererseits. Die meisten fielen vom Glauben ab, viele von ihnen gründeten die Grüne Partei, andere später die Antideutschen. Diese eroberten nach 1991 die Hegemonie in der radikalen Linken.


Die Flugzeugentführung nach Entebbe…


Seit Anfang 1976 eskalierte der libanesische Bürgerkrieg. Nach monatelanger Belagerung stürmten Falangisten am 12. August das Lager von Tel al-Zaatar und töteten Tausende palästinensische Flüchtlinge.


Im Zusammenhang damit entführte ein deutsch-palästinensisches Kommando aus RZ und PFLP-EO am 27. Juni 1976 ein Flugzeug nach Entebbe und forderte die Freilassung von politischen Gefangenen. In der Nacht zum 4. Juli befreiten israelische Spezialkräfte die meisten der Geiseln. Das wird von gewissen Kreisen bis heute als das beste Kommandounternehmen aller Zeiten bejubelt (etwa: »Mit der Geiselbefreiung von Entebbe zeigte Israel vor 50 Jahren, wie man den Terror bekämpft« Nius 2. Juli 2026). Benjamin Netanjahu, dessen älterer Bruder bei der Befreiungsaktion starb, hat seine gesamte politische Karriere auf »Entebbe« und den »Kampf gegen den Terrorismus« aufgebaut.


»Die Aktion von Entebbe wurde rasch zu einem Vorwand für verschiedene Akteure, die bislang mit dem Milieu der radikalen Linken verbunden waren, sich von Internationalismus und Antiimperialismus ganz zu lösen.« (Gerhard Hanloser: »Desaster mit Nachspiel«)


Wegweisend war der Anti-Repressionskongress des Sozialistischen Büros Anfang Juni (»Pfingstkongress«). Am Abschlusstag hatte der spätere Außenminister Joschka Fischer vor 20.000 Besuchern in der berühmten Römerberg-Rede mit seiner militanten Vergangenheit gebrochen. Später hat er – die Dinge chronologisch auf den Kopf stellend – auf seinem Weg ins Außenministerium immer mal wieder betont, »Entebbe« sei das Ereignis gewesen, das ihn vom Saulus zum Paulus gemacht habe. Dabei lieferte es nur nachträglich den Vorwand.


»Entebbe« ist bis heute wirkmächtig. Das sah man an den Dutzenden von Artikeln und mehreren Büchern, die zum 50. Jahrestag erschienen. Das sah man aber auch daran, dass im März 2023 Mitglieder der Entebbe-Spezialeinheit eine der schärfsten Kritiken an Benjamin Netanjahu in einem offenen Brief formulierten. Netanjahu opfere den Staat Israel und das israelische Volk für seine eigenen Interessen, diffamiere Demonstranten gegen die Justizreform als Anarchisten und alle, die ihn nicht unterstützen, als Terroristen; er hetze Israelis gegeneinander auf.


… und die beginnende Institutionalisierung der radikalen Linken


1976 hätte auch anders ausgehen können. Im Juli hatten Chemiearbeiter in Seveso gestreikt, um die Katastrophe überhaupt öffentlich zu machen – aber sie hatten nicht mehr die Macht wie Jahre zuvor, die Wirtschaftspolitik des Landes neu zu orientieren. Die massenhaften Schüler- und Studentenproteste in Soweto seit Juni waren größtenteils selbst organisiert und schienen politisch endlich eine Alternative zum ANC zu eröffnen. Aber die Bullen schlugen die Bewegung brutal nieder; sie töteten mehr als 500 der …

title: Συγκεντρώσεις αλληλεγγύης, Τετάρτη 7/10
content:
>Κινητοποίηση αλληλεγγύης στον πολιτικό πρόσφυγα Soner Inanç, 9:00 στο υπουργείο Μετανάστευσης και Ασύλου


>Συγκέντρωση για την υπεράσπιση των Αγράφων, 10:00 στο ΣτΕ


>Δίκη τριών εκπαιδευτικών της ΕΛΜΕ και του προέδρου του Ε.Κ. Πειραιά, 10:00 στα δικαστήρια Πειραιά


>Συγκέντρωση αλληλεγγύης στα προφυλακισμένα της υπόθεσης 1/7 στη Θεσσαλονίκη, 9:00 στα δικαστήρια


>Κινητοποίηση αλληλεγγύης στον πολιτικό πρόσφυγα Soner Inanç


ΚΑΛΕΣΜΑ ΣΕ ΚΙΝΗΤΟΠΟΙΗΣΗ/CALL TO DEMO [GR/ENG]


Κινητοποίηση στο Υπουργείο Μετανάστευσης και Ασύλου την Τετάρτη 07/10 09:00 (Λεωφόρος Θηβών 196-198)


Tην Τετάρτη 7 Οκτώβρη ο Soner Inanç πολιτικός αγωνιστής για τα εργατικά δικαιώματα και τις δημοκρατικές ελευθερίες στην Τουρκία κλείνει 42 ημέρες απεργίας σε απεργίας πείνας ενώ είνα διαδοχικά από τα τέλη Ιούλη σε κράτηση στο ΑΤ Λαυρίου, έπειτα στη Θεσσαλονίκη και από τις 9 Σεπτέμβρη στο ΠΡΟΚΕΚΑ Παρανεστίου Δράμας. Τα αιτήματα της απεργίας πείνας είναι η απελευθέρωση του και η απόδοση καθεστώτος ασύλου.


Σε ενδεχόμενη απόρριψη του αιτήματος ασύλου του ο Soner Inanç κινδυνεύει με άμεση απέλαση και φυλάκιση στην Τουρκία. Ο ίδιος αναγκάστηκε να εγκαταλείψει την Τουρκία καθώς έχει στοχοποιηθεί για την πολιτική δράση του από το τουρκικό κράτος και ήδη έχει φυλακιστεί στο παρελθόν για τη συμμετοχή του στο κίνημα του Gezi Park.


Στις 5 Οκτωβρίου εκδόθηκε η απόφαση του Διοικητικού Πρωτοδικείου Καβάλας επί των αντιρρήσεων κατά της κράτησης του. Η απόφαση απορρίπτει τις αντιρρήσεις του Soner, βασιζόμενη σε μία σειρά από ψευδείς παραδοχές και νομικές υπερβάσεις μετά από πρωτοφανή, πολιτικού χαρακτήρα, παρέμβαση του ΠΡΟΚΕΚΑ Δράμας μέσα από τον ψευδή ισχυρισμό πως ο Soner Inanç ξεκίνησε απεργίας στις 18/09 (!!). Για όλους εμάς, αυτή παρέμβαση καταδεικνύει την πολιτική στοχοποίηση του όπως και όλων των πολιτικών προσφύγων από την Τουρκία μέσα από τις όχι-και-τόσο-κρυφές συμφωνίες μεταξύ Ελλάδας και Τουρκίας. Ταυτόχρονα, η “λογική” των απορριπτικών ως τώρα αποφάσεων της υπηρεσίας ασύλου καταδεικνύει τις συνέπειες των μεγάλων αλλαγών που έχουν επέλθει στο καθεστώς ασύλου τα τελευταία έτη καθώς έχουμε να κάνουμε με την καταστρατήγηση της έννοιας του πολιτικού ασύλου. Γι’αυτό και ο αγώνας του Soner είναι και αγώνας για το πολιτικό άσυλο γενικότερα και χρειάζεται τη στήριξη όλων μας.


Καταγγέλουμε το ΠΡΟΚΕΚΑ Δράμας, τη δίοικηση και το ιατρικό προσωπικό του για την σκοπίμως ελλειπέστατη πρόσβασή του σε υπηρεσίες υγείας και την υποβολή του Soner σε εξευτελιστική μεταχείριση, προσπαθώντας να τον «πείσουν» (δηλαδή, να τον πιέσουν) να σταματήσει την απεργία ή ελέγχοντας αν «όντως δεν τρώει». Μετά από πολλές εβδομάδες στέρησης βιταμινών, αναγκαίων για την μη ύπαρξη μόνιμων επιπτώσεων, το αίτημα αυτό άρχισε να καλύπτεται όπως όφειλε εξαρχής μετά από συνεχή πολιτική κινητοποίηση και δημοσιογραφική κάλυψη για τον κίνδυνο τον οποίο διατρέχει αν δεν του χορηγηθούν. Το ΠΡΟΚΕΚΑ Παρανεστίου οφείλειως απεργός πείνας ο Soner Inanç να παρακολουθείται από ανεξάρτητη ιατρική επιτροπή για να διασφαλιστεί η απρόσκοπτη άσκηση της ως πολιτική δράση με συγκεκριμένα αιτήματα: τη συνέχιση της διαδικασίας απόδοση ασύλου, την μη απέλαση του στην Τουρκία και την απελευθέρωσή του. Ο Soner δηλώνει αποφασισμένος να συνεχίσει στον αγώνα του, αφού κρατείται άδικα, περιμένοντας νέα απόφαση για το άσυλό του.


Την Τετάρτη 7 Οκτώβρη εξετάζεται και πάλι προσφυγή επί του αιτήματος ασύλου του, απόφαση για την οποία χρειάζεται να εκδοθεί το συντομότερο δυνατό καθώς η απεργία πείνας του Soner βρίσκεται σε εξαιρετική επικίνδυνο στάδιο. O Soner Inanç δε ζητάει τίποτα περισσότερο και τίποτα λιγότερο από μια ανεπηρέαστη απόφαση, η οποία θα αναγνωρίσει την ουσία του ζητήματος: ο Soner Inanç διώκεται πολιτικά και ως εκ τούτου ποινικά από το τουρκικό κράτος και τους κατασταλτικούς μηχανισμούς του. Η πολιτική στοχοποίηση στο ελληνικό κράτος είναι μια δεύτερη δίωξη, η οποία καταστρατηγεί κάθε έννοια ασύλου.


Στηρίζουμε σε όλα τα επίπεδα την άμεση απελευθέρωση και απόδοση πολιτικού ασύλου στον Soner Inanç. Σε αυτήν την κατεύθυνση καλούμε σε:

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "Incredible Moment for the Borderlands": Judge Blocks Border Wall Expansion in Big Bend & West Texas
content:
In a victory for environmentalists and immigration rights’ advocates, a federal judge in El Paso, Texas, has blocked further border wall construction inside Big Bend National Park. “We slammed the brakes on $7 billion worth of corrupt construction contracts,” says Laiken Jordahl, a national public lands advocate with the Center for Biological Diversity, which sued to block the expansion. “We have effectively stopped construction across West Texas, and it’s incredible.”


Jordahl also responds to the Trump administration’s excavation of a 200-year-old cottonwood tree on the Arizona-Mexico border that had been protected by activists for months. “Watching those videos of them toppling this ancient tree that was very likely older than the border itself is symbolic of how

DHS

 has treated the border region. They see our communities, our wildlife, our nature as a sacrifice zone,” says Jordahl.

author: Andrés
title: Dos años bordando historias: memoria, identidad y comunidad
content:
Foto: Daniel Ávalos


«Bordando Historias – Construyendo Memoria» cumplió dos años y lo celebró con música, baile y encuentro entre distintas comunidades. Mujeres paraguayas y bolivianas compartieron sus danzas, la música del norte argentino acompañó la jornada y la memoria volvió a aparecer como un territorio común. A pocos días del 12 de octubre, la celebración puso en el centro la diversidad cultural y las historias de quienes construyen sus identidades lejos de los relatos oficiales.

Por Daniel Ávalos (ANRed).


Hay memorias que se escriben con palabras y otras que se construyen con las manos. Hay historias que sobreviven en fotografías, en relatos familiares, en canciones y también en una tela atravesada por hilos de colores. Hace dos años nació Bordando Historias – Construyendo Memoria, un espacio que encontró en el bordado una herramienta para recuperar historias, encontrarse y construir memoria colectiva. Ayer, sus integrantes celebraron ese recorrido con una jornada donde el arte, la música y las distintas identidades culturales ocuparon el centro de la escena.


La celebración tuvo música y baile. Mujeres compartieron sus danzas, mientras la música del norte argentino acompañó un encuentro que reafirmó los lazos entre distintas comunidades. Porque allí donde muchas veces se construyen fronteras, el encuentro puede convertirse en una forma de resistencia.


El aniversario estuvo atravesado también por la proximidad del 12 de octubre, Día del Respeto a la Diversidad Cultural. Una fecha que invita a revisar las miradas históricas sobre los pueblos originarios y, al mismo tiempo, a reconocer las múltiples culturas que forman parte del presente. En ese sentido, la celebración de Bordando Historias tuvo algo de declaración colectiva: las identidades no están congeladas en el pasado. Se encuentran, se mezclan, se transforman y se sostienen en comunidad.


Foto: Daniel Ávalos


El espacio está vinculado además a la memoria de los trabajadores textiles, con las historias de quienes padecieron condiciones de explotación y precarización, particularmente en torno a la Masacre de Luis Viale, ocurrida en 2006.


Recuperar ese pasado es también poner en discusión las condiciones de vida y trabajo de las comunidades migrantes y de los sectores populares. Pero la memoria no apareció ayer como una pieza de museo. Apareció viva. En las manos que bordan. En las mujeres que bailan. En las canciones compartidas. En las distintas maneras de hablar, de recordar y de celebrar. En una comunidad que se reconoce diversa y que hace de esa diversidad un punto de encuentro.


Dos años de Bordando Historias son dos años de construir memoria desde abajo, de recuperar voces y de transformar el recuerdo en encuentro. Puntada a puntada, historia a historia, las distintas comunidades siguen tejiendo una trama común. Quizá allí esté la potencia de este espacio: entender que la memoria no solamente se conserva; también se construye colectivamente, se baila, se canta y se vuelve presente.

From the 1880s through the 1940s tens of thousands of anarchists were active in the United States, the overwhelming majority of them first- and second-generation immigrants. But most were not yet devotees of the anarchist cause when they arrived on American shores. Instead, a clear link existed between migration and the embrace of anarchist ideology. This study asks how and why thousands of migrants became anarchists, and how their embrace of an anti-nationalist and cosmopolitan ideology shaped their identities, experiences and actions.

Utilizing anarchist publications, government surveillance files, and archival materials, it focuses on Eastern European Jews and Italians—the two largest segments of the anarchist movement by the turn of the century—and the development of anarchism among these groups in three important centers of American anarchism: New York’s Lower East Side, Paterson, New Jersey, and San Francisco. It then follows the changing fortunes of the movement in the face of war, the Russian Revolution, the First Red Scare, and the birth of communism and fascism, and ends with an examination of immigrant American anarchist participation in the Spanish Civil War of 1936–39, and that conflict’s dramatic impact on the movement in the United States.

This study argues that it was American conditions that usually made immigrants into anarchists, rather than European ones, inextricably linking the histories of migration and American anarchism. author: Joshua W.J. Brown
title: What replaced the slave trade?
content:
The first thought came out ugly because the event itself was ugly: tens of thousands of people moving at once toward Ceuta, a Spanish city in North Africa, beaches and roads filling, people dying, police lines folding, rumors moving faster than governments. I looked at Morocco on one side, Spain and the European Union on the other, and thought: What exactly is being traded here?

I don’t mean that migrants are slaves. They aren’t. That isn’t the argument, and collapsing the two would make the argument stupid. Slavery means ownership: a human being captured, bought, sold, inherited, coerced, and legally treated as property. A migrant is not somebody else’s property simply because a state wants to stop him, move her, return them, admit them, or keep them out.

What I’m asking is what came after. What happens to economies and states that once participated in systems where human movement itself generated external value? Does abolition erase that logic, or does value move somewhere else?

Ceuta is where the question became impossible for me to ignore.

On July 30, more than 70,000 people crossed or attempted to cross

 from Morocco into the Spanish enclave in the largest such surge the border has seen.

Current reporting doesn’t support the easy conspiracy version

. Economic frustration mattered. False claims spread online that the border was open. Smugglers and informal networks mattered. Moroccan security forces were overwhelmed, and Morocco later reinforced the frontier and prosecuted people accused of facilitating the crossing. If I have to invent a secret order from Rabat to make my argument work, then I don’t have an argument.

But I don’t need one. Europe already pays for migration control in public.

In 2023, the European Union announced a

€152 million migration program for Morocco

 covering border management, anti-smuggling work, migration and asylum policy, voluntary returns, and reintegration. The EU describes cooperation with countries of origin and transit as a core part of its migration system. In July 2026, on the very day the Ceuta crisis exploded, the

European Commission announced new funding calls

 for migration partnerships, border management, and internal security with partner countries.

That isn’t a scandal by itself. Borders cost money. Refugees need housing. Smuggling networks need to be investigated. Returns require cooperation between governments. A state beside a major migration route will obviously spend resources managing it, and there is nothing inherently corrupt about Europe sharing that cost.

The problem appears when I follow the incentive one step farther.

If Europe places a high political value on keeping irregular migration outside Europe, then the government that is capable of helping to accomplish this goal possesses something Europe wants. Geography becomes valuable. Police cooperation becomes valuable. Readmission becomes valuable. Hosting becomes valuable. The ability to make movement harder becomes valuable. And, in the darker version, the possibility that cooperation might disappear becomes valuable too.

Nobody has to sell the migrant. The migrant can still generate leverage simply by being movable.

That’s the distinction I keep coming back to. Under slavery, the person was the commodity. In the modern system, control around the person can become the asset.

The literature already has pieces of this. Scholars write about migration diplomacy, refugee rentier states, remittance dependence, border externalization, and coercive migration. I’m not trying to rename their work. I’m trying to put those pieces beside the historical question that bothered me in the first place: After an economy loses the legal right to trade people, what actually replaces the external income and political structures that trade supported?

My first formulation was too clean. I thought: These countries stayed poor because they never replaced slavery with productive economies. Morocco itself disproves that sentence. It manufactures cars. It exports phosphates and fertilizers. It has tourism, agriculture, logistics, major infrastructure projects, and growing industrial capacity.

The IMF estimated Moroccan real GDP growth at 4.9 percent in 2025

.

In the first four months of 2026, automotive products were its leading export

. This is not an economy that can honestly be reduced to migration.

But that correction doesn’t kill the question. It makes it better.

A country can build a modern productive …

title: Συνέντευξη Τύπου για την Απεργία Πείνας του Πολιτικού Πρόσφυγα Soner İnanç - 10/5/2026, 11:59:17 AM
content:
Κάλεσμα από τη συνέλευση

Solidarity with Migrants

:


Ο Soner İnanç, πολιτικός αγωνιστής για τα εργατικά δικαιώματα και τις δημοκρατικές ελευθερίες, είναι από τις 27 Αυγούστου σε απεργία πείνας σε καθεστώς κράτησης, ενώ κινδυνεύει με άμεση απέλαση λόγω της ενδεχόμενης απόρριψης της αίτησής του για άσυλο.


O πολιτικός πρόσφυγας Soner İnanç αναγκάστηκε να εγκαταλείψει την Τουρκία καθώς έχει στοχοποιηθεί για τη δράση του από το τουρκικό κράτος και ήδη έχει φυλακιστεί στο παρελθόν για τη συμμετοχή του στο κίνημα του Gezi Park.


Μετά την απορριπτική απόφαση ως προς το αρχικό αίτημα ασύλου του, Soner İnanç κατέθεσε αίτημα ακύρωσης και ακολούθησε όλες τις σχετικές διαδικασίες. Τέλη Ιουλίου, συνελήφθη και βρέθηκε σε διοικητική κράτησης στο ΑΤ Λαυρίου.


Ένα μήνα μετά, μεταφέρθηκε στη Θεσσαλονίκη με σκοπό την απέλαση του. Μετά από τέσσερις εβδομάδες στέρησης βιταμινών, αναγκαίων για την μη ύπαρξη μόνιμων επιπτώσεων, το αίτημα αυτό άρχισε να καλύπτεται όπως όφειλε εξαρχής μετά από συνεχή πολιτική κινητοποίηση και δημοσιογραφική κάλυψη για τον κίνδυνο τον οποίο διατρέχει αν δεν του χορηγηθούν.


Το ΠΡΟΚΕΚΑ Παρανεστίου οφείλει, παράλληλα, ως απεργός πείνας, ο Soner İnanç να παρακολουθείται από ανεξάρτητη ιατρική επιτροπή για να διασφαλιστεί η απρόσκοπτη άσκηση της ως πολιτική δράση με συγκεκριμένα αιτήματα: τη συνέχιση της διαδικασίας απόδοση ασύλου, την μη απέλαση του στην Τουρκία και την απελευθέρωσή του.


Ο Soner δηλώνει αποφασισμένος να συνεχίσει στον αγώνα του, αφού κρατείται άδικα, περιμένοντας νέα απόφαση για το άσυλό του.


Ως Solidarity with Migrants, γνωρίσαμε τον Soner στο στρατόπεδο προσφύγων Οινοφύτων όπου πάντα προσπαθούσε με όλα τα δυνατά μέσα να υποστηρίζει τα δικαιώματα όλων των προσφύγων με μια βαθιά διεθνιστική προσήλωση. Η "λογική" των αποφάσεων της υπηρεσίας ασύλου καταδεικνύει τις συνέπειες των μεγάλων αλλαγών που έχουν επέλθει στο καθεστώς ασύλου τα τελευταία έτη καθώς έχουμε να κάνουμε με την καταστρατήγηση της έννοιας του πολιτικού ασύλου.


Γι'αυτό και ο αγώνας του Soner είναι και αγώνας για το πολιτικό άσυλο γενικότερα και χρειάζεται τη στήριξη όλων μας.


H συνέντευξη τύπου θα πραγματοποιηθεί τη Δευτέρα 5 Οκτωβρίου στο Στέκι Μεταναστών, Τσαμαδού 13 Εξάρχεια, ώρα 12 το μεσημέρι.

Die italienische Seenotrettungsleitstelle war bereits 12 Stunden vor der Rettung der Schiffbrüchigen von der Notrufhotline Alarm Phone über den Notfall informiert worden. Sea-Watch liegen zudem deutliche Hinweise darauf vor, dass die Europäische Grenz- und Küstenwache Frontex am Abend des 28. September mit ihrem Flugzeug Eagle6 über den Notfallort geflogen ist. author: Mohammed Altaj
title: Israel Above the Law … Palestine Beyond Justice
content:
The world did not lack knowledge of what was happening to Palestinians.

It knew that a people had been living under occupation for decades; that land was being confiscated, settlements expanding, homes demolished, and checkpoints cutting cities and villages off from one another.

The United Nations knew. Governments knew. Parliaments and international courts knew.

The shift now visible across significant parts of Western public opinion did not begin because the world suddenly discovered new facts about Palestine.

What changed was the distance between the news and the human being.

People saw what war means when a child is trapped beneath rubble, what displacement means when a family carries whatever it can and walks away without knowing where it will go.

And the numbers began to acquire names, faces and voices.

One of those names was Hind Rajab.

I do not mention Hind because her story encompasses everything that happened in Gaza. I mention her because some tragedies become windows through which people see what numbers alone cannot reveal.

Hind was trapped inside a car in Gaza in January 2024 after members of her family had been killed. She called for help. Twelve days later, she was found dead inside the car. The two paramedics sent to rescue her were also found dead.

But Hind was no longer a number.

The world also saw seven World Central Kitchen aid workers killed in Israeli strikes while carrying out humanitarian work. And even after the ceasefire announced in October 2025, the killing did not end. According to Palestinian Ministry of Health figures cited by the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, by September 23, 2026, 1,402 Palestinians had been killed and 4,881 injured since the ceasefire announcement.

Bodies remained beneath the rubble, while families waited to reach loved ones not to save them this time, but to bury them.

But Palestinian history did not begin in Gaza.

And it did not begin on October 7, 2023.

In 1994, Baruch Goldstein, an Israeli settler and member of the Kach movement, opened fire on Muslim worshippers in the Ibrahimi Mosque in Hebron, killing at least twenty-nine people. In 2014, sixteen-year-old Mohammed Abu Khdeir was abducted from Shuafat, beaten and burned alive. A year later, the Dawabsheh family home in Duma was set on fire while the family slept; toddler Ali and later both his parents died.

So when a Palestinian is asked to begin the story on the morning of October 7, he is effectively being asked to erase what came before.

None of this makes the targeting of civilians acceptable, whoever they are.

Justice cannot begin halfway through history.

By September 14, 2026, the United Nations had documented more than 1,600 settler attacks resulting in Palestinian casualties, property damage, or both, across 275 Palestinian communities since the beginning of the year. More than 1,500 Palestinians had been displaced because of demolitions of structures lacking Israeli-issued permits, while more than 2,600 had been displaced in the context of settler violence and related access restrictions.

Between September 15 and 21 alone, the UN documented 51 settler attacks resulting in casualties, property damage, or both. At least 800 olive, fruit and palm trees were damaged, uprooted or burned. In the same week, demolitions displaced 147 Palestinians, including 73 children.

These are not isolated incidents.

This is land being transformed, communities disappearing, families being pushed out.

And this is where the phrase “extremist settlers” is no longer enough.

Who plans the settlements? Who allocates the land? Who builds the roads, extends the infrastructure and provides the protection?

At what point does settler violence cease to be merely the act of an individual and become a problem within the system itself?

In September 2026, UN Secretary-General António Guterres warned that settlement expansion was accelerating, outposts were proliferating and settler violence was rising to alarming levels. He also warned that advancing the E1 settlement plan would deal a “deathblow” to the prospect of a contiguous and viable Palestinian state.

How, then, can the world continue to declare its support for a two-state solution while the geography on which one of those states is supposed to exist is being transformed?

The problem is not confined to land.

Η

7η Οκτωβρίου

Μια συνέχεια της αντίστασης που χρονολογείται από τη στιγμή της ίδρυσης του κράτους του “Ισραήλ” το 1948, αλλά και ακόμη νωρίτερα, κατά τη διάρκεια της βρετανικής αποικιακής κατοχής. Ήταν ένας λαός και ένα κίνημα που ξεσηκώθηκαν ενάντια στην κατοχή. Η ημέρα αυτή θα συνεχίσει να τιμάται ως τέτοια για τις επόμενες γενιές, ακόμη και αν οι σιωνιστές και οι ιμπεριαλιστές προσπαθήσουν με κάθε μέσο να ελέγξουν και να αλλάξουν το αφήγημα. Τα αλεξίπτωτα πλαγιάς που πετούσαν πάνω από τον φράχτη προς την κατεχόμενη Παλαιστίνη, ο φράχτης που περιέκλειε τη Γάζα και γκρεμίστηκε από τους ανθρώπους που εκδιώχθηκαν από τη γη τους πριν από δεκαετίες: αυτές οι εικόνες δεν θα ξεχαστούν και θα παραμείνουν στη μνήμη μας ως σύμβολα της αντίστασης του Παγκόσμιου Νότου.


Η απάντηση της σιωνιστικής οντότητας, με την υποστήριξη των ΗΠΑ, υπήρξε ανελέητη. Από τον Οκτώβριο του 2023 γινόμαστε μάρτυρες μιας γενοκτονίας που μεταδίδεται ζωντανά και πολλών φρικαλεοτήτων που διαπράττονται από τη σιωνιστική οντότητα και τους ιμπεριαλιστές των ΗΠΑ (με την υποστήριξη ευρωπαϊκών κρατών). Η Γάζα έχει ισοπεδωθεί από τους βομβαρδισμούς και, παρόλο που γίνεται λόγος για κατάπαυση του πυρός, συνεχίζουν να βομβαρδίζουν και να πυροβολούν αδιακρίτως. Ο Λίβανος και η Συρία τελούν υπό κατοχή και δέχονται συνεχείς επιθέσεις από τη σιωνιστική οντότητα. Οι κυβερνήσεις αυτών των περιοχών καταστέλλουν την αντίσταση και την εναντίωση στη Δύση και το “Ισραήλ” στα εδάφη τους, ενεργώντας ως εντολοδόχοι των ΗΠΑ. Όλα αυτά συμβαίνουν ενώ το “Ισραήλ” καταλαμβάνει όλο και περισσότερα εδάφη, αποσταθεροποιώντας περαιτέρω την περιοχή.


Το κράτος του “Ισραήλ” και οι ΗΠΑ καταστρέφουν ορισμένες από τις αρχαιότερες περιοχές με συνεχή κατοίκηση στην ιστορία του πολιτισμού, στην Παλαιστίνη, τον Λίβανο, τη Συρία και το Ιράν. author: heinhtetkyaw
title: Simone Weil: The waning of the working class, technique and the rise of fascism
content:
The only hope of socialism resides in those who have already brought about in themselves, as far as is possible in the society of today, that union between manual and intellectual labour which characterizes the society we are aiming at. ~ Simone Weil

The long-foreseen moment has arrived when capitalism is on the point of seeing its development arrested by impassable barriers. In whatever way we interpret the phenomenon of accumulation, it is clear that capitalism stands essentially for economic expansion and that capitalist expansion has now nearly reached the point where it will be halted by the actual limits of the earth’s surface. And yet never have there been fewer premonitory signs of the advent of socialism. We are in a period of transition; but a transition towards what? No one has the slightest idea. All the more striking, therefore, the carefree security with which we settle down in this transition period as though it were a definite stage, so much so that considerations concerning the crisis of the system have almost everywhere become commonplaces. Certainly, we can always go on believing that socialism will arrive the day after tomorrow, and make a duty or a virtue of this belief; so long as we go on taking, day by day, the day after tomorrow to mean the next day but one after today, we shall be sure not to be disappointed; but such a state of mind is difficult to distinguish from that of those worthy people who believe, for instance, in the Last Judgment. If we want to traverse this sombre age in manly fashion, we shall refrain, like the Ajax of Sophocles, from letting empty hopes set us afire.

Throughout history men have struggled, suffered and died to free the oppressed. Their efforts, when they did not remain sterile, have never led to anything except the replacing of one oppressive régime by another. Marx, who had observed this, thought he was able to demonstrate scientifically that things were different in our day, and that the struggle of the oppressed would now lead to a true emancipation, not to a new oppression. It is this idea, which we have preserved as an article of faith, that we need to examine afresh, unless we mean systematically to close our eyes to the events of the past twenty years. Let us spare ourselves the disillusionments of those who, having fought for Liberty, Equality, Fraternity, discovered one fine day that what they had got was, as Marx says, Infantry, Cavalry, Artillery. But they at any rate were able to draw some lesson from the surprises of history; sadder is the lot of those who perished in 1792 or 1793, in the street or on the frontiers, fully convinced that with their lives they were purchasing the freedom of mankind. If we are to perish in the battles of the future, let us do our best to prepare ourselves to perish with a clear vision of the world we shall be leaving behind.

The Paris Commune was an example not only of the creative power of the working-class masses in movement, but also of the fundamental impotence of a spontaneous movement when it comes to fighting against organized forces of repression. August 1914 marked the bankruptcy of proletarian mass organizations, both on the political and the trade-union planes, within the framework of the system. From then onwards it became necessary to abandon once and for all the hopes placed in this mode of organization not only by the reformists, but by Engels. On the other hand, October 1917 ushered in new and radiant prospects. At last the means had been found of combining legal with illegal action, the systematic labours of disciplined militants with the spontaneous seething of the masses. All over the world communist parties were to be formed to which the Bolshevik party would pass on its knowledge and technique; they were to replace social democracy, already described by Rosa Luxemburg, in August 1914, as a “stinking corpse”, and very soon to disappear from the stage of history; and they were to seize power within a very short time. The political régime set up spontaneously by the workers of Paris in 1871, then by those of St. Petersburg in 1905, was to become solidly entrenched in Russia and so on to embrace the entire civilized world. author: Monthly Review Press
title: In Amsterdam in November? Head to Pakuis de Zwijger for Chris dePloeg’s “The Exterminating Empire”
content:
Join

Pakuis de Zwijger

 for a conversation with author Chris de Ploeg about his new book, a radical and urgent indictment of the global capitalist system and the imperial violence it unleashes upon people and planet alike. At its core, the book argues that genocide and ecocide are not tragic byproducts of capitalism – they are its fundamental features. Together with renowned climate author Jason Hickel (in person), frontline Palestinian surgeon Ghassan Abu-Sittah (joining online) and our moderator, climate justice activist and researcher Harriët Bergman, we will dive deeper into the interconnections of the great challenges of our time–and more importantly, how to fight back. There will also be cultural performances from Chihiro Geuzebroek and brothers Chris and Max de Ploeg, tying their ancestral struggles in Bolivia and Armenia to the global struggle for liberation.


REVIEWS:


Counterpunch

, “

Resisting Annihilation: Reviewing “The Exterminating Empire”

, by Seth Sandronsky


“…de Ploeg, who does far more than compile lists of atrocities, draws parallels between the American holocaust of the native inhabitants’ relations with buffaloes and Israel’s genocide against Palestinians and their farming of olive trees. Land theft and separating those living on the land from it are nothing new. The author has skin in the game, given his family survived the Armenian genocide and Nazi holocaust…”


Counterpunch

, “

Capitalism is Waging War on Palestine While Creating a Burning Planet

” by Daniel Falcone:


Daniel Falcone:

What is the central argument of

The Exterminating Empire

 and how is the book structured? It looks as though the book serves as an intervention as well as an addition to current scholarship.  


Chris Kaspar de Ploeg:

 I open the book with some jarring facts that seem paradoxical at first sight. We need about 30 percent of our productive capacity to

give everyone on the planet a good life

. Not just the basics like housing, clothing and healthcare, but also modern appliances like refrigerators, laptops, access to the internet and more. At the same time, that standard of living is denied to about

80 percent of the world population

. Green energy has been cheaper than fossil fuels for years, yet climate breakdown is only accelerating. We could

solve world hunger

 with about 0.03 percent of global GDP, but hunger is only increasing.


That looks like an extraordinarily wasteful system, and it is. The point, however, is that under capitalism, these are not paradoxes at all. In fact, they are signs of capital’s success. Under our current economic system, the primary goal, ruthlessly pursued, is

profit maximization

. That profit maximization is reached through pushing down costs–and we are those costs, our labour, our environments, our lives–and by conquering markets, often through a mix of military and economic warfare. That essentially puts

capitalism on a warpath against life

. The system is working exactly as it is supposed to.


We see, for example, that profit rates are higher in the fossil fuel industry because it essentially

functions through monopolies

, despite the higher costs. We see that the military-industrial complex is growing exponentially, targeting any vestiges of resistance against

US-led global hegemony

, which globalized harsh budget cuts in social welfare, healthcare and education. These very conditions of

structural impoverishment

 then create the conditions of desperation necessary for people and countries to accept their status as sources for cheap labour, resources and land for global corporations, mostly centered in the Global North.


In the book I write about a dialectic between slavery and genocide, and between structural genocide and active genocide. A good way to understand that relationship is by going back to the

We Charge Genocide petition

, which was presented in 1951 at the United Nations by William L. Patterson, on behalf of the

Civil Rights Congress

. He estimated that, since the abolition of slavery, some 10,000 black people had been lynched, often for something as small as looking a white woman in the eyes. These lynchings were not hidden affairs, but were a

public spectacle

, for which neighbors came together, and pictures were spread on postcards across the country.


Patterson

 goes on to argue that this kind of active violence serves a deeper purpose. It was meant to intimidate the black masses to accept lower living standards …

author: Julius Gavroche
title: “If Bolsonaro wins, they kill us; if Lula wins, they let us die.”
content:
from the

CrimethInc.

 collective, 29/09/2026


On the 2026 Elections in Brazil


In Brazil, the third term of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva of the Workers’ Party is drawing to a close. Lula could win a fourth term—making him the most-elected politician in the country’s history—if he defeats the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro. However, Flávio Bolsonaro—son of the man dubbed the “Trump of the Tropics,” who attempted

a coup d’état in 2023

 strikingly similar to the one Donald Trump attempted in 2021—is dangerously close to taking the lead in the polls.


It is time to assess the threats that a new Bolsonaro administration would pose, as well as the risks that will remain or emerge under a continuing center-left government. We spoke with fellow Brazilian anarchists active on a variety of fronts about the challenges that both scenarios could pose to human beings, the environment, and social movements resisting capitalism and colonialism.


Flavio Bolsonaro in a photo-op with Trump in May 2026 during a meeting at which he lobbied for the US to designate Brazilian drug cartels as “terrorist groups.”


What the 2026 Elections Mean for Brazil and the Americas


The 2026 election will determine to what extent the gains achieved through hard-fought social struggles are stripped away. Just as Trump returned to power via the 2024 election, there is a risk that Flávio Bolsonaro could resume his father’s attacks on the working class, marginalized groups, women, Indigenous peoples, and the environment. The Workers’ Party and the left in general have not managed to produce new figures to succeed their charismatic leader; without Lula, they appear doomed to electoral defeat.


There is a risk that the left will fail to field an effective new candidate for 2030, when Lula will no longer be eligible for reelection. It is also likely that, if elected, Lula could fall victim to the so-called “

incumbency crisis

“—a pattern that has emerged in elections worldwide this decade. Leaders on both the left and the right see their public standing erode after taking office, as they fail to address the inexorable impact of capitalism on the lives of ordinary people. Symbolism and abstract ideology carry significant weight in the increasingly polarized political landscapes of bourgeois electoral politics, and around the world, the ruling class is relying less and less on the carrot and more and more on the stick.


Therefore, it is likely that the far right will soon return to power. This is a reality we must face. It could happen in 2030, but it could occur as early as 2026.


This is taking place in a context in which Trump’s United States is attempting to reorganize the world order through force, showing everyone what anarchists have always known: that representative democracy, international law, and institutions like the United Nations exist at the pleasure of the ruling class and will not protect us. In the course of its first fourteen months in power, the second Trump administration toppled two heads of state—killing the Iranian leader and abducting the Venezuelan president. In both cases, there was open talk of seizing the oil from these territories; in Venezuela, the administration successfully stole billions of barrels, which are now under Washington’s control.


As head of state, Flávio Bolsonaro would voluntarily hand over Brazilian workers, forests, and land to US imperial interests. We are already in a dire situation under the neoliberal arrangement that Lula manages; with a fascist who is beholden to the US in power, the struggle for survival would become even harder. Furthermore, the oil, minerals, rivers, and forests in the territory known as Brazil would serve to fuel the technological, military, and nuclear arms race that endangers life across the entire planet.


The United States is openly attempting to interfere in Brazilian elections to favor Bolsonaro by sending “observers” to

question election results

 and threatening to impose further tariffs on Brazil. At the same time, the US-based company Meta—which controls much of the content circulating on social media—is

blocking Lula’s campaign content

 just weeks before the election without explanation. The same elites with the same reactionary agenda control both military power and the companies that dominate technology and digital communication.

The Consequences of Lula’s Third Term …

Anarchism and Insurrectionary Anarchism

Hacktivism as Digital Insurrection

Examples of Hacktivist Resistance

The essay you are about to read was written in the past when I was an early grad student still becoming a realized writer of anarchism’s ideas. Some of the information may be overly moralistic and other points may be overly empirical. Some of the writing may be overly casual while other areas may be overly academic. Some information that should be cited may not be, and some information that is cited may not have to be. My standpoints and interpretations of ideas throughout this piece may have changed since its writing, but it was my analysis at the time that I stood behind and defended. For any questions on the information presented, my updated perspectives and beliefs, or anything of the like, feel free to message me directly. If you believe the question you are asking is of good faith and may encourage a fruitful conversation including others, feel free to comment below to start the conversation. Be kind.

On December 29, 2025, a hacker known as Martha Root took the stage at an annual hacking convention in Hamburg, Germany. Dressed in a pink Power Rangers outfit, she shared how for months, she had been infiltrating three white supremacist dating websites by creating AI chatbots to interact with users while collecting their personal information. In the panel’s final fifteen minutes, she remotely accessed and deleted all three websites, much to the neo-Nazi website creator’s disapproval, which he described in a tweet as “cyberterrorism.” Root noted how easy it was to hack into the websites, citing “poor cybersecurity hygiene that would make even your grandma’s AOL account blush.”[1] Root’s actions can arguably show how the principles of insurrectionary anarchism, such as direct, autonomous, and disruptive intervention, can extend from physical spaces into the digital realm. Such actions can include Root’s hacking/hacktivism as well as DDoS attacks and the targeted takedowns of extremist, corporate, or state-controlled websites. Cyberspace itself can be seen as a loosely-governed libertarian space that offers hackers near-total freedom to translate traditional anarchist tactics into digital actions. Insurrectionary anarchism can take form in contemporary digital spaces through autonomous hacktivism, the disruption or removal of oppressive online networks, and decentralized digital interventions.

Anarchism can be defined as a sociopolitical philosophy that is against hierarchies wherever they may be found. Le samedi 10 octobre, de 9h30 à 18h, Radio Libertaire sera en direct et en public depuis l'

AERI

, 57 rue Etienne Marcel à Montreuil (Métro Croix de Chavaux) pour diffuser et enregistrer les débats du Colloque «

 

Anarchie, Femmes, Émancipation

 

».


Radio Libertaire, sur le 89,4

FM

 et en streaming sur le site

https://radio-libertaire.org/accueil.php


Depuis le 150

e

 anniversaire de la Commune de Paris en 2021, groupe Commune de Paris de la Fédération anarchiste consacre annuellement une journée d'étude à un des thèmes majeurs de cette révolution. Ce fut le cas avec l'autogestion, l'art et la culture, la place des idées anarchistes dans la Commune… En 2026, quatre groupes de la région parisienne, les Groupes Louise Michel, Salvador Segui, Pierre Besnard et Commune de Paris organisent une journée destinée aux femmes, à leur rôle pendant la Commune, en projetant leurs revendications dans les luttes actuelles en France et dans le monde.


Aujourd'hui, comment les luttes des femmes participent à la perspective anarchiste

 

?


Sur tous les continents, les femmes luttent malgré les guerres, les dictatures, les emprisonnements, les déplacements forcés, les violences sexuelles. La situation des femmes relève aussi de l'apartheid de genre et, les féminicides ne cessent. Mais les combats pour le droit à l'avortement, à la scolarisation, à l'accès à l'emploi, à l'égalité des salaires se rejoignent contre le patriarcat et le capitalisme. De même du côté du genre et de la pensée queer, ou dans le champ culturel, apparaissent des revendications contre l'invisibilisation des femmes, sur la liberté du corps, le respect de chacun et chacune, être libre. Il reste à continuer de définir et de faire vivre l'anarcha- féminisme.

author: Unknown
title: Thomas More : L'utopie - lecture Anarchiste du 12 octobre 2026
content:
L'Utopie n'a pas attendu les anarchistes. Le mot est créé par Thomas More qui le met en titre de son livre, paru en 1513, et lui donne un contenu toujours aussi brûlant.


u-topie : du grec ‘u' qui signifie ‘sans' et ‘topos' qui signifie ‘lieu'.


Un projet sans lieu, hors sol

 

? Si Thomas More a le mérite d'avoir inventé le mot, son livre a surtout suscité beaucoup d'engouement et provoqué un débat qui s'est prolongé jusqu'à nous, malgré les perplexités qui l'ont accompagné... Mais ce n'était qu'un début

 

!


Les anarchistes ne sont pas des rêveurs, ils veulent donner à l'utopie une dimension concrète : construire une société égalitaire et libertaire.


La question de l'utopie sera au cœur des lectures anarchistes durant l'année 2026/2027.


À une époque qui ne cesse d'en appeler au réalisme, au pragmatisme, voire à un utilitarisme étroit, où le mot «

 

dystopie

 

» s'est imposé au regard des menaces politiques, économiques et écologiques qui hantent les sociétés actuelles, l'utopie a-t-elle encore une place dans les débats politiques

 

? Entendre : une place autre que celle que lui vaut l'usage méprisant de l'adjectif «

 

utopique

 

» dans l'expression «

 

c'est utopique

 

»

 

? Au fil de séances à venir, nous proposons donc la lecture de quelques grands textes consacrés à l'utopie – ou, plus justement, aux utopies rédigées par quelques auteurs marquants – ou aux commentaires critiques qu'ils ont suscités.


Chaque séquence s'appuiera ainsi sur un texte, présenté en ouverture de la causerie, de manière à introduire le débat. Les participants seront ensuite invités à y prendre une part active.


Ci-dessous, le programme de cette année 2026-2027 des lectures anarchistes :


 12 octobre : Thomas More - L'Utopie

 9 novembre : Voltaire - Candide ou l'optimisme, chap. 17 et 18

 14 décembre : Denis Diderot - Supplément au voyage de Bougainville

 11 janvier : Charles Fourrier - Le nouveau monde industriel et sociétal

 8 février : Victor Considérant - Exposé abrégé du système phalanstérien

 8 mars : Étienne Cabet - Voyage en Icarie

 12 avril : Louis Blanc : Organisation du travail

 10 mai : Joseph Dejacque - L'Humanisphère, utopie anarchique

 14 juin : Friedrich Engels - Socialisme utopique et socialisme scientifique


L'objectif de ces causeries, inspirées des causeries du 19

e

 siècle, est de créer un espace social, où l'on peut échanger en dehors du cadre du travail ou du cadre amical/familial, faire société ensemble. C'est un espace où on peut confronter nos idées et nos arguments et y politiser nos vies, face à un système qui nous pousse de plus en plus à en être passif.


Chacun.e y est légitime pour prendre la parole, ou simplement écouter. Chacun.e y est légitime pour modérer la parole, dans une organisation sans hiérarchie, une organisation anarchiste.


Vous pouvez amener quelques victuailles à partager lors des causeries. Aussi bien à manger qu'à boire, même si le bar est ouvert.

author: heinhtetkyaw
title: Bad Anarchism: Aestheticized Mythmaking and the Legacy of Georges Sorel
content:
This is a peer-reviewed article published via "Anarchist Developments in Cultural Studies (ADCS)". Link: https://journals.uvic.ca/index.php/adcs/article/download/17818/7439/0

This article considers the varied impact of the notion of revolutionary consciousness first developed by the French political theorist Georges Sorel (1847–1922) on proponents of anarchism and Marxism, including Walter Benjamin, Bart de Light, Frantz Fanon, Antonio Gramsci and, most recently, Ernesto Laclau and Chantal Mouffe.

I question the strategy amongst these thinkers to draw selectively from Sorel’s writings in an attempt to create a cordon sanitaire around those aspects of his thought that are problematic by virtue of their impact on proto-fascist and fascist ideologues throughout Europe. In addressing this issue.

I examine how Sorel’s anarchist theory of anti-Statism, constructed around the power of myths, led him to endorse anti-capitalist antiSemitism as an extension of class struggle; and I critique his Janusfaced concept of aestheticized violence as it relates to his quest for moral regeneration through revolution

author: Julius Gavroche
title: The subject, the proletariat, anarchist organisation and other nostalgias
content:
Barricade in Seville, Summer 1936


by Laura Vicente


It is quite possible that no one will pay much attention to this brief piece, but just in case, I will say in anticipation that my aim is modest and that I do not intend to be polemical, although I would not mind sharing arguments and thoughts, moving beyond the stereotypes we all hold that lead us to be obtuse and, at times, blind.


There are comrades who have been pondering the existence, or lack thereof, of the proletariat for some time, searching for the lost revolutionary subject, building “the” anarchist organization capable of developing “a” program, “a” strategy, and concrete tactics that will lead us down the path of revolution. I have not read all their writings, I am sorry to say, because I am exhausted by anarchism’s difficulty in imagining a way out of capitalism that does not involve returning to the past and to nostalgia, even melancholy. This is how two authors, Julie Graham and Katherine Gibson [who go under the pen name J. K. Gibson-Graham] perceive it in their book

A Post-Capitalist Politics

. They claim that a lack of imagination is a pathology of the left, something that reminds me of the “melancholy” of the left, applicable to anarchism, which Wendy Brown discusses in her essay on this topic. Leftist melancholy is a stance in which attachment to an identity or a political analysis of the past is stronger than interest in current possibilities for mobilisation, alliance, or transformation. The melancholic subject identifies with lost ideals and experiences their absence as feelings of desolation and dejection. This fixation on the past has a clear connection to the total paranoid theory that says nothing can happen. Fisher calls it a “severe Leninist superego”.

[1]


The proletariat, the working class, was the subject of the revolution in another era of industrial development that ended in the mid-20th century, not because there were no other subjects, but because of the power of the narrative that championed the proletariat. When we speak of workers’ consciousness as the foundation of their “being a subject,” it seems we’re talking about something pre-existing that simply needs to be awakened, discovered. But consciousness-raising, in reality, is a practice of collective discussion that underscores the inequalities under which people collectively live. Consciousness does not pre-exist, it is not given, but rather it must be constructed from our place within a structure of inequality (capitalism, patriarchy, white supremacy, colonialism). The way to construct it is with other people who share a similar material existence.


Class consciousness has receded because the idea that there is no alternative to capitalism has advanced; the narrative has fallen apart.


On the other hand, holding closed seminars, waiting for the right information, the advanced political and ideological discussion that shapes a well-defined strategy to “awaken” the revolutionary subject, bringing to the surface a situation capable of awakening action by the people or any other subject, does not fit with what I have learned in history, either today or yesterday. No theory has ever transformed reality.


I have not forgotten of the need to “organise anarchism” as if it were not already organized. It gives the impression that the real aim is to impose order on anarchist diversity and multiplicity, transforming these interconnected, horizontal, decentralised, and non-hierarchical networks into parts of a whole that must be “the” effective, hyper-organised anarchist organization with strong militancy, etc.

[2]


I recently said in an anarchist space that this debate is a men’s debate. The reality is that, even with women involved, the writings I have seen are by men. Reflecting on this, I concluded that women, and those perceived as such, have long known that there are other revolutionary subjects (think of

Mujeres Libres

, creating their own revolution between 1936 and 1939 and being ignored by the world, which is why I want to highlight them).


The struggles and events of the feminist movement were able to mobilise social transformation on an unprecedented scale, without resorting to a vanguard party or any of the other “needs” we have associated with political organisation (strategy, tactics, ideological narratives, modelled revolutions, etc.). title: ΒΑΛΚΑΝΙΚΟ ΑΝΑΡΧΙΚΟ ΦΕΣΤΙΒΑΛ ΒΙΒΛΙΟΥ ΣΤΑ ΣΚΟΠΙΑ Συνεισφορά στην επεξεργασία συγκεκριμένων δράσεων, επικεντρώνοντας σε μιλιταρισμό, φασισμό, παλαιστινιακό και διεθνιστική αλληλεγγύη
content:
Συνέντευξη με τον Αρτάν, μέλος της Αναρχικής Συλλογικότητας

Smokva

 των Σκοπίων, που διοργάνωσε το προ ημερών 18

ο

 Βαλκανικό Αναρχικό Φεστιβάλ Βιβλίου. Διατυπώνει μια πρώτη αποτίμηση, που επικεντρώθηκαν οι συζητήσεις, σε τι συνεισέφερε στα ευρύτερα ζητήματα και κυρίως ποιες αποφασίστηκε να είναι οι άμεσες δράσεις.


>Πώς αποτιμάται το 4ήμερο Βαλκανικό Αναρχικό Φεστιβάλ Βιβλίου στα Σκόπια;


Όπως είχαμε την ευκαιρία να συζητήσουμε, είχαμε μια πολύ ιδιαίτερη εμπειρία αυτού του φεστιβάλ στα Σκόπια. Αποτελεί μια από τις σημαντικές συνεισφορές στην περιοχή.


Τρία ή τέσσερα χρόνια πριν δεν θα είχαμε τέτοια δυνατότητα. Αλλά επειδή στο προηγούμενο ΒΑΒ στη Θεσσαλονίκη που ήμασταν περίπου 20 ακτιβιστές από εδώ γεννήθηκε η ιδέα να διεξαχθεί στα Σκόπια, κάτι που αποτέλεσε κίνητρο για εμάς και αμέσως αρχίσαμε την προετοιμασία του.


Έτσι άρχισε να ενεργοποιείται ένας κόσμος, ιδιαίτερα νεολαίοι που πριν δεν είχαν κάποια εμπλοκή με τα κινήματα. Κάτι που το είδαμε όλοι μας αυτές τις ημέρες με τη συμμετοχή τόσων ανθρώπων από την πόλη, εδώ.


>Σε ποια θέματα επικεντρώθηκαν οι εκδηλώσεις και συζητήσεις;


Ξεκινήσαμε από τοπικά ζητήματα της περιοχής αλλά και ευρύτερα διεθνή ζητήματα, όπως η γενοκτονία στη Γάζα και η διεθνιστική αλληλεγγύη στην Παλαιστίνη, η αντίδραση στον νέο μιλιταρισμό ιδιαίτερα στην Ευρώπη, η καταπίεση και καταστολή κα. Έτσι είχαμε αρκετές συζητήσεις πάνω σε αυτά τα θέματα και πώς θα οργανώσουμε την αντίστασή μας.


Επίσης, είχαμε συζητήσεις για τις πολιτικές, τους τρόπους οργάνωσης και τις κινητοποιήσεις ενάντια στον φασισμό στα Βαλκάνια, αλλά και στην Ευρώπη, και θα συνεχιστεί η συζήτηση μέχρι το επόμενο ΒΑΒ. Κάτι που αποτέλεσε συνεισφορά των συντρόφων που ήρθαν από ευρωπαϊκές χώρες, να μην περιοριστούμε στα Βαλκάνια αλλά ευρύτερα διεθνώς.


Άλλωστε τα Βαλκάνια σήμερα αποτελούν σημαντικό σημείο επικέντρωσης των αναρχικών διεθνώς. Και αυτό είναι ένα στοίχημα το πως μια βαλκανική οργάνωση μπορεί να συνεισφέρει ευρύτερα, κάτι που αναγνωρίζεται. Ήταν πρόκληση 14 χρόνια μετά την προηγούμενη διοργάνωση εδώ στα Σκόπια.


>Ποια μπορούμε να πούμε ότι είναι το σημαντικότερο χαρακτηριστικό αυτού του ΒΑΒ;


Νομίζω ένα από τα σημαντικότερα ήταν η μεγάλη συμμετοχή στις συνελεύσεις πάνω σε ζητήματα δράσης. Δεν μείναμε μόνο στο επίπεδο της κατάθεσης πολιτικών ιδεών αλλά στην επεξεργασία συγκεκριμένων βημάτων δράσης και όχι μόνο στα Βαλκάνια. Έτσι ελήφθησαν 3 συγκεκριμένες αποφάσεις.


Μια περιφερειακή και διεθνής αντιμιλιταριστική οργάνωση και μία ημέρα διεθνούς δράσης κατά του μιλιταρισμού. Όπως επίσης συζητήσαμε και για τον τόπο διοργάνωσης του επόμενου ΒΑΒ που θα καταληχθεί στον επόμενο μήνα.
