Саверио Мерлино пишет в первом номере этого журнала[1]: «Анархисты всегда страдали и остались бессильными вследствие разногласия, никогда не прекращавшегося в их среде между индивидуалистами и коммунистами, которые так же далеки друг от друга, как северный полюс от южного, и сходятся лишь в одном пункте: в ненависти к парламентаризму».

По моему мнению, Мерлино преувеличивает, приписывая бессилие анархистов разногласиям между коммунистами и индивидуалистами. Когда случаи оказывались благоприятными для действия и, главным образом, когда хотели и могли сделать что-либо практическое, забыв о разногласиях, коммунисты и индивидуалисты (я говорю, конечно, о тех, кто были действительно анархистами и, следовательно, верными принципу «ни господ, ни рабов») снова боролись бок-о-бок. Бессилие анархистов зависело от множества других причин, особенно от отсутствия немедленно годной к применению практической программы, за исключением, конечно, тех общих обстоятельств, среди которых они были вынуждены действовать. Иными словами, дело заключается в том, что они смотрели на идеал, опережая этим своё время, и поэтому, вместо того чтобы воплощать свои идеи в жизнь, считали себя обязанными своим апостольством приблизить тот час, когда осуществление станет возможным.

Мерлино еще преувеличивает, когда пишет, что идеи коммунистов и идеи индивидуалистов (я все время говорю, конечно, об анархистах искренних и сознательных) диаметрально противоположны: так могло бы показаться, если принять литературные и «философские» уклоны некоторых лиц всерьез; но на самом деле речь идет, чаще всего, о словесных недоразумениях.

Анархический индивидуализм потерпел несчастье излагаться часто лицами, которым не доставало какого бы то ни было анархического чувства: буржуазными литераторами, желавшими при посредстве парадоксов привлечь к себе внимание, чтобы иметь возможность с подобием успеха вступить в лоно официальной литературы; полуграмотными и полунеграмотными, которые хотели произвести впечатление; больными, которым чтение непонятной литературы повредило рассудок; наконец, и хуже всего, злодеями более образованными, и чтобы точнее выразиться, смышлеными, чем обычные преступники, чувствовавшими необходимость оправдать свои преступления теорией; в Италии эти последние, главным образом, кончали фашизмом. Буржуазия, правительство и различные политические партии пользовались этими заблуждениями, чтобы клеветать на анархизм и слишком часто им удавалось вредить нам и дискредитировать нас в глазах масс. Недоразумения и личные вопросы срывали дискуссии и часто приводили к расколам даже среди самих анархистов. Но все это не мешает тому, чтобы в своем существе, то есть в своих моральных движущих силах и в своих окончательных целях, анархизм индивидуалистический и коммунистический не были бы одним и тем же или почти одним и тем же.

Я настоятельно рекомендую прочесть книгу Армана «Введение в анархо-индивидуализм»[2], которая скоро выйдет в переводе на итальянский язык, сделанным товарищем Меникони (смотреть в конце этого номера журнала). Это – важная и добросовестная книга, написанная одним из наиболее признанных среди анархо-индивидуалистов писателем, получившим среди них общее одобрение. И что же мы видим? Читая этот труд, спрашиваешь себя почему Арман говорит постоянно об анархическом индивидуализме, как об особой доктрине, в то время, как он только то и делает, что излагает принципы общие для всех анархистов, каково бы ни было их направление. Арман, любящий называть себя аморалистом, на самом деле написал нечто вроде руководства по анархической морали – нисколько не «анархо-индивидуалистической», а анархической вообще. Даже более того, не просто по анархической морали, а по морали общечеловеческой, так как она основана на …

author: Unknown
title: Синтез христианства и анархизма в свете западного богословия
content:
Издательский кооператив «Напильник» предлагает ознакомиться со статьей магистра теологии Александра Питыка, который рассуждает о возможных путях синтеза анархизма и христианского вероучения.

Начав с разбора взглядов на религию, встречавшихся в работах анархистских теоретиков, Питык переходит к рассказу о религиозных деятелях, стоявших на анархических позициях: одном из основателей «Индустриальных рабочих мира» католическом священнике Томасе Дж. Хагерти, католическом священнике Айта Патси, выступившем на стороне Республики во время Гражданской войны в Испании, и английском священнике и анархо-социалисте Грешеме Киркби, боровшемся за ядерное разоружение.

Многим обсуждение христианского анархизма кажется таким же непривычным, как и обсуждение анархического христианства. Тем не менее, политико-религиозное движение христианского анархизма, проявляющееся в различных формах, существует уже давно. Многие движения и личности, как в прошлом, так и в настоящем, придерживаются идеи либерального христианства и решительно заявляют, что анархизм и христианство не обязательно должны быть взаимоисключающими идеологиями. Напротив, если найти определённый подход, они скорее сходятся в содержании, чем расходятся. Жак Эллюль в своей книге «Анархизм и христианство» так и пишет:

«Считается само собой разумеющимся, что анархисты враждебно относятся ко всем религиям […]. Также считается само собой разумеющимся, что набожные христиане ненавидят анархию как источник хаоса и отрицания установленной власти. Именно эти упрощённые и неоспоримые предположения я намерен оспорить».

Попытка определения анархизма сталкивается с проблемой его стереотипного образа. Представление о том, что анархизм — это отсутствие порядка, а не правительства, что он является синонимом хаоса и бессмысленного насилия, сохранилось с викторианского периода и стало известным благодаря таким произведениям, как «Секретный агент» Джозефа Конрада. Конечно, существуют некоторые формы повстанческого анархизма, которые, по-видимому, соответствуют этому стереотипу — достаточно вспомнить деятельность Неформальной Анархической Федерации (Federazione Anarchica Informale, FAI) — но, вопреки распространенному мнению, использование насилия для большинства анархистов есть неприемлемым в виду подавления личности человека, даже если откровенный пацифизм является позицией меньшинства. Далекие от бессмысленности и деструктивности, большинство анархистов считают себя вовлеченными в конструктивный проект, состоящий из новые представления о будущем, политика, которая воплощает это будущее в настоящем, и самостоятельная организация людей.

Известно также, что и большинство христианских церквей традиционно скептически или даже враждебно относятся к социалистическим идеям. Анархистские и социалистические движения часто определяли себя через атеизм и материализм; они считали себя просвещенными и прогрессивными именно благодаря отказу от религии и Церкви. Можно посмотреть на любого классика анархизма конца XIX или начала XX вв. В XIX веке критика Церкви и религии была незаметной, поэтому негативное отношение к религии часто считается «обязательным» для анархиста. Возьмём, к примеру, одного из самых известных анархистов Михаила Бакунина: в книге «Бог и государство» он предупреждает, что религия «отупляет и развращает народы» и что она убивает в людях разум, который «есть главный инструмент освобождения человека». Он приходит к выводу:

«Если Бог существует, человек — раб; но человек может и должен быть свободным: следовательно, Бога не существует».

Эрих Мюзам рассматривает религию и государство как взаимосвязанные инструменты угнетения и пишет в «Освобождении общества от государства», что «Бог и государство […] являются двумя полюсами власти», которые «основаны на отрицании равенства, взаимности и личной ответственности. Пётр Кропоткин — один из важнейших представителей коммунистического анархизма и, безусловно, далёкий от христианского анархизма, — например, признаёт, что христианство было испорчено институционализацией, когда он описывает христианство как «восстание против имперского Рима», которое было подавлено «тем же самым Римом, принявшим его принципы, обычаи и язык» и ставшим, таким образом, «римским правом». Кропоткин пишет, что «в христианском движении, несомненно, были серьёзные анархистские элементы». Однако «анархистское содержание», которое он находил в «истоках» христианства, исчезло для него, когда «это движение постепенно превратилось в церковь»10. Эта аргументация на самом деле …

author: Antisystemic
title: Εξέγερση και αντι-εξέγερση στη Γαλλία
content:
Εξέγερση και αντι-εξέγερση στη Γαλλία


“Η βία αυτή δεν είναι σήμερα αστήρικτη, ασήμαντη, παραβατική. Λέγει ουσιαστικά πράγματα για τη ζωή των πληθυσμών των προαστίων και άρα για ολόκληρη την κοινωνία […] Η βία αυτή είναι υγιής, γιατί εναντιώνεται στη διατήρηση της αδικίας και του κοινωνικού χάους […]”.


Michel Ganozzi, La violence d’une partie de la jenuesse des banlieues est legitime, necessaire et saine


Οι λαϊκές εξεγέρσεις στη Γαλλία τα τελευταία χρόνια τείνουν να μετατραπούν σε μόνιμο γνώρισμα της πολιτικής και κοινωνικής πραγματικότητας. Ο κύκλος της βίας εξαπλώνεται και έλκει σταδιακά όλο και περισσότερα ταξικά υποκείμενα στη συγκρουσιακή ακολουθία του. Κάποιοι σχολίασαν ειρωνικά ότι τα “μπάχαλα” έχουν γίνει το νέο εθνικό σπόρ των “Γάλλων”. Προσπαθούν έτσι να απαξιώσουν τη σημασία των γεγονότων και να εμφυσήσουν την ιδέα μιας, αντεστραμμένης έστω, εθνικής ομοψυχίας. Την ιδέα της ύπαρξης μιας “εθνικής” τάσης, εκεί που στην πραγματικότητα υπάρχει μονάχα σύγκρουση, αντίφαση και φυγόκεντρες δυνάμεις που παλεύουν να αποκτήσουν την αυτονομία τους απ’ το κέντρο της κρατικής εξουσίας. Εκεί δηλαδή όπου υπάρχει μόνο η σταδιακή αποσύνθεση αυτού που αποκαλούμε “έθνος” ως ζώσας κοινωνικής πραγματικότητας.


Άλλοι επιχειρούν να στρέψουν επιδέξια την μία μερίδα των εξεγερμένων ενάντια στην άλλη, καλλιεργώντας το μίσος και τον ταξικό ρατσισμό, που αποτελεί τον κύριο μηχανισμό ιδεολογικής κυριαρχίας του νεοφιλελευθερισμού στις καπιταλιστικές μητροπόλεις. Αυτό για παράδειγμα είναι το περιεχόμενο της στρατηγικής “εθνικής σωτηρίας” που συνιστά την αιχμή του δόρατος της εκλογικής προπαγάνδας της Μαρίν Λεπέν. Η κινητοποίηση της λευκής μάζας των δυσαρεστημένων μικροαστών της ενδοχώρας, οι οποίοι πριν κάποια χρόνια συσπειρώθηκαν στις μεγαλειώδεις αντικυβερνητικές διαδηλώσεις των Κίτρινων Γιλέκων, ως αντίβαρο στις εξεγερσιακές διαθέσεις του προλεταριάτου των πόλεων, καθώς και του πολυεθνικού λούμπεν προλεταριάτου των προαστίων. Αν κάποιο συμπέρασμα προκύπτει αβίαστα από αυτή τη συνεχή κοινωνική αναταραχή στη Γαλλία, είναι η έκδηλη αδυναμία του  νεοφιλελεύθερου κράτους να οικοδομήσει ένα ταξικό μπλοκ που θα του εξασφαλίσει την απαραίτητη κοινωνική αποδοχή και θα εγγυηθεί την μακροημέρευση της κυριαρχίας του.


Το πρόβλημα βέβαια με αυτόν τον επαναλαμβανόμενο κύκλο εξέγερσης και αντιεξέγερσης είναι η αδυναμία που επιδεικνύουν εξίσου οι επιμέρους ανταρσίες κι εκστρατείες κοινωνικής ανυπακοής που συγκροτούνται αυθόρμητα από-τα-κάτω, να συμμαχήσουν σε ένα ενιαίο κίνημα και να καταφέρουν το οριστικό χτύπημα στη νεοφιλελεύθερη χούντα του Μακρόν που παραπαίει. Μπαίνουμε εδώ στον πειρασμό να θυμηθούμε τον ιστορικό Eric Hobsbawm που κάποτε είχε γράψει ότι κατά την πρώτη εποχή της κυριαρχίας της, στα χρόνια που ήταν ακόμη σε εξέλιξη η βιομηχανική επανάσταση, η αστική τάξη είχε μάθει να ζει με τα περιοδικά ξεσπάσματα αγανάκτησης των προλετάριων. Είχε μάθει να τα θεωρεί ως ένα αναγκαίο κακό, όπου όμως “δεν δικακυβευόταν τίποτε […] πέρα από κάποια περιουσιακά στοιχεία που μια πλούσια χώρα μπορούσε κάλλιστα να τα αντικαταστήσει”.i Με άλλα λόγια, οι αστοί έδειχναν μια ανοχή σε αυτές τις παροδικές εξεγερσιακές εκρήξεις των φτωχών, διότι είχαν καταλάβει ότι αυτό ήταν τίμημα που έπρεπε να καταβάλλουν για να εξαγνίσουν την κυριαρχία τους.


Παρ’ όλα αυτά, η απελπισία των ελίτ στη Γαλλία έχει φτάσει σε τέτοιο σημείο ώστε επιστράτευσαν το παραμύθι των “πρακτόρων της Μόσχας” που δήθεν υποδαυλίζουν τις κοινωνικές ταραχές σε ολόκληρη τη χώρα.ii Εδώ τα διδάγματα από το υπερσυντηρητικό εργαστήρι της εμπόλεμης Ουκρανίας είναι κάτι παραπάνω από πολύτιμα. Λίγο μετά τη λαϊκή εξέγερση που ανέβασε στην εξουσία την ακροδεξιά χούντα του Μαϊντάν, ο τότε πρωθυπουργός Γιάτσενιουκ αποκάλεσε τους ανθρώπους που διαμαρτύρονταν στους δρόμους για την απότομη αύξηση στις τιμές του πετρελαίου θέρμανσης και τις περικοπές στις δαπάνες για την υγεία και την παιδεία, “πράκτορες των Ρώσων” και πέμπτη φάλαγγα που ενεργούσε καθ’ υπόδειξη του εχθρού, δηλαδή της Ρωσίας.iii Να λοιπόν που η ρωσοφοβική προπαγάνδα για το μαύρο χέρι του “Μόσκοβου” είναι σαν τη διαφήμιση της κοκα-κόλα. Πάει με όλα. Παρά την προφανή γελοιότητα της, η θεωρία του “ξένου δάκτυλου” που απεργάζεται στο παρασκήνιο την αποσταθεροποίηση των ευρωπαϊκών κοινωνιών είναι το τελευταίο καταφύγιο των ευρωπαϊκών πολιτικών και οικονομικών ελίτ που έχουν απωλέσει τα κοινωνικά στηρίγματα τους και βυθίζονται σε μια κρίση νομιμοποίησης της εξουσίας τους. title: Adam Gary Lewis - Cultures of Anarchist Anti-Colonialism
content:
Author

: Adam Gary Lewis

Title

: Cultures of Anarchist Anti-Colonialism

Subtitle

: Considering Anarchist Prefigurative Possibilities for the Future

Date

: 2026

Notes

: *A text edited for the workshop “Cultures of Anarchist Anti-Colonialism” at the 2026 Hamilton Anarchist Bookfair. **Note: This zine is a heftily edited version of chapters, ideas, and discussions that appear in the 2026 PhD dissertation. I have aimed to condense this work, and dispense with some of the excess academic referencing, language and theory. This is not to suggest that these elements cannot be useful to anarchists, but in the spirit of generating wider forms of discussion I present this initial edited version. The interviews referenced here come from my conversations with 17 anarchists in Southern Ontario, that span a range of cities, communities, and scenes, and encompass a range of complex social identities. In particular, I highlight the words and perspectives of Indigenous participants. Pseudonyms were used to help to maintain some aspect of anonymity. I hope these ideas further some of the ongoing and important conversations on anarchism and anti-colonial politics both here in Southern Ontario, but also further afield as well. My heartfelt and ongoing thanks to all who participated and supported this project over many years, and all the anarchist crews in Southern Ontario. Of course for those with more academic and theory oriented desires I invite you to check out the full dissertation work as well: Adam Gary Lewis. 2026. Cultures of Resistance, Cultures of Potential: Anarchist Value-Practices, Settler Colonialism, and Indigenous Resurgence. PhD Dissertation. York University.

Source

: Retrieved on October 4, 2026 from https://anarchistnews.org/content/cultures-anarchist-anti-colonialism


Someday, somewhere, today’s empires are tomorrow’s ashes.


—Propagandhi


 Commitments to resist settler colonialism and articulate affinities with Indigenous struggles carry potentials for greater forms of anti-colonial politics within anarchism. Such commitments are important points of resistance and action within anarchism, but they are often limited, and require greater expansion in both theory and practice in order to actually generate disruptive forms of anarchist anti-colonialism.


 Anarchists have long named settler colonialism as a key form of oppression and domination that needs to be opposed, alongside more standard anarchist oppositions like the state and capitalism. This is most readily visible in intro to anarchism books, zines, and discussions. Opposition to colonialism is nestled alongside the wide range of opposition to all forms of oppression and domination that characterizes contemporary anarchist politics. In many of these accounts, and especially those that are more theoretical in nature, there is little discussion as to what this sort of anti-colonial opposition might look like. There may be vague nods to support for Indigenous resurgence, or wider histories of complicity with international forms of anti-imperialist struggle, but rarely is there more detailed discussion of how committed form of anti-colonial politics might be enacted in here and now –in specific places at specific times– and with direct reference to the histories and flows of struggle that might disrupt anarchism for the better.


 This results in a tendency to leave colonialism among a wider laundry list of things to be opposed, and lacking in greater qualification and consideration of what this means as practical forms of politics. How, then, are anarchists actually seeking to practically, materially, and intentionally oppose settler colonialism, and support Indigenous resistance and resurgence? This zine attempts to shed light on some of the everyday ways that anarchists in Southern Ontario are engaging this work, and how they are thinking about the relationship between anarchism and anti-colonial politics.


 I consider how spirituality, history, relationships to land and place, and prefigurative imaginations for the future interact with anarchist anti-colonialism. I begin with spirituality as a tension that is perhaps even less discussed amongst anarchists, but which intersects directly with Indigenous resurgence politics, given the centrality of Indigenous cosmologies, grounded normativities, and relationships to land. The limited anarchist approach to spirituality is a stumbling block for anarchist affinities with Indigenous struggles, as well …

author: Kévin Drif
title: The North African family French critics couldn’t see
content:
Since her 2016 debut feature

Raw

, the French auteur Julia Ducournau’s films have been a staple of the body horror genre. Her movies reflect an unapologetic approach to exploring physical transformation and the “monstrous feminine,” an idea coined by feminist film scholar Barbara Creed to underscore the significance of gender and sexuality in the construction of monstrosity. In Ducournau’s films, female characters strive for emancipation from social and familial norms through cannibalism or transhumanism. Yet while

Raw

 and her sophomore feature

Titane

 (2021) center white protagonists,

Alpha

 (2025), her third film, foregrounds the complex dynamic of a family of North African descent, marking a significant departure for the auteur. Curiously, this demographic difference has been almost entirely absent from discussions of the film.

Set between the 1980s and 1990s,

Alpha

 follows its 13-year-old eponymous character; her mother, who is a doctor; and her uncle Amin as they confront a mysterious virus that transforms bodies into blue-veined marmoreal statues that eventually turn to dust. Critics have understandably focused on the epidemic narrative, the stigma attached to the infected, and its evocation of the AIDS crisis, but in doing so, they have overlooked another dimension of the story:

Alpha

 is one of the few contemporary French films to place a family of North African origin at the center of a national trauma.

Ducournau hardly conceals the central family’s roots. She casts actors of Algerian, Moroccan, and Iranian descent and the characters move between French and dialectal Arabic. In one scene that features the most cinematic French postcolonial locality — the

banlieue

 —

Alpha

 joins her extended family to share a couscous meal for an Eid celebration. The problem here is not simply that reviewers omitted demographic details but that their silence in effect reproduces a broader tendency and difficulty within French cultural discourse to see race, acknowledge colonial history, and address postcolonial belonging even when it permeates the screen.

Approaching

Alpha

 through a postcolonial lens opens more interpretative possibilities. Consider the body itself, a central concern of Ducournau’s cinema:

Alpha

’s makeshift tattoo, which symbolically binds her to Amin, evokes traditions of Amazigh inking while also drawing attention to the postcolonial body as a site of inscription, memory, and belonging. The gesture turns the body into a site where cultural memory can persist without being explicitly articulated;

Alpha

’s body becomes a postcolonial archive — a place where histories and affiliations that remain largely unspoken can nonetheless be inscribed, carried, and transmitted. Furthermore, the film’s concern with body regulation recalls the colonial politics of visibility explored by Frantz Fanon in his writings on French Algeria, where the control of bodies, especially female bodies through the practice of unveiling, functioned as a mechanism of domination.

Alpha

’s epidemic narrative also takes on new meanings when viewed through the history of North African migration. The AIDS crisis in France disproportionally affected marginalized communities. According to

a 1999 study

 led by the French Institut de veille sanitaire, or Institute of Health Surveillance, between 1978 and 1998, immigrant populations accounted for 14 percent of AIDS cases in France, when they only represented 6 percent of the adult population at the time. Drug users of North African origin infected through contaminated needles, much like Amin, represented the main mode of contamination for heterosexual men and accounted for 45 percent of North African immigrant cases. Still, they remain largely absent from narratives of the epidemic. This omission and silence of the infected is the result of the religious taboo attached to the disease and the larger structural disinterest in these populations. Ducournau’s attention to Amin gestures towards histories that have largely escaped commemoration.

Alpha

’s imagery of suffocation, disease, and social abandonment invites reflection of the lives and afterlives of colonial violence beyond France. The calcification of infected bodies recalls forms of historical petrification through which colonial atrocities are rendered distant, abstract, and invisible within French national memory. The structural and social segregation imposed on the sick in the film, illustrated in the …

author: Joshua W.J. Brown
title: The New Native Needs a Theory of Obligation, Not a Blood Test
content:
The New Native should not become the old Native with a better genealogy.


That is the danger I keep hearing underneath the question

The Elephant

 has been asking this year. The “New Native” in this series is not a newly discovered ethnic group. It is a political figure emerging from a Kenyan public that has begun to act as though citizenship might mean more than being represented upward by an ethnic kingpin, disciplined by a church, managed by a civil servant, or frightened back into the inherited categories of the colonial state.


Akal Mohan sees the consolidation of a Kenyan identity beyond old orders of tribe, clan and denomination. Wangui Kimari traces the state’s fear of the “detribalized native”, then and now: the urban African who does not stay where authority says identity belongs. Joe Kobuthi reads the 2024 rupture through theology and the failure of a state that has demanded something close to sacred obedience. Across the series, the New Native becomes legible precisely when older intermediaries stop being able to explain the citizen to himself.


But once “native” is liberated from colonial administration, a second problem arrives. What is it going to mean?


If native means only ancestry, the term can become a blood test. If it means only citizenship, it can become historical amnesia. Neither answer is adequate for a country in which people can be equal citizens while communities still possess radically unequal historical relationships to land, dispossession, state violence, migration and political power.


Kenya’s own constitution already knows this, even when political language forgets.


One country, more than one kind of right


Chapter Three of the constitution does not grade citizenship by antiquity. A Kenyan citizen is a citizen. Citizenship may be acquired by birth or registration, and citizens possess the rights, privileges and benefits of that status. The constitution does not say that a person becomes more Kenyan because his ancestors arrived first, or less Kenyan because a grandparent crossed a border.


Then Chapter Five does something equally important: it refuses to pretend that equal citizenship has dissolved collective history. Article 63 recognizes community land, including ancestral lands and lands traditionally occupied by hunter-gatherer communities. The Community Land Act recognizes customary rights and gives them legal force. Article 56 requires affirmative measures for minorities and marginalized groups.


These provisions are not an embarrassing inconsistency in the constitutional order. They are a clue.


Equal citizenship and historically specific rights can coexist because they answer different questions. Citizenship asks: who belongs to the political community, and on what civic terms? Ancestral land rights ask: what relationship does a particular community possess to a particular place, and what happened to that relationship? A remedy for dispossession is not a superior passport. A passport is not a land restitution programme.


Conflate those categories and the state gets two convenient escapes. It can tell a dispossessed community that everyone is equal now, therefore the old theft no longer requires a specific remedy. Or it can tell citizens descended from later-arriving populations that they may live under the law but can never fully belong because history placed their ancestors in the wrong column.


Both moves turn time into an alibi.


The Ogiek case is about more than recognition


The Ogiek litigation makes the first danger impossible to romanticize away.


In 2017, the African Court on Human and Peoples’ Rights found Kenya responsible for violations involving Ogiek land, property, natural resources, culture and development. In 2022, the Court ordered reparations, including compensation and measures to secure Ogiek ancestral land rights. In December 2025, after years of implementation failure, the Court found Kenya had still not made the ordered compensation payments, had not completed the identification, delimitation, demarcation and collective titling of Ogiek ancestral land, and had not begun the consultations required to resolve concessions and leases affecting that land.


That matters to the New Native argument because it shows why a purely civic vocabulary is insufficient. “We are all Kenyans” cannot do the work of a title, a payment, a boundary, a consultation, or the restoration of a legal relationship to ancestral land.


Universal equality is not the …

author: Nada Elia
title: Women and Youth Are at the Forefront of the Struggle for Palestinian Liberation
content:
They follow in the footsteps of Palestinian women and children who have resisted colonialism in the past century.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

I grew up in a household of women and children that, as my sisters and I matured, eventually became a household of only women. My father was frequently gone on long overseas business trips before his untimely death when I was seven. I often wonder if this is the reason the expression “women and children” strikes me as essentially flawed: It suggests that women and children are the more vulnerable members of society, rather than its resilient survivors. It infantilizes women by grouping them with children, rather than adult men.

In the context of a national struggle, it strips women of agency, as if such agency can only manifest through armed revolt. In a military context, the expression “women and children” — or “womenandchildren,” to use the term coined by antimilitary feminist scholar Cynthia Enloe — presumes that women and children never take up arms or participate in resistance, even as we see such actions occurring in numerous struggles around the world. And in listing casualties, it implies that men’s deaths and injuries are less tragic, less mournable.

In the case of Palestine, women and youth have led, and continue to lead, some of the most transformative efforts and initiatives in our people’s quest for justice — that is, our resistance first to imperialism, then to settler colonialism and apartheid. They have not been spared Israel’s violence, just for being women, or children, and many have been and remain at the forefront of popular resistance to Zionism’s ultimate aim of eliminating all Palestinians. While this may have become more obvious during Israel’s accelerated genocidal assault on Gaza following Hamas’s October 7, 2023, attacks, it had always been clear to anyone not deliberately looking away.

From a number of uprisings over the past century in Palestine, it is obvious that youth, “the children,” are not just among the leaders; they are the more effective, more transformational leaders. Unfettered by traditions and social norms they do not relate to, they engage in novel forms of organizing, seeking the complete abolition of oppressive systems, rather than their reversal. And women, in their capacity as autonomous adults, rather than merely as wives and mothers, have consistently resisted both the imperial ideology targeting their country, and the military assaults that accompanied it. They did so while providing men, as well as the youth and children, the moral, emotional, and practical support the Palestinian people need in order to persist. This was perhaps most evident on a global scale during the 1987–93 Intifada, when women organized most of the popular committees tending to the educational, nutritional, and health needs of Palestinians resisting Israel’s clampdown, as youth took to the streets daily to express their rejection of Israel’s decades-long oppressive rule. These defenseless children hurled rocks at armored tanks, fully aware of the hefty price they would pay for their defiant act, because they knew that risking limb and life is preferable to living without freedom and dignity.

Women’s and children’s agency is enacted daily in the courage of girls such as Janna Jihad, who was dubbed “the world’s youngest journalist” when she started documenting Israel’s crimes at a mere seven years of age. Jihad started recording Israel’s attacks using her mother’s cell phone, posting her recordings far and wide on social media. She has repeatedly said that her camera is her weapon of choice. Jihad is the cousin of Ahed Tamimi, the “lioness” who has confronted heavily armed Israeli soldiers determined to take over her village lands since she was a toddler. Israel imprisoned Tamimi for eight months when she was sixteen; she used the time behind bars to read up on international law, later enrolling in college planning to go to law school, so as to hold Israel accountable for its violations. “I am a freedom fighter. So I will not be the victim,” she told journalists upon her release.

Palestinian children’s agency was also clear in the 2022 uprising of rebellious youth standing up to Israel’s might. author: Yohannes Woldemariam
title: Imperial Nostalgia: History, Sovereignty, and the Unfinished Work of Decolonization in the Horn of Africa
content:
History in the Horn of Africa is rarely allowed to remain history. An ancient civilization becomes evidence of modern sovereignty. A medieval dynasty becomes proof of national continuity. Territory incorporated during one political era is later remembered as though it had always belonged to the state that governed it.


This habit has become especially visible as the Red Sea has returned to Ethiopian political discourse. Ethiopia is landlocked and has obvious economic reasons to seek dependable maritime trade. But there is a fundamental difference between negotiating the use of a port and claiming that a neighboring country possesses territory that properly belongs to Ethiopia. That distinction disappears when Assab is described as a “lost Ethiopian port.”


Ethiopia did not lose a sovereign port in 1993. Eritrea recovered sovereignty over territory that had been incorporated into Ethiopia after the violation and eventual termination of an internationally established federal arrangement. To describe this as Ethiopia “losing the sea” begins the story at the moment of Ethiopian possession and ignores how that possession came about.


This is what I mean by imperial nostalgia.


Imperial nostalgia is not merely admiration for emperors or attachment to an earlier age. It is a way of remembering political space. Territory once incorporated into an empire is remembered not simply as territory once governed, but as territory that naturally belonged there. Incorporation becomes ownership, ownership becomes entitlement, and independence can then be remembered as national loss.


Christopher Clapham’s notion of an Ethiopian “manifest destiny” is useful at the margins of this argument, although I invoke him cautiously and not to validate Ethiopian historical claims. The phrase captures a mentality in which expansion can stop looking like expansion when incorporation is presented as the fulfillment of history. Manifest destiny looks forward. Imperial nostalgia looks backward and imagines that a geography produced through expansion was the natural order all along.


The deeper problem is the projection of modern states backward into political worlds that did not organize themselves according to contemporary borders. Aksum is an obvious example. Its political and commercial world crossed territories that are now divided between Eritrea and Ethiopia and formed part of a much larger Red Sea system.

UNESCO’s account of Aksum

 describes an ancient civilization. It does not describe a modern territorial state possessing a contemporary claim to the Red Sea.


Calling Aksum simply “ancient Ethiopia” imports the political geography of today into antiquity. Calling it “ancient Eritrea” would make the same mistake. Civilizations, languages, religions, trading networks, and archaeological landscapes regularly cross the boundaries of modern states. Shared history does not create shared sovereignty.


I explored this problem more fully in

There Is No Timeless Eritrea or Ethiopia

. The point is not to diminish the history of either country. It is to stop asking ancient civilizations to perform the work of modern territorial law. Aksum should be studied as Aksum rather than recruited into a contemporary argument over Assab.


Richard Reid examined this problem directly in

The Trans-Mereb Experience: Perceptions of the Historical Relationship between Eritrea and Ethiopia

. Reid is useful because he is skeptical of efforts on either side to recruit antiquity into modern nationalism. The same history can be arranged to prove a supposedly eternal Ethiopia or, in the opposite direction, an Eritrea with no meaningful historical relationship to communities south of the Mereb. Neither approach is good history.


Even the word Ethiopia should make us cautious. The Greek term

Aithiopia

 did not refer neatly to the bounded territorial state called Ethiopia today. Recognizing this does not make modern Ethiopia less legitimate. It simply acknowledges that political names, communities, and territorial states change over time.


Eritrea should be approached in exactly the same way. Fred Halliday, writing in 1971 while the Eritrean war was still underway, acknowledged in

“The Fighting in Eritrea”

 that Eritrea in its modern territorial form had been defined under European colonialism. That fact does not weaken Eritrean sovereignty. It places Eritrea within the history of modern Africa.


Most African states inherited territorial forms created or …

Le 24 septembre 1853, un colon Français pose le pied à Balade, un village sur une île du Pacifique Sud, la Kanaky. Il prend possession de l'île au nom de la France. Cette date symbolise aujourd'hui le jour de la prise de possession et le début du colonialisme en Kanaky.


Depuis 1853, les

kanak

 ont été relégués géographiquement, économiquement et politiquement dans leur propre pays. Ils ont été dépossédés de leurs terres, ce qui revient pour eux à la perte de leur identité. Ils ont vu aussi leurs moyens de subsistance s'amoindrir et leurs sites sacrés confisqués.


De 1888 à 1946, ils furent confinés dans des réserves et régis par le Code de l'indigénat qui les maintenait en dehors du droit commun.


Les Kanak ont toujours manifesté leur opposition à cette colonisation, mais les incessants soulèvements furent tous réprimés brutalement par l'administration française.


Parmi les plus mémorables résistances, il y a le soulèvement de 1878 conduits par Ataï et d'autres chefs kanak visant la prise de la capitale, Nouméa,

Le 24 septembre est devenu une date anniversaire, symbolisant la prise de possession du pays par la France, marquant le début de la colonisation. C'est une journée de deuil pour le peuple kanak.

author: Paul Tiyambe Zeleza
title: The Historiographical Legacy of B.A. Ogot and His Generation
content:
Good evening, colleagues, and the Governor of Kisumu County, Professor Anyang Nyong’o! It is truly a pleasure for me to join you in this commemoration of the towering historian, scholar, and public intellectual, Bethwell Alan Ogot. I believe I speak on behalf of all of us in extending our deep gratitude to the Council for the Development of Social Science Research in Africa (CODESRIA) and the Department of History at Kenyatta University for organizing this important conference. Personally, my appreciation extends to that rarity of experiences, the opportunity to meet several of my former students at Kenyatta University between 1984 and 1989 who have become distinguished academics and administrators. It’s a befitting tribute to our intellectual father, grandfather, quickly becoming a great-grandfather, who was raised and spent his last years and is buried in nearby Yala, that this conference is being held in his home city of Kisumu, under the transformative leadership of one of Kenya’s leading scholars and public intellectuals, Governor Peter Anyang Nyong’o.


Introduction


Let me begin by noting that I last visited Kisumu in January 2019 to join Professor Ogot as he celebrated his 90th birthday. I first visited this city nearly forty years earlier, in 1980, when I was doing research for my doctoral dissertation on Kenyan economic and labor history, and spent time at this venue, the Tom Mboya Labor College. Professor Ogot had a lot to do with my interest in Kenyan history. My engagement with him goes back to 1976 when he served as external examiner at the University of Malawi.


Years later, he would proudly tell audiences at events where both of us were present that I owed my degree with distinction to him! In our classes on East African history, we had read Ogot’s books, and it was an indescribable honor and privilege to meet him in person. I was deeply touched and humbled when he asked to meet the student who had received the distinction, and he prevailed upon the department to bring me to the cottage along Lake Malawi, where the department took him to show their gratitude for bestowing the department with the distinction of his presence. .


That was the beginning of a lifelong mentoring and intellectual relationship that changed the trajectory of my personal and professional life, on which I will say more later.


When Professor Ogot passed away in January 2025, there was an avalanche of tributes in the popular and academic media celebrating his life and immense scholarly contributions. It is befitting that we are gathered here to remember and celebrate him as a towering historian and intellectual polymath.


Ogot belongs to an exceptional generation of the pioneering architects of the African academy in its multifaceted epistemic and institutional dimensions. These were extraordinary individuals, inspired by the fierce historical and humanistic urgency and imperatives of African nationalism: decolonization, nation-building, regional integration, development, and democracy. They were driven by the audacity, passion, and commitment to remaking the production, dissemination, and consumption of knowledge in, and for, Africa and the world.


They were scholar-activists who transformed existing disciplines and founded new ones, who built interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary paradigms, perspectives and practices, who believed in the power of education as a public good and engine of development, who relished their role as rigorous academics and public intellectuals, who jealously guarded academic freedom and the intelligentsia as the conscience of their new nation-states.


Their lives were large, complex, and multilayered. The trajectory of Ogot’s career is quite emblematic of his peers, born between the third and fourth decades of the twentieth century in the immediate aftermath of the formation of the colonial conquest state, whose ideologues deluded themselves would last for centuries, if not millennia, only to collapse spectacularly as Ogot and his peers matured into adulthood. I would like to explore, rather briefly given the limitations of time, five aspects of Professor Ogot’s remarkable life and legacy: Ogot the man, the historian, the institution builder, the public figure, and the mentor. Let me add that today we’ve heard much about many of these themes. My excuse for revisiting them is that I came a long way, and I have to justify my ticket!


Ogot the Man


Biographical reflections and commemorations …

author: Kodao Productions
title: Chinese teachers leaving in droves: Victims of inter-imperialist propaganda?
content:
About 150 Chinese teachers have begun leaving the Philippines in batches since last week, worried about their safety in a country that has had Chinese schools that are as old as 127 years.


The Chinese Embassy in Manila and the Federation of Filipino-Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry Inc. (FFCCCII) on Saturday said the foreign teachers were asked by their families to leave the Philippines for their safety.


The exodus came after a purported US security expert raised questions about the Chinese teachers’ true intentions in the country.


Ray Powell, founder and director of SeaLight, an initiative connected with Stanford University’s Gordian Knot Center for National Security Innovation, wrote last July that China’s Jinan University was involved in training Chinese-language teachers for schools in the Philippines.


Powell alleged their deployment to the Philippines had been directed by the Chinese Communist Party.


Philippine defense secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. echoed Powell’s warning, urging public vigilance regarding China-linked cultural and educational exchange programs and alleging that Jinan University “spreads fake news” by claiming that the Philippine northernmost province of Batanes belongs to China.


Teodoro also warned that foreign-linked academic and educational exchanges could be used as a front to “gain a foothold into the Philippines in order for them to scope for information.” “[I]t is really part of the doctrine of China. One of the main efforts of China is the United Front Work,” Teodoro said.


Why are there Chinese teachers in the Philippines?


There are about 150 Chinese schools throughout the country that caters to the substantial number of ethnically Chinese Philippine residents. China-Philippine relations go as far back as the 9

th

 century with many waves of Chinese migrations to the Southeast Asian country.


The Chinese schools, known mainly for having the best math students, teach Mandarin as preservation of their ethnic identity.


Filipino-Chinese teacher and social media personality Thunderson Tan said Chinese schools import Mandarin teachers because they remain the best mentors of the language.


“Sure, many Filipino-Chinese could speak Mandarin. But we are mostly Cantonese speakers. Our Mandarin is already stained by Cantonese and the various Filipino languages,” Tan explained.


Inter-imperialist propaganda victims


Immaculate Conception Academy in San Juan City and Jubilee Christian Academy in Quezon City were two of the Chinese schools that would be affected by the exodus.


“The parents were concerned about the articles written by Ray Powell attacking Chinese-language schools in the Philippines,” FFCCCII said.


The organization said the Chinese Embassy and relevant Chinese authorities were formally notified of the decision to bring them home before the schools were informed. FFCCCII said the Chinese Embassy had approved the recall.


The Chinese Embassy meanwhile denounced the “malicious smear campaigns” against Chinese language education.


“We firmly reject the baseless accusations and strongly denounce the malicious smear campaigns targeting educational and people-to-people exchanges between China and the Philippines, including Chinese-language education in the Philippines,” embassy spokesperson Ji Lingpeng said.


Ji said educational and people-to-people exchanges had long contributed to relations and mutual understanding between the Philippines and China.


“We believe those malicious rhetoric and actions against China-Philippines people-to-people exchanges by certain individuals have no place in the Philippines and time-honored friendship between the Chinese and Filipino peoples will continue to stand,” he said.


The latest incident adds more tension to the already frayed China-Philippine relations under the pro-US Ferdinand Marcos Jr. government anchored on the Chinese nine-dash line claim of about 90 percent of the South China Sea, including huge swaths of the Philippine exclusive economic zone in the area.


The teachers began returning home on October 1. #

(Raymund B. Villanueva)

author: Rodrigo Acuña
title: Cubans See Hope in Reforms But Worry Over How the US May Thwart Them
content:
Residents of Havana discuss the obstacles facing the revival of the Cuban economy amid the US fuel blockade.

Residents of Havana discuss the obstacles facing the revival of the Cuban economy amid the US fuel blockade.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Last month, Cuban Prime Minister Manuel Marrero Cruz declared that 158 new economic and social measures, out of an original package of 176 approved in July by the Cuba’s National Assembly, were being implemented and backed by 197 legal decrees. The measures include allowing private business to import medicines and other goods, loosening restrictions on private tourism, and authorising privately owned banks — under Central Bank supervision — on a regulatory basis equivalent to state banks. Adding to these measures, the National Assembly for the first time permitted foreign capital to invest directly in Cuban private businesses instead of having to operate exclusively through state-controlled structures. Private companies also will no longer be restricted to a maximum of 100 employees.

According to Daniel Torralbas, a London-based Cuban economist, the National Assembly’s new measures are “the most profound economic reform programme … since the 1959 revolution.” Headed by Fidel Castro, the government in Havana between the mid and late 1960s nationalized a vast array of U.S.-owned businesses that controlled major shares in key industries such as public utilities, mining, railways and infrastructure, and land and agriculture.

Mauricio Alonso, a 68-year-old former nuclear engineer who lives in Havana and now runs an Airbnb rental, is embracing the government’s new economic measures.

“On a personal level this is going to benefit me,” says Alonso, “because it’s going to allow, for example, me — since I’m self-employed — to partner with foreigners, to team up, to be part of a larger organization, and to carry out actions with my lodging business, and so on.” Working with travel agencies, in Alonso’s view, will now be made easier with the lifting of restrictions. “If I qualify, if I get accredited as such,” says Alonso, “I can carry out the work of a tour guide without any kind of problem.”

During the 1980s, Alonso worked at the Central Electronuclear de Juraguá, near the city of Cienfuegos, which was being built with the aid of the Soviet Union to become Cuba’s first nuclear power station. Alonso says that, “when the Soviet Union collapsed in late 1991, work on the plant came to a halt in 1992.” Although Alonso continued working in the nuclear sector until 1995, he “realized that the project couldn’t go on — due in part to [the] intense pressure from the U.S. government.” At that point, he decided to “switch to the private sector and start renting out rooms” after inheriting a large apartment from his mother.

Had Cuba’s nuclear power station become operational, it is doubtful the island would be facing its current energy crisis.

Despite a small recovery between 2021 and 2022, after Cuba’s GDP in 2020 contracted by 10.9 percent as COVID-19 effectively shut down international tourism, the island’s economic crisis has been worsened by the Trump administration’s fuel embargo. When U.S. President Donald Trump began to take action against Venezuela’s oil shipments to Cuba in 2025, which approximated 26,500 barrels per day, Cubans saw a serious reduction of fuel on the island. On January 29, the Trump administration formalized the oil sanctions on Cuba by signing Executive Order 14380, which did not simply add another sanction on the island, but instead, created a mechanism to penalize third countries that supply oil to Cuba. Should a country provide crude oil or petroleum products, then the United States government can impose further tariffs on that country’s goods entering the U.S.

For Amalia Díaz Pérez, a 21-years old recent graduate in philosophy from the University of Havana, the Trump administration’s oil embargo disrupted her final year of study. Speaking to Truthout, she said:

The total blockade of fuel imports — with only one ship arriving in nine months — caused public transportation to disappear and reduced daily electricity availability to a minimum. Consequently, my study conditions and most of my daily recreational activities were affected. Compounding this situation, household chores became increasingly difficult due to the strain of the nationwide fuel shortage placed on water and …

title: Flávio Bolsonaro y Lula van a segunda vuelta en Brasil
content:
Con casi el 100% de las mesas escrutadas, Flávio Bolsonaro se impone con el 47,05% de los votos y suma en total 56.082.216 votos. Este resultado no le alcanza para ganar la presidencias, por lo que se disputará una segunda vuelta con el actual presidente Lula Da Silva que consiguió 45,14% de los votos, que equivalen a 53.799.870. Las elecciones se dan en un contexto de extrema polarización, incertidumbre e injerencia del imperialismo yanqui. El resultado de las elecciones brasileñas tiene un especial peso en la balanza de las fuerzas políticas en Latino América. Tanto por el tamaño de la economía de Brasil como por la polarización entre el actual presidente Lula y el hijo de Bolsonaro subordinado al alineamiento del continente a Trump, el Escudo de las Américas y su doctrina de seguridad Donroe.

Por La Izquierda Diario.


Distintos analistas sostienen que el voto indeciso fue el que sorprendió en esta primera vuelta al volcarse a favor de Flavio Bolsonaro, que quedó dos puntos arriba de Lula. Este resultado refleja lo que las encuestas captaron días antes, una mejora de Bolsonaro quien capitalizó el voto útil de otras fuerzas conservadoras.


La presión del imperialismo parece haber surtido efecto como en la Argentina en las elecciones intermedias de 2027. Allí con el respaldo de dinero y la amenaza de retirar el apoyo y hundir las finanzas del Estado, de la mano del Secretario del Tesoro yanqui Scott Bessent. En Brasil, la amenaza se materializó con el cierre de consulados y la embajada por una supuesta cuestión de seguridad que la Policía Federal investigó y descartó. Además, está el antecedente de Venezuela y todas las acciones de presión con aranceles, y otras presiones diplomáticas sobre el gobierno de Lula.


Por otro lado, en todos estos años de gobierno petista no se cambió la estructura de la nación dependiente del imperialismo, así como tampoco se resolvieron las diferencias sociales, el racismo ni la concentración de tierras en manos de los latifundistas. Los salarios bajos y las familias endeudadas demuestran eso. No es solo el grave tema de las apuestas on line, son los ingresos de las familias, cada vez peores.

author: Céli Pinto
title: The Most Important Election in Brazilian History
content:
We usually say that in general elections, we’re choosing a president, governors and lawmakers for the next four years. That much seems obvious. But in this election, with the first round on October 4 and the runoff on October 25, we’re not just choosing who governs. We’re choosing the country’s future for decades to come.

This isn’t a choice between candidate A and candidate B. It’s a choice between a sharp lurch toward colonized totalitarianism and the survival of democracy. Every voter needs to have this clearly in mind. We are responsible for this country’s future. Future generations will blame us, and rightly so, if we fail and Brazil is handed over to colonizer vultures.

Voters, whether or not they are politically active, whether they are young, middle-aged or elderly, have plenty of issues with the current government. It’s true the government could have done more, particularly if it didn’t have a Congress dedicated almost exclusively to serving its own interests. Even so, the government accomplished a great deal. It did this not despite Congress, but because Congress exists. That made it possible to negotiate with lawmakers and to pressure them through the press and social media.

We can only keep doing that if we also fight to change how Congress does politics. Everyone who wants to speak must be free to speak. Everyone must be free to fight politically. Institutions must be able to investigate, and to be investigated in turn. That means guaranteeing elections that are completely free and fair. None of this is possible unless we secure the survival of democracy, problems and all.

Voters, activists, young, middle-aged and elderly people all have good reason to be frustrated with the Supreme Court. There is a glaring indecency in the conduct of this group of mostly older men, all of them white. As for the court’s only woman, who is conservative, there hasn’t been a single incident involving her conduct as a public official.

But we live in a democracy. The only reason we weren’t overrun by the attempt to sabotage the 2022 election, and later by the attempt to pardon the military officers and their allies behind a heavily armed coup, is that the Superior Electoral Court and the Supreme Court exist. And the only reason we even know what’s happening now is that we live in a democracy, where everything can come to light.

The Trump administration is deepening its imperialist policy to alarming levels, even for those of us who have always understood the United States’ colonial ethos. This current phase of capitalism has abandoned even its weak pretense of democratic values. It now advances unbridled on the autonomy and sovereignty of countries in the Global South, especially in Latin America.

When President Lula said, in his address at the opening session of the U.N. General Assembly, that “Brazil doesn’t fit in anyone’s backyard,” he knew exactly what he was saying. Like many of us, he knows that a plot against Brazilian sovereignty is being assembled, led by the Bolsonaro family and its most obvious financial backers. Everyone involved would be pardoned if the worst were to happen, and the country would be driven into misery and excess.

This is a moment of absolute gravity. Circumstances like these have to be confronted directly, without half measures. If Lula wins the election, paradise won’t arrive overnight. Many people will keep facing frustrations. But I can assure you of this: no one will take the food out of people’s mouths, or the roof from over their heads, their universal right to public health through the Unified Public Health System (Brazil’s Sistema Único de Saúde, or SUS), or free medications, or the economic and racial quotas in education and public sector hiring.

If Lula wins, Brazil won’t magically become a country free of violence. Men won’t stop killing women in the senseless way they do today. But you can be certain that fewer poor, Black youth will die, and that police will be held accountable more often for mass killings.

The government will keep fighting organized crime, as it does now, by cutting off criminal factions’ money and arresting their leaders, including the politicians among them. There won’t be spectacular massacres like the one carried out by a police force whose state governor stands accused of colluding with the commanders responsible for the 122 deaths in October 2025 in Rio de Janeiro’s Complexo do Alemão favela.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Claudio Katz: “Hay que construir la izquierda para derrotar a Milei”
content:
Tras la repercusión de la Marcha de la Bronca, Claudio Katz analizó el rol de la izquierda en la coyuntura actual, donde juegan cada vez más fuerte dos variables: el retroceso de Milei y un potencial estallido económico.


Las incógnitas sobre el peronismo, la apuesta del establishment a perpetuar el esquema de ajuste, explotación laboral y saqueo del país que logró establecer durante la actual gestión, la impunidad de la Corte Suprema y la agresividad del imperialismo estadounidense en la región son datos ineludibles del escenario presente ante los cuales la izquierda deberá plantearse nuevas tácticas y compromisos, consideró Katz, si quiere llegar al gobierno y disputar el poder.


Indymedia: – ¿Cómo ves el papel de la izquierda luego de la Marcha de la Bronca?


Claudio Katz:

 – Está cumpliendo un papel muy positivo ante todo en la acción callejera. La marcha fue un éxito

 por la

 concurrencia y el impacto de un acto político, que traspasó la resistencia social y democrática a los atropellos de Milei. Contrastó frontalmente con la capitulación de la CGT que deja pasar el ajuste.


La movilización alcanzó el nivel más alto de una convocatoria de

la izquierda. Superó lo conseguido con la “Plaza del No” en los años 90 y con las grandes concentraciones que en el pasado articulaba el

PC. Exhibió un nivel de politización muy superior a las marchas piqueteras e ilustró nuevamente cómo gravita la izquierda en las coyunturas de inmovilidad del peronismo.


Esa indefinición del justicialismo se vio por ejemplo cuando ganó Alfonsín, durante el neoliberalismo de Menem o en la época de Alianza. Actualmente, vuelve a aflorar por momentos y por eso hubo cierta presencia de militantes o simpatizantes del peronismo en la marcha. Igualmente te diría que el dato más significativo fue la centralidad de Myriam

Bregman. La movilización consolidó su protagonismo y la consiguiente incidencia de la izquierda en las próximas elecciones.


Indymedia: –

Pero cuál es la proyección electoral efectiva de Myriam, porque las encuestas resaltan una imagen muy positiva sin equivalencia en la intención de voto…


Claudio Katz: – Hay infinitas especulaciones sobre esa relación y no tiene mucho sentido obsesionarse con el tema, cuando falta más de un año para la elección. El número de votos que lograría el FIT-U depende de escenarios muy

abiertos con dos variables centrales: el retroceso de Milei y un potencial estallido económico, que podría repetir lo ocurrido tantas veces en la Argentina.


Foto:

Nicolas Solo ((i))


Nadie sabe si el gobierno podrá sostener el tipo de cambio hasta el 2027. La recesión, la pobreza y el endeudamiento podrían desencadenar el mismo tipo de rebelión que sepultó a De la Rúa o la protesta masiva que derrotó a Macri. No cabe duda que la izquierda estará en la primera línea de ese eventual estallido.


Pero en cualquier caso su crecimiento dependerá de lo que suceda con el peronismo y en ese campo hay varios cursos posibles de división o cohesión y de amoldamiento conservador o resurgimiento progresista.


Por el momento se verifica una gran fractura en el justicialismo, entre corrientes de adaptación y crítica al modelo que la clase dominante apuntala con Milei. En general predomina la postura de no decir nada a la espera de lo que más conviene. Pero mientras tanto, un fascista como Cúneo participa del espacio de Kicillof, que a su vez emite mensajes de adaptación tipo Alberto Fernández y elude comentarios básicos de denuncia del genocidio de Palestina. Pero lo que haría como presidente es un misterio. Conviene recordar que nadie imaginaba el giro progresista de Néstor y Cristina antes del 2001 y sería un error ignorar la recomposición que logró el peronismo al calor de la gestión kirchnerista.


Indymedia: –

 ¿Por qué importa ese dato?


Claudio Katz: – Porque conforma el escenario en el que actúa la izquierda. Desconociendo ese hecho es muy difícil desenvolver estrategias para derrotar a Milei, revertir el ajuste y reconquistar los derechos populares. Ese camino transita por llegar al gobierno y disputar el poder, mediante frentes comunes y acuerdos de lucha con los sectores dispuestos a reconstruir el país, apostando a un gobierno que en sus primeros días de gestión revierta de un plumazo todo lo hecho por Milei.


Foto:

Nicolas Solo ((i))

title: Antiimperialistische Aktionswoche 7. - 11. Oktober
content:

title: Elecciones Brasil 2026, una batalla contra el imperialismo
content:
Las amplias elecciones que el próximo 4 de octubre tendrán lugar en Brasil, en las que se elegirán presidente, gobernadores y legisladores, son de importancia estratégica para nuestra Abya Yala y para todo el globo terráqueo. Brasil es el 5to país más extenso, está entre las 10 economías más grandes y demográficamente ocupa el séptimo lugar en el mundo.


Por otra parte, el Brasil de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, del Partido de los Trabajadores (PT), forma parte de los BRICS, quienes vienen abogando por un orden mundial más justo y equilibrado; su principal socio comercial es China, con una tendencia al crecimiento en su intercambio comercial; ha hecho fuertes críticas al ente sionista que, con la ayuda de los EE. UU., está ejecutando un genocidio contra el pueblo palestino. Todo lo anterior lo convierte en el principal objetivo del presidente Trump en el hemisferio. Ya le ha impuesto a las importaciones de EE. UU. desde Brasil, entre el 12.5 % y el 50 % de aranceles, lo que ha hecho descender las exportaciones brasileñas hacia los EE. UU. a sus niveles más bajos desde 1997, lo que ha afectado negativamente su economía, expresado esto, en el bajo crecimiento de su PIB durante 2026.


Trump y su secretario de Estado, Marco Rubio, se han estado pronunciando a favor de la candidatura de Flavio Bolsonaro y criticado ferozmente el juicio que se le siguió a Jair Bolsonaro, por el intento del golpe de Estado, llegando al extremo de tomar medidas coercitivas unilaterales contra el juez que llevó la causa.


La intromisión de los EE. UU. en los asuntos internos de otros países es bien conocida. En Nuestra América han derrocado decenas de gobiernos e instalado dictaduras militares, han desestabilizado gobiernos legítimos, han bloqueado e impuesto medidas ilegales e inhumanas contra pueblos enteros y han llegado a violar la soberanía de varios países con agresiones militares directas: México, Cuba, Haití, Nicaragua, República Dominicana, Panamá, Granada y Venezuela son ejemplo de ello. Han manipulado elecciones abiertamente, teniendo los últimos 18 meses los ejemplos de Honduras, Ecuador, Colombia y Perú, donde, de manera grotesca y descarada, han impulsado candidatos, amenazado a la población con bloquear el envío de remesas, amedrentado a los gobiernos y empresarios con elevar aranceles y han utilizado sus mecanismos de manipulación y desinformación contra amplios sectores de la población, utilizando técnicas como la Big Data, los algoritmos de las redes sociales y buscadores y la última tendencia que es el uso de la inteligencia artificial como una más de estas nefastas herramientas.


La injerencia de EE. UU. en los asuntos internos de decenas de países, ha quedado registrado en diversos libros, como los de William Blum (2005) y (2006), Guenther Roppel (2005) y Luis Suárez Salazar (2006) entre otros. En el caso brasileño ya en 1960 los militares, por presión de la embajada yanqui, exigieron y lograron la salida del presidente Quadros, quien pocos meses antes de ser destituido había otorgado la máxima condecoración, para autoridades extranjeras, al Che Guevara. En 1964 le darían un golpe de Estado al presidente Joao Goulart, poco después de anunciar la expropiación y redistribución de tierras privadas y la nacionalización de refinerías de petróleo y lograrían la destitución de la presidente Dilma Rousseffa del PT, a través de un impeachment, en 2016.


Por otra parte, el candidato con mayores posibilidades de disputar la presidencia a Lula, es el actual senador del Partido Liberal (PL), Flávio Bolsonaro. Como digno hijo de su padre, el ex presidente Jair Bolsonaro, viajó a Washington a reunirse con el secretario de Estado, para planear la campaña en contra de Lula, lo que resultó en la aplicación de aranceles del 50 % a importantes productos provenientes de Brasil, pretendiendo afectar a todo el pueblo de Brasil, con la intención de robarle apoyo al gobierno de Lula. Pocos días después de esta visita, llegó Rubio a declarar que, “Brasil no es amigo de Estados Unidos”, lo cual fue dirigido a genera malestar y angustia en las clases medias y altas del país.


Flavio Bolsonaro también visitó Tel Aviv, buscando el apoyo de Netanyahu y ofreció cambiar la embajada de Brasil a Jerusalem, en caso de ganar las elecciones. El apoyo sionista es muy importante, ya que tienen relaciones muy importantes con los grandes grupos económico-financieros que manejan la economía brasileña y mundial. title: Nationale Demo - Smash Imperialism - 11. Oktober
content:
Bewegung 11. Oktober


Der Imperialismus hat seine Transformation in eine neue Phase begonnen. Die Hegemonie des von den USA angeführten imperialistischen Blocks läutet ihr eigenes Ende ein. Dies zeigt sich – um nur einige Beispiele zu nennen – in eskalierenden Angriffskriegen (Iran), Genoziden (Palästina, Sudan) und Ressourcenkriegen (Kongo). Ebenso werden im Stellvertreterkrieg zwischen der NATO und Russland in der Ukraine abertausende Leben von oftmals zwangsrekrutierten Arbeiter:innen für europäische und US-Interessen geopfert. Andernorts bestrebt das US-Imperium – wie sich in Kuba und Venezuela in äusserster Brutalität zeigt – verstärkt den absoluten Machtanspruch auf Lateinamerika, in US-Perspektive als eigene Einflusszone angesehen, auch "backyard" genannt.


Aus Angst unterzugehen, schlägt die Bestie wild um sich. Die materielle Übermacht schwindet immer mehr und der Hauptkonkurrent China – und damit auch viele Verbündete der Volksrepublik – gewinnt an globalem Einfluss. Die Kapitalist:innen schüren Krise um Krise: Sei es der unmittelbar bevorstehende Klimakollaps, die Faschisierung der westlichen Staaten, die zunehmende Überwachung durch KI und die aggressive Umverteilung von unten nach oben.


Die Lügen der herrschenden Klasse werden immer offensichtlicher. Sie versuchen uns für dumm zu verkaufen, indem sie uns erzählen, in Gaza gäbe es einen Waffenstillstand. Indem sie legitimen und notwendigen Widerstand als "Terrorismus" deklarieren. Indem sie Palästina als "Israel" bezeichnen. Damit versuchen sie den Status Quo aufrechtzuerhalten: Eine weisse Vorherrschaft, die es ihnen erlaubt, ungebremst Kapital anzuhäufen und ihr Territorium gewaltsam zu erweitern.


Im Kongo fördern multinationale Konzerne im Dienste westlicher Mächte seit über 30 Jahren Genozid, um das Land im Chaos versinken zu lassen. Durch aktive Destabilisierung lassen sich die Ressourcen leichter abbauen und das Land ausbeuten. Dasselbe geschieht im Sudan, wo ein sogenannter "Bürgerkrieg" befeuert wird, um die zahlreichen Bodenschätze auszubeuten.


Dies sind nur einige wenige Beispiele von zu vielen, die aufzeigen, dass Millionen von Menschenleben (vor allem Schwarzes und Braunes Leben) den Herrschenden scheissegal sind. Was zählt, sind kurzfristige Gewinne. Alles auf Kosten von Mensch und Natur.


Das US-Imperium agiert dabei mit einer militärischen Gewalt und einer Grösse, die alle bisherigen Ausmasse übersteigt. Weiter ist das US-Militär der mit Abstand grösste Einzelverbraucher fossiler Brennstoffe und damit der grösste Umweltverschmutzer der Welt.


Unsere individuellen Initiativen, die Umwelt zu schützen und zu respektieren, verenden im Angesicht der wütenden Bestie in völliger Bedeutungslosigkeit. Doch der Fokus auf individuelles Konsumverhalten offenbart einen tieferliegenden Mechanismus: Nachhaltiges Verhalten wird zum Massstab erhoben und wer davon abweicht, wird verurteilt. Die Logik dahinter: "Divide and rule"


So wird unser Fokus und unsere Energie auf die gegenseitige Kontrolle gelegt, anstatt die Tausenden von Bomben zu stoppen, die Mensch und Natur komplett zerstören. Symptombekämpfung wird als Lösung hochstilisiert; wertvolle Zeit, die wir im Kampf für Klimagerechtigkeit brauchen könnten, geht verloren.


Wir müssen endlich verstehen: Der Kampf gegen die globale Kriegsmaschinerie und der Kampf für Klimagerechtigkeit ist ein und derselbe Kampf!


Die bürgerliche Demokratie möchte uns klarmachen, dass wir mittels Abstimmungen etwas verändern können und verkauft uns, dass wir mit unserem individuellen Konsumverhalten die Natur "retten können". Demokratie gibt uns zu verstehen: "Alle Menschen sind gleich". Doch wenn wir genauer hinschauen, verstehen wir die bürgerliche Demokratie als Teil des Problems. Denn auch sie ist nur ein Mittel, das Volk zu unterdrücken und eines freien Lebens zu berauben und somit die Kapitalinteressen der herschenden Klasse zu befriedigen. Unter dem Vorwand der "Demokratsierung" (eigentlich "Zivilisierung") werden seit jeher Länder angegriffen, Überausbeutung legitimiert und Proteste gewaltsam niedergeschlagen. Die Aussengrenzen werden aufgerüstet, Menschen illegalisiert. Militarisierung und Aufrüstung wird auf Kosten der Gesundheit und Bildung vorangetrieben. Faschistoides Gedankengut schiesst wie Pilze aus dem Boden und zeigt sich in Form von Parteien, in Gesetzesvorlagen, in medialer Hetze, oder dem Antifa-Verbot. title: „Die Kürzungen sind unerträglich“: Ein breites Bündnis hat den Kampf zur Verteidigung des öffentlichen Bildungswesens in Madrid aufgenommen
content:
Dossier


„

Mehr als 20 Organisationen haben sich zusammengeschlossen, um zu versuchen, das, was sie als Plan der Regionalregierung zur Dekapitalisierung des öffentlichen Bildungswesens zugunsten des privaten Bildungswesens ansehen, rückgängig zu machen. Mit dem Ruf „Bildungsqualität oder unbefristeter Streik“ haben Tausende von Menschen heute Morgen im Zentrum der Hauptstadt mehr Mittel für die öffentliche Bildung in Madrid gefordert. An der von mehr als 20 Organisationen, darunter Gewerkschaften, Universitätsversammlungen und verschiedene soziale Gruppen, organisierten Demonstration nahmen Vertreter und konkrete Forderungen aus allen Bildungsbereichen, von den 0- bis 3-Jährigen bis zu den Studenten und der Berufsausbildung, sowie politische Parteien teil. Nach Angaben der Organisatoren nahmen etwa 120.000 Menschen an der Demonstration teil

…“ So beginnt der umfangreiche span.

Artikel von Guillermo Martínez vom 23. Februar 2025 in elDiario.es


 (maschinenübersetzt) mit schönen Fotos der Transparente – siehe mehr Infos:


„Rettet das öffentliche Bildungswesen“: Allein zur Mobilisierung für den unbefristeten Streik ab 14. Oktober marschierten 20.000 durch Madrid zur Verteidigung der Rechte auf Bildung aber auch Wohnen


Madrid setzt sich für das öffentliche Bildungswesen ein: Tausende Menschen marschieren von Atocha nach Sol als Auftakt zum unbefristeten Streik


„

Tausende Menschen sind an diesem Sonntag in Madrid auf die Straße gegangen, um bei einer Großdemonstration, die durch die Hauptverkehrsachse der Hauptstadt von der Nähe des Bahnhofs Atocha (Cuesta de Moyano) bis zur Puerta del Sol führte, für das öffentliche Bildungswesen einzutreten. Der Protest, der gemeinsam von Gewerkschaften, Studentenorganisationen und Familienverbänden organisiert wurde, ist ein klares Zeichen der Stärke im Vorfeld des unbefristeten Streiks, der für den kommenden 14. Oktober in allen Bildungsstufen mit Ausnahme der Hochschulen geplant ist. Unter dem Motto „Lehrer und Schüler gemeinsam gegen Ayuso“ skandierten die Demonstranten Parolen und trugen Transparente mit den wichtigsten Forderungen der Branche, die einen Kurswechsel in der Bildungspolitik der Autonomen Gemeinschaft Madrid fordern. Das Gemeinsame Streikkomitee für das öffentliche Bildungswesen in Madrid, das die Mobilisierung initiiert hat, hat eine Reihe von Forderungen formuliert, die sich auf die Verbesserung der Arbeitsbedingungen des Lehrpersonals und der Unterrichtsqualität konzentrieren. (…) Die Demonstration der Bildungsbewegung hat sich an der Puerta del Sol mit zwei weiteren Protestaktionen vereinigt, die am selben Ort stattfinden. Zum einen handelt es sich um das Zeltlager für das Recht auf Wohnen, das in der Nacht vom 26. September nach der Zwangsräumung von Mari Carmen begann und bei dem weiterhin mehr als 150 Zelte auf dem Platz stehen. Zum anderen die Demonstration, zu der der Verband der Nachbarschaftsvereine von Madrid (FRAVM), „Ecologistas en Acción“ und andere Plattformen gegen das LIDER-Gesetz aufgerufen haben, das von der Regierung unter Isabel Díaz Ayuso vorangetriebene regionale Bodengesetz. Die Organisatoren des Bildungsmarsches haben betont, dass dieses Zusammentreffen „die gegenseitige Unterstützung und den gemeinsamen Kampf für die Verteidigung grundlegender Rechte wie Bildung oder Wohnen“ verdeutliche. Der Tag hat eine zunehmende Koordinierung zwischen verschiedenen sozialen Bewegungen in Madrid deutlich gemacht, wobei die Forderungen nach hochwertigen öffentlichen Dienstleistungen mit dem Kampf gegen Immobilienspekulation und für das Recht auf menschenwürdigen Wohnraum verbunden wurden

…“ span.

 mit Fotogalerie (maschinenübersetzt), siehe zum kommenden Streik:

September, gehen sie auf die Straße, um die PP-Regierung zu warnen, was auf sie zukommt, wenn sie die Forderungen nicht akzeptiert.  Wir von den Plattformen für die öffentliche Universität solidarisieren uns mit dem übrigen öffentlichen Bildungswesen, denn dessen Kampf ist auch unser Kampf. Und wir organisieren uns bereits in den Versammlungen, um unsere Kräfte einzuschätzen und zu entscheiden, wie wir die Mobilisierung und den Streik auch auf die Universitäten ausweiten können
