author: Katharine Trendacosta
title: Site-Blocking Will Not Defend IP, No Matter the Bill’s Name
content:
There has been a raft of site-blocking bills in the latest Congress, and the latest is called the “Deterring Extraterritorial Foreign Exploitation of Networks Damaging Intellectual Property” aka the “

DEFEND IP Act

.” The problem is that instead of “defending IP,” this bill will incentivize censorship, overblocking, and bad faith attempts to block access to a website. DEFEND IP Act, and all of these site-blocking proposals, threaten the open web.

 


We keep seeing attempts to pass site-blocking legislation–from SOPA/PIPA in 2012 to

Block BEARD

,

FADPA

, and

ACPA

 this year. Every one of them has at its core the rotten idea that enforcing copyrights requires building a censorship machine for websites into the architecture of the internet. This is, of course, a disaster for a free and open web. There is no way to create a mechanism for blocking access to an entire website that does not invite both deliberate abuse and lots of collateral harm to free and lawful speech.


DEFEND IP deputizes every service provider into a copyright cop, so long as a rightsholder has accused a website of copyright infringement. Let’s be clear: this isn’t about removing access to an infringing work–that already exists via the DMCA. This isn’t about getting damages from the website or the uploader. It is about making an entire website inaccessible for everyone trying to visit it.


DEFEND IP lets any rightsholder go to a court and get an order requiring service providers to block access to an entire website after alleging copyright infringement. What DEFEND IP does not have is any deterrent for someone seeking to block a website in bad faith. There are no punishments for getting a website blocked for protected speech. There are no meaningful remedies for those whose speech is vanished from the internet due to an entire website being disappeared. It creates a one-stop shop for getting an entire website–again, not an instance of infringement but an entire site hosting all sorts of user content–removed. But for those whose business, speech, or access to information is affected, there is no easy way to get the site restored.


DEFEND IP scales up the extraordinary legal structures that already exist for copyright enforcement. In doing so, it likewise scales up the problems those regimes pose to protected speech.

 


We see this with DMCA takedowns all the time. We see it with bad faith

takedowns

 used to silence criticism or commentary. We see it with the voluntary use of copyright filters by sites like YouTube, where seconds of sound matching seconds of sound in another video can prevent an entire work from reaching its audience. In these existing systems, there are at least some mechanisms of challenge available to the targeted creator. DEFEND IP has none. Instead, site owners, users, or readers will have to find a lawyer and go to court and hope to challenge the order, a slow, expensive, and daunting process


Those existing systems are already frustrating for the targeted creators and users, but under DEFEND IP a whole class of people doing protected speech will find themselves deplatformed because of the actions of others


This bill is not a defense of creativity or creators. It is a way to reshape the internet by building a vast new infrastructure of censorship. Congress should put aside DEFEND IP and the failed idea of site-blocking laws, for good.

author: Sofia Little
title: Get the Flock Out
content:
On September 23rd, the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism held a hearing titled “Always Watching: Flock’s Nationwide AI Surveillance Network,” examining the privacy risks, data sharing, and misuse of private automated license plate reader (ALPR) networks.

The hearing was chaired by Sen. Hawley (R-MO) and featured five witnesses, including Lindsey Isaacs, a wrongfully accused driver, Alasdair Whitney from Legislative Counsel Institute for Justice, Sheriff Ross Teeple, Benn Jordan, a self-proclaimed “hacker”, and policy counsel analyst Chad Marlow from the ACLU, where they have coined a campaign called “Get the Flock Out.”

The hearing highlighted pertinent concerns about how ALPR technology can be used and shared. Public concern about Flock cameras has also grown in recent months. A September 2026 Navigator Research survey found that 62% of registered voters were concerned about Flock camera use, including 66% of Democrats, 55% of Republicans, and 70% of Independents.

Flock Safety was founded in 2017 by CEO Garrett Langley, operating as a small startup meant to provide ALPR cameras to homeowners associations and neighborhoods looking to reduce petty theft and local property crimes. Now, it has grown into something alarmingly dystopian: an AI powered network of over 120,000 cameras across 49 states that photograph, scan, tag, and log every driver that passes, whether or not they are suspected of any crime.

License plate reader technologies have existed since the 1970s, in the form of speed, toll, and red-light cameras. These are only triggered by a specific action, such as running a red-light or driving through a toll booth, and only track license plate numbers. The entry of venture capitalist funding and advanced AI technology into the mass surveillance industry has transformed these automatic traffic enforcement cameras into a complex web of invasive surveillance tools.

During the hearing, ACLU’s Mr. Chad Marlow argued that companies operating ALPR systems are profiting from the collection and sharing of information about people’s movements. The ACLU has called for greater limits on how ALPR data can be collected, accessed, and shared.

Privacy concerns extend to how ALPR data can affect people seeking reproductive health care. During the hearing, Sen. Booker (D-NJ) raised concerns that states could use ALPR technology to track people traveling to obtain reproductive care. The concern comes amid documented cases of law enforcement using vehicle surveillance systems to investigate people seeking or suspected of seeking abortion care.

Unfortunately, this ‘hypothetical’ scenario has become the reality for women across the country.

Witnesses Alaster Whitney and Sheriff Ross Teeple both testified about the overreach of Flock’s ALPRs, with Whitney highlighting jurisdiction concerns which police officers have already been accused of taking advantage of.

In Texas, a sheriff’s deputy used 83,000 Flock ALPRs to track a woman who allegedly performed a self-administered abortion, at the behest of her abusive partner. In Massachusetts, a police officer used Flock networks to stalk a former romantic partner who said she had changed her identity to escape from his abuse. In Kentucky, a police officer was accused of searching his child’s mother 1,000 times through Flock’s network, though she has a protective order. The Institute for Justice has catalogued more than 200 incidents of these ALPR abuses, including romantic stalking, wrongful stops and detentions, non-law enforcement use and other types of misconduct.

These encroachments do not just stop here, as Sen. Padilla (D-CA) spotlights the use of loopholes within Flock, which ICE officers take advantage of to track immigrant communities. While Flock has guaranteed no direct access to the Border Patrol subagency, Witness Marlow points out all it takes is one sympathetic person connected to ICE for the agency to obtain access to billions of pictures of citizens, including facial properties.

Concerns about ALPR surveillance have crossed traditional political lines. During the hearing, Sen. Hawley noted that supporters of the Second Amendment have “long feared national databases of any kind.” This has drawn criticism from across the political spectrum highlighting the bipartisan opposition.

While Flock operates as a leading company which produces ALPRs, they are not the sole producers. Companies like Axon and Motorola have slowly begun increasing …

author: EDRi
title: The KIDS Act will make the internet less safe
content:
On 16 September, the European Commission presented the KIDS ACT, its plan for making online experiences safer for young people. Far from being a move to lead the EU towards better digital environments, this move is a missed opportunity to address the root cause of why online platforms are harmful to children – and everyone else. This blog analyse the proposal’s shortcomings.

During her annual address to the European Parliament, the President of the European Commission announced her intention to protect young people from platforms and services that deprive children of their childhood and of their focus. The next day, the Commission published the KIDS ACT (an acronym for ‘Keeping Internet Digital Spaces Accountable and Trustworthy’). This announcement arrives after a period of much debate around protecting young people online, and even announcements of social media bans from countries across Europe. As a response to this discussion, on April 22, youth organisations across Europe came together to demand real change, instead of exclusions and bans, from EU lawmakers.

The Commission had the opportunity to change the rules of the dangerous game that makes people unsafe online. Instead, it’s mostly restricting who gets to play. Not only is the KIDS ACT a terrible proposal, it’s also a missed opportunity for the European Commission to lead the EU towards a safer digital environment for children and everyone else. The proposal instead determines who is allowed to use services built upon harmful design choices, and clumsily tries to make some of these choices safe for a narrow age bracket, rather than addressing why they can be harmful in the first place. In doing so, it leaves largely untouched the business models that put us all at risk, and sets complex standards for safety which will cement Big Tech dominance. Let’s unpack the proposal.

The KIDS ACT mostly delays young people’s exposure to online harms. On the one hand, it would ban social media accounts for those under 15*. On the other hand, it would require companies to apply certain protections to minors’ accounts against pervasive exploitative tracking, intrusive default settings, and AI companions designed to create emotional dependencies, among other risky features.

What is striking is that these protections apply only to people aged 15*-18. It’s as if these services, practices and functionalities will magically cease to be harmful on someone’s 18th birthday. We all remain vulnerable to manipulative design and unfair personalisation even as adults: not even the most digitally literate person can examine every single default setting, decode every recommendation system, or resist every strategically timed prompt designed to get us to keep clicking. Fairness must be built into the environment itself, not left to the skills of the people using it. Many of the measures proposed in the KIDS ACT address harms that are not specific to childhood and were therefore meant to be tackled through the forthcoming Digital Fairness Act (DFA), which the Commission said will address addictive design for all consumers. The risk is that by treating these practices primarily as child-safety problems, the Commission is lowering the ambition of the rules still to come. Under the appearance of acting on online harms, the KIDS ACT may rob us of stronger protections for ALL of us, including children.

The underlying logic of the KIDS ACT is that, while some risks can be mitigated for people aged 15-18, those under 15* years old should be banned from social media altogether. This blanket age-based exclusion treats children’s online presence as the problem, rather than following young people’s own call to examine the conditions under which digital services expose them to harm. Under the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child, young people — including those under 15 — have the fundamental right, online and offline, to participate in society, access information, communicate with others, play, and develop their identities. Age-gates undermine these rights.

They would also fundamentally change the open nature of the internet: services would have to treat users as children by default unless they prove their age. The Commission’s approach would create a two-tier internet in which children but also adults who cannot or do not wish to pass an age check are excluded from spaces that have become important for education, socialisation, access to information and participation in public life. Open Source Is Not the Same Thing as Liberation

Open Source Is a Tool, Not a Commandment

There is a peculiar form of ideological dogmatism that has emerged within parts of the FOSS movement. Even in anarchist circles, some people seem to believe that opposition to intellectual property must take precedence over virtually every other ethical consideration. After all, if copyright, patents, and other forms of intellectual property are inherently illegitimate, then any attempt to place limits on how the things we create are used or distributed must necessarily be reactionary, right? Even when those limits are intended to protect workers, creators, and wider communities from exploitation by capital?

Anarchists do not seek to abolish one particular category of property while leaving other relations of domination untouched. Nor do we advocate stripping workers of control over the fruits of their labor in the name of an ideological dogma that ultimately has little to do with fostering anarchism.

The rise of so-called “generative AI” has made this contradiction impossible to ignore. My recent essay on this technology was criticized by some open-source diehards because, in their view, no one has the right to restrict the flow of information — even when that flow gushes directly from the minds and labor of workers and creatives into the bulging bank accounts of Silicon Valley billionaires.

To be clear: I am not opposed to free and open-source software. The forum I run (Raddle.me) was built on software (Postmill) that my cofounder released into the commons from the outset under a FOSS license. Even when fascists forked her code to spread hate and harassment, and when a scummy developer violated the license and tried to pass her work off as his own for profit, we did not respond by retreating behind a closed-source license. As anti-authoritarians and anti-capitalists, we certainly could have justified doing so when her work was being used to harm marginalized communities and enrich capitalists, but the license was kept open.

The same principle applies to my own writing. I release all of my essays freely, and I give zine-makers permission to reprint them without restriction. I believe in sharing knowledge and making creative work accessible. People have the option to donate to support my work if they want to. What I oppose is capital taking that generosity, enclosing it within a for-profit ecosystem, and turning it into another mechanism for extracting wealth from the people who created it.

This is not an argument that copyright is inherently liberatory. It is an argument that the abolition of intellectual property is not, by itself, liberation.

I feel compelled to take a stand against the increasingly rigid open-source absolutism that has taken hold in parts of the milieu: against the ruling class taking our collective knowledge, privatizing it, and selling it back to us. I do not consider this a pro-IP argument, but I’m sure plenty of people will disagree. It is an argument against AI slop …

author: Slingshot robot #1
title: Live in the Real World
content:
Our dependence on our phones isn’t an accident. We depend on them logistically for our navigation, payment, and communication. But our phones and the apps they contain are also designed to build emotional dependence — there are entire teams of top-of-their-field psychologists, engineers, sociologists, and designers getting paid hundreds of thousands of dollars a year to make apps even just a little bit more addictive. The emotional and logistical dependence on our phones intertwine in a mutual feedback loop, making it difficult to reduce either.

Every interaction we have with our phones deepens opportunities for state surveillance. Our online activity creates a database of our interests, purchase history, friend networks, location, and activism that the FBI of yesteryear could only have dreamed of. But the biggest problem, as with any addiction, is how something that is fun and useful in small doses can start to take more and more of our time and attention, preventing us from doing other things that we value. So what is there to do?

For most of us, the apps that most deeply build psychological dependence on our phones are social media apps and games. These often take, in some ways, the place of cigarettes in our society today — we do them on a quick break, or when we need to ‘unwind’. But like nicotine, they mostly sate the need that they themselves create. After unwinding in this way, do you feel deeply rested and reset?

If there is an app that you feel wastes your time, or you dislike how much you use, just delete it! You can always re-download it. Note down in your organizer the date and time you deleted the app, and why. If you redownload the app, note that down too. It’s helpful to understand our own patterns of use, to help us understand where we use “tools” or “toys” out of necessity or fun, versus out of psychological dependence.

Think about other activities you can do when you would have used your phone. If you delete an app, it’s easy for some other app to quickly replace it. Be realistic about what might feel fulfilling and restful while deprogramming, in those times and in that headspace. Watching landscapes slide past, noticing the people around you, thinking about your present, past or future, having a conversation with a friend or stranger, reading: each of these might feel more wholesome or restful than your phone. Your Slingshot organizer may be able help you… Don’t you think the edges of the date pages could use additional intricate doodles? Or perhaps you can journal a bit, filling in past date entries with what you remember doing, seeing, eating, or thinking on that day? Use the blank pages in the back to write poetry or outline a manifesto or draw art. Let your boredom be a canvas, a portal to discovery, not something to avoid.

These activities won’t feel as stimulating or give you the same dopamine rush as the apps you’re used to. It’s normal to feel a sense of confusion or loss in this process. Perhaps at some deep level the bright, shifting light of the screen feels like a flickering fire: a thousand generations of finding safety and community in campfires draws us inexorably to this bright cold flame. Try changing your phone’s settings to have the display be in black and white, or switch to a dimmer, less attractive color palette.

We can also feel emotional dependence on the instant knowledge and communication phones provide. What if we can’t respond right away to a friend or loved one? It’s so easy to ask a question to AI like Siri or Google and get an affirming answer! Like puppies or young children, we become anxious without the constant presence of that communication or knowledge. Try consciously pushing your limits more often — if you don’t know something, discuss it rather than looking up ‘the answer’ right away. Delete search bars and AI assistants from your phone and download the Wikipedia app, so if you do need to look something up, you will break that instant gratification loop, finding your own answer and giving yourself context along the way. And try setting aside a specific time of the day to answer your messages. Let friends or loved ones know you might not respond quickly outside of that time.

Logistical dependence is hard in a different way. Practical uses for our phones are often the most problematic sites of government and corporate surveillance, and reinforce emotional dependence by repeatedly forcing us back to our screens.

author: Monica Atieno, Angela Chukunzira and Athandiwe Saba
title: Inside Kenya’s Hidden Deals with Big Tech
content:
When an outsourcing company working for Meta found itself being sued in Kenya, it took its problem to the President.


The dispute had begun in May 2022, when former Facebook content moderator Daniel Motaung sued Sama and Meta over working conditions. Another 43 moderators brought a case in March 2023. The workers had been employed by Sama to moderate Facebook content, work that required them to repeatedly view disturbing material. They argued that Meta, which ultimately benefited from and controlled aspects of their work, should also be held responsible.


Sama was not a minor contractor in Kenya. It was part of the labour pipeline that allowed a global technology company to outsource some of the most harmful work of the internet to Kenyan workers. Meta fought to remove itself from the litigation, arguing, among other things, that Kenyan courts did not have jurisdiction over the foreign company. But on 20 September 2024, the Court of Appeal rejected that argument.


Then on 11 November 2024, less than two months after that ruling, the Business Laws (Amendment) Bill was published. It proposed new rules for Kenya’s outsourcing industry, including provisions dealing with who should carry responsibility for workers employed by outsourcing companies.


Less than a month later, on 9 December, President William Ruto publicly said Sama had approached him about its legal troubles. “Now I can report to you that we have changed the law,” he said, adding that “nobody will take you to court again on any matter.”


But the bill was still before Parliament, where a fight was unfolding over who should be held responsible for outsourced workers. Business groups including KEPSA and the Kenya Association of Manufacturers

argued

 that responsibility should largely remain with the outsourcing company. Tech workers argued that companies that control or benefit from their work should also be held responsible. This was very important for workers trying to sue companies such as Meta rather than only their local contractors.


Figure 1: Africa Tech Workers Movement members during a joint press conference in August 2025, raising concerns about the Business Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024.


The workers also went to court to try to stop the bill. In June 2026, the High Court

declined

 to intervene. On 19 August 2026, the National Assembly passed the amendments. It now awaits for presidential assent. 


For James Oyange, a former content moderator, Ruto’s statement sent a clear message about whose side the government was on. Workers had gone to court seeking protection from some of the world’s most powerful technology companies; instead, he said, the government appeared to be changing the rules in the companies’ favour.


“We are on our own. It is the responsibility of the government to protect us, but they are taking Big Tech’s side. It means the companies can do what they want.”


Oyange fears that if technology companies can turn to the government when workers sue them, while workers are left with fewer ways to hold those companies responsible, the balance of power shifts even further away from workers.


The Sama case is one part of a much wider relationship between Kenya’s government and global technology companies.

The Continent

 identified at least 12 publicly documented meetings, agreements, regulatory engagements and partnerships between the Kenyan government and Microsoft, Google, Amazon, TikTok and Starlink since 2023.


The investigation also found a pattern across these relationships. Major technology companies are being brought into public services, infrastructure and policymaking, often through agreements the public cannot see. At the same time, laws and policies are being developed that can make it easier for these companies to operate. What is much harder to find is who negotiated these arrangements, what Kenya agreed to in return, and who is checking whether they serve the public interest.


Agriculture is one example. In 2020, the Ministry of Agriculture signed an agreement with Microsoft to use technology to

improve farming and food security.

 Microsoft would provide cloud technology for digital tools using information about weather, pests, farming inputs and production.


The partnership expanded in 2022, when AGRA joined Microsoft on a digital agriculture programme that included Agribot known as Kuzabot, a service that sends farmers advice by SMS and WhatsApp. According to the

Community Alliance for Global Justice’s …

author: Brian Hioe
title: Does China Intend to Target Taiwan With New National Security Legislation?
content:
TAIWANESE GOVERNMENT officials, speaking under conditions of anonymity to the media, have warned that China may roll out national security legislation directed at Taiwan in the coming months. Such national security legislation would follow up on China’s recently passed ethnic unity law.

The law criminalizes actions aimed at disrupting a vaguely defined “national unity”. Although initial warnings were that the law was mainly aimed at Tibetans and Uyghurs, the Lai administration has framed such national security legislation as potentially a threat to Taiwan. Under such laws, after all, support for Taiwanese independence–or even just maintaining Taiwan’s current democratic freedoms and its de facto independence–could be construed as illegal and criminal under the law.

Such Taiwanese government officials have pointed to a number of laws, some of which are still in the review process, as potentially impacting Taiwan. This includes the Regulations of the State Council on Exit and Entry Administration, Measures for the Supervision and Inspection of Cyberspace Security, and National Defense Mobilization Law.

In particular, the Regulations of the State Council on Exit and Entry Administration could be used to prevent Taiwanese who have traveled to China from leaving. This already occurred in the past, however, most prominently in the case of activist Lee Ming-che, who spent over five years in Chinese jails on charges of seeking to subvert the state. Lee is thought to have been detained over exchanges with Chinese friends on Taiwan’s experiences regarding democratization. Others imprisoned, however, have been noted to include pan-Blue academics, who seem to have fallen afoul of espionage charges in spite of pro-unification viewpoints.

Measures on cybersecurity take place at a time when the Chinese government has attempted to depict Taiwan as engaged in cyberattacks against critical infrastructure. Such allegations seem to be an attempt to depict Taiwan as engaged in the same activity it routinely accuses China of being engaged in, seeing as China consistently conducts cyberattacks on Taiwan and probes key infrastructure. Importantly, such allegations could also be used to cement a casus belli to justify war.

Indeed, to this extent, the National Defense Mobilization Law has been warned as potentially intended to provide the legal grounds for wartime mobilization. Indeed, such a law might be necessary ahead of a Chinese invasion, particularly if the Chinese government intends to move Chinese society as a whole toward war footing, and mobilize all of society to conduct an invasion.

Still, at a time of highly polarized politics between the KMT and DPP, it can be expected that the KMT will probably deny that China has intentions for future national security legislation. KMT chair Cheng Li-wun has, of course, attempted to depict China as only having goodwill toward Taiwan, while depicting the DPP as, in fact, the ones who have sought to provoke China. As such claims to the media are made ahead of elections in November, they will be depicted as simply intended to drum up public fear for the sake of electioneering.

author: kinder des zorns
title: Feuer der KI-Kriegsindustrie! CleanTech Business Park Marzahn sabotiert
content:
„

Was haben die Zielauswahl durch die israelischen Streitkräfte (IDF) im Gaza-Krieg, die Verschleppungen durch die US-Migrationsbehörde ICE und die sogenannte Abwendung drohender Gefahren durch deutsche Landespolizeien gemeinsam? Sie setzen ein neues Modell datengetriebener Herrschaft über Menschen durch, ein Modell, das von wenigen Tech-Konzernen kontrolliert wird. Es basiert auf den Daten, die wir alle täglich bei der Nutzung der Systeme von Unternehmen wie Meta, X, OpenAI und Google erzeugen. […] Unsere zivilen Daten sind notwendiger Bestandteil dieser zivil-militärischen Infrastruktur – oder andersherum: Es gibt keine rein zivile Nutzung zivil-militärisch entwickelter Technologien! Wir sind Teil der KI-Kriegsindustrie und Teil der Zerstörung! […] Es ist an der Zeit, […] aus der Architektur des Krieges zu desertieren, verbunden mit der konsequenten Sabotage der vielfältigen Prozesse und Knotenpunkte, in denen sich das Zivile ins Militärische einwebt.“


Wir haben uns den Aufruf „

KI beginnt hier

“ zu Herzen genommen und einen der sensibelsten Bereiche zivil-militärischer Technologien angegriffen. Durch gezielte Brandlegungen¹ an dutzenden Starkstromkabeln haben wir die Stromzufuhr des CleanTech Business Parks am Stadtrand von Berlin-Marzahn unterbrochen und damit mehreren Unternehmen, die mit ihren Halbleitern/Mikrochips, Präzisionsmaschinen und elektronischen Hochleistungsbauteilen das Gehirn und das Herz des technologischen Angriffs bilden, die Lebensadern durchtrennt. Konkret gilt unsere Sabotage den Produktionshallen von Swissbit Germany AG, Finetech und Emerson/Flexim. Alle drei Firmen fertigen Dual-Use-Produkte. Diese finden sowohl in vermeintlich zivilen Bereichen wie Rechenzentren, der Luft- und Raumfahrt, der Öl- und Gasförderung, in Atomreaktoren, Windkraftanlagen oder im Bergbau Anwendung als auch in nahezu allen modernen Waffensystemen. Zu ihren Abnehmern zählen Sicherheitsbehörden, das Militär und Unternehmen der Rüstungsindustrie. Bereits ein kurzzeitiger Stromausfall kann ihre hochspezialisierten Fertigungsanlagen erheblich beschädigen und zu wochenlangen Verzögerungen führen. Genau das war unsere Absicht.


Wir haben lange abgewogen, ob die Sabotage von Stromleitungen derzeit ein angemessenes Mittel im Kampf für eine andere, gerechtere Welt ist. Angesichts der Auswirkungen des Stromausfalls im Januar infolge der Sabotage des Gaskraftwerks Lichterfelde haben wir diese Entscheidung nicht leichtfertig getroffen. Dass wir uns trotzdem dafür entschieden haben, ist in erster Linie eine Konsequenzen aus dem Scheitern anderer Protest- und Aktionsformen. Diese haben sich in Anbetracht der globalen Eskalation von Kriegen, Wettrüsten, Artensterben, Umweltzerstörungen, Flutkatastrophen, Waldbränden, Hitzetoten und einem erstarkenden Faschismus vielfach als unzureichend erwiesen. Wir sind der Meinung, dass die Zeit der Symbolpolitik und des guten Willens ein Ende haben muss. Wir wollen die Abläufe kapitalistischer Ausbeutung wirksam und unmittelbar unterbrechen und den Profiteur:innen von Krieg und Umweltzerstörung spürbare wirtschaftliche Verluste zufügen. So wie es andere in den vergangenen Monaten getan haben. Außerdem soll die Aufmerksamkeit, die eine solche Aktion erzeugt, dem Image Berlins als Investitionsstandort für Technologie- und Rüstungsunternehmen nachhaltig schaden. All dies halten wir aktuell für dringend notwendig und ist erklärtes Ziel dieser Unterbrechung. Aber auch in Sachen Repression und staatlicher Gewalt scheint uns der Weg der nächtlichen Sabotage sicherer zu sein als z. B. Demos, die zunehmend von Schikanen, Einschüchterungen und brutalen Festnahmen geprägt sind. Sich bei Aktionen vor Ort festnehmen zu lassen, – wie es andere aus der Klimagerechtigkeits- und Antikriegsbewegung praktizieren – um Gerichtsprozesse als Bühne zu nutzen und an das Gewissen der herrschenden Rechtsprechung zu appellieren, oder bei der Räumung von Sitzblockaden auf die Nachsicht der Cops zu hoffen, halten wir angesichts einer zunehmenden Faschisierung jedoch für gefährlich und naiv. Trotzdem gilt allen Repressionsbetroffenen natürlich unsere volle Solidarität.


Ein weiteres Kriterium für die Ausführung unserer Tat war, dass ein Stromausfall, dessen Ausmaß wir im Vorhinein nicht vollumfänglich abschätzen konnten, bei spätsommerlichen Temperaturen für mögliche Betroffene, die nicht das eigentliche Ziel unserer Aktion sind, weniger einschneidend ist. Wir waren bemüht, durch die Auswahl des Ortes unserer …

title: Rusya'dan Ukrayna'ya kapsamlı saldırı: Askeri sanayi tesisleri hedef alındı
content:
Rusya Savunma Bakanlığı, Ukrayna’ya gece saatlerinde kara, deniz ve havadan fırlatılan yüksek hassasiyetli silahlar ile insansız hava araçları kullanılarak kapsamlı saldırı düzenlendiğini açıkladı.

Bakanlığın açıklamasına göre saldırıların hedefinde, Ukrayna’nın savunma sanayisine yönelik üretim faaliyetleri yürütülen tesisler yer aldı.

Rusya Savunma Bakanlığı, saldırılarda özellikle “Flamingo” seyir füzeleri ile uzun ve orta menzilli İHA’ların üretimi ve depolanmasında kullanılan tesislerin hedef alındığını öne sürdü.

Açıklamada söz konusu tesislerin, Ukrayna merkezli Fire Point şirketinin faaliyetleri kapsamında kullanıldığı belirtildi.

Kiev ve Kiev bölgesinin yanı sıra Çernigiv, Kirovograd, Dnipropetrovsk, Poltava ve Harkiv bölgelerindeki askeri sanayi tesislerinin de saldırıların hedefi olduğu kaydedildi.

Rusya Savunma Bakanlığı, Odessa bölgesindeki liman ve gemi onarım altyapısının da saldırılarda hedef alındığını bildirdi.

Açıklamada ayrıca Ukrayna ordusunun çıkarları doğrultusunda kullanılan bazı deniz araçlarının vurulduğu ileri sürüldü.

Rusya Savunma Bakanlığı’nın ikinci açıklamasında ise Rus hava savunma sistemlerinin gece boyunca ülkenin farklı bölgelerinde 311 Ukrayna İHA’sını imha ettiği iddia edildi.

Rus makamları tarafından paylaşılan bu bilgilere ilişkin Ukrayna tarafından yapılmış bağımsız bir doğrulama ya da saldırıların yol açtığı hasara ilişkin ayrıntılı bilgi ise açıklamada yer almadı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Pela 1ª vez desde redemocratização, Brasil terá 10 militares no Congresso e nos governos
content:
Investigamos o que importa para os brasileiros além do que passa na campanha eleitoral. Leia mais reportagens como essa clicando

aqui

.


Dois governadores, dois senadores, quatro deputados federais e 23 suplentes no Congresso Nacional. Esse é o saldo das eleições para uma categoria muito próxima da direita e do bolsonarismo: os militares das Forças Armadas. Com raízes no Exército Brasileiro, um oficial de alta patente e dois de baixa patente são os responsáveis por fazerem dos resultados do último domingo (4) um marco histórico na militarização da política no país.


Nome forte do bolsonarismo na Câmara dos Deputados, o tenente-coronel da reserva do Exército Luciano Zucco (PL) teve 58% dos votos válidos para se tornar o primeiro militar das Forças Armadas eleito governador do Rio Grande do Sul desde os anos 1950 – quando o também tenente-coronel do Exército

Ernesto Dornelles

 foi eleito.


Um amigo de Zucco dos tempos de Academia Militar das Agulhas Negras (Aman), também se reelegeu governador no 1º turno – o capitão da reserva Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos), com mais de 62% dos votos válidos em São Paulo. Isso torna esta a primeira

vez que

dois governadores ex-Forças Armadas

 são eleitos desde a redemocratização.


Zucco vai governar o Rio Grande do Sul ao mesmo tempo em que o colega de Aman Tarcísio de Freitas estará à frente de São Paulo


No Senado, a partir de janeiro de 2027 dois militares se juntarão ao general da reserva do Exército Hamilton Mourão (Republicanos-RS), um dos

fiadores do início da carreira política de Zucco

, em 2018, e ao tenente-coronel aviador da reserva da Aeronáutica Marcos Pontes (PL-SP): o capitão da reserva Renan Contar (PL-MS) e o 3º sargento reformado do Exército Antônio Nicoletti (PL-RR). Desde a Constituição de 1988, o Congresso Nacional nunca teve quatro senadores oriundos das Forças Armadas.


Mais de 856 mil eleitores votaram no capitão Contar para senador em Mato Grosso do Sul, na eleição seguinte àquela em que ele quase se elegeu governador com

apoio direto

 do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro (PL). Antes, em 2018, o ex-capitão do Exército já tinha se tornado o deputado estadual mais bem votado da história de Mato Grosso do Sul, com 78 mil votos – marco não superado em 2026.


Atualmente deputado federal, o 3º sargento do Exército Antônio Nicoletti se elegeu senador por Roraima com apoio direto do candidato Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ). Ele deixou a caserna para fazer carreira na Polícia Rodoviária Federal (PRF), mas enfatiza até hoje nas redes sociais a sua origem como “militar do Exército”. No governo Bolsonaro, Antônio Nicoletti foi inclusive homenageado pelo Exército com a honraria da Medalha do Pacificador, como mostra o

boletim

 da Força de julho de 2021.


Antônio Nicoletti foi eleito por Roraima e será um dos quatro militares a ocuparem cadeiras no Senado


Para o professor de Relações Internacionais da Universidade de Brasília (UnB) Juliano Cortinhas, o avanço de candidaturas militares destoa da aproximação das Forças Armadas com a candidatura (e o próprio mandato) do ex-capitão do Exército Jair Bolsonaro.


“Vejo que as Forças Armadas se afastaram da família Bolsonaro durante o atual governo, e, nesta corrida eleitoral, o Flávio não contou com eles, nem se aproximou. Então acho que vemos um movimento de indivíduos, mais do que propriamente da instituição militar, diferentemente do que ocorreu em 2018”, avalia Cortinhas, que coordena o Grupo de Estudos e Pesquisas em Segurança Internacional da UnB.


“Acho que o resultado do 1º turno das eleições sugere uma nova tendência, com cada vez mais militares candidatando-se a cargos eletivos daqui pra frente. Mas isso é um problema porque, em geral, militares são despreparados politicamente, seja por sua formação ideológica, seja pelo fato de não serem forjados para a política – e, na minha opinião, eles não devem ser preparados para tal, sob o risco de não cumprirem sua função”, afirma.


Já para o co-autor do estudo

Fardados Partidos

, que reflete sobre as relações históricas entre as Forças Armadas e a política no Brasil, pesquisador e doutor em antropologia social pela Universidade Federal de São Carlos (UFSCar) Guilherme Lemos, o resultado das urnas mostra falhas do atual governo e de seus antecessores em separar os quartéis da política partidária.

author: By Brendan Maslauskas Dunn, Contributor
title: Waging Peace in a Time of War in Thailand and Cambodia
content:
The fog of war has not fully dissipated from the mountains and dense forests of Cambodia and Thailand’s borderlands, well over a year after the two nations became ensnared in deadly clashes. It is still unclear who fired the first shot, although both governments blame the other side for starting the conflict. Both armies left a wake of destruction in many of the normally peaceful, serene villages and towns along the border. It may take years to repair the damage caused by the fighting. 


At the peak of the conflict,

rockets rained down on houses and hospitals in Thailand

. Civilians at a 7-Eleven in Thailand met their fate in an inferno of flames

caused by a Cambodian rocket that struck the building

. In Cambodia, children ran in a panic when their schools were evacuated. Thai F-16 fighter jets flew over Cambodia on

bombing missions

.


The ancient Khmer (Cambodian) temple and UNESCO World Heritage site

Preah Vihear was barraged by ordnance from the Thai army

,

shattering parts of it into pieces

.

. Hundreds of thousands of Thai and Khmer civilians were displaced from their villages, and moved into makeshift shelters. Many have not yet returned home.


In total,

at least 30 civilians in Cambodia, and 44 in Thailand were killed

, with many more wounded. The Royal Thai Army laid to rest 43 soldiers. The Cambodian government has not publicly disclosed the total number of soldiers killed but

estimates range from 73 to over 160

.


 A victim lies on the ground in front of the 7-Eleven and gas station that was struck by a 

Cambodian rocket in Sisaket Province, Thailand. Eight people were killed, and 13 injured. Scores of civilians have been killed in both Thailand and Cambodia during the conflict. (Source:

Royal Thai Army / AFP

)


Both countries agreed to a ceasefire in December, brokered by the U.S. and Malaysian governments, but this peace hangs delicately in the balance in a political environment overshadowed by the dominance of hyper nationalism and militarism, and the rapid spread of hatred and bigotry between Thai and Khmer people. Much of this has been fueled by social media, conspiracy theories, and AI. Since the conflict started, ruling elites and military hardliners in Thailand and Cambodia have consolidated more power and tightened the gears of repression.


Kosal Sorphea sits at the funeral ceremony for her mother, Mut Savern, 43, who was a 

Cambodian soldier. Mut was pregnant when she was killed by a bomb dropped from a Thai F-

16 jet during an airstrike in December 2025. (Photo: 

Cambodianess

)


In the midst of the politically volatile whirlwind where many citizens have lined up in support of their respective governments and militaries, a scattered network of Thai and Khmer activists forged solidarity with each other, spoke out against war and demanded peace at a time when it seemed impossible, even dangerous to do so.


‘We Firmly Oppose this War’


Paw Cratchang said she shut down her social media accounts when the fighting started between Cambodia and Thailand. The nationalist views expressed by many Thais, even from her friends, was “overwhelming,” she says. “People always think that war is black and white. They should have someone to lose and should have someone to win, and they hope the winning side is going to be their country,” she says. The reality, she explains, is much more complex.


“I was born in Surin province. It’s on the border with Cambodia,” she says. “Sometimes we speak a little bit of Thai and Cambodian language. It’s kind of like a mix.” Growing up so close to the border left an imprint on her understanding of national identity. “We are friends, we are relatives. People cross the border many times. They don’t think there’s a difference between each other,” she says of Khmer and Thai people.


And although she is a Thai citizen she says her family is “100% Lao” but were “colonized by Thailand” over the years. She also feels a deep affinity with and affection for Khmer people. 


Thai activists protesting against the Thailand-Cambodia border conflict on December 13, 2025 

in Chiang Mai, Thailand. The signs on far left and right both say ‘No war.’ The sign at middle says ‘Get to the negotiating table to find a peaceful solution.’ (Source: 

Prachatai

)


Cratchang is an anarchist. She holds a sharp critique of nationalism, nation-states, and borders. The Cambodian-Thai border, to her, is an arbitrary line that has ushered in a history of disaster and violence …

L'inscription obligatoire à France Travail de tous-tes les privé-es d'emploi relève d'un fichage à grande échelle de la population. L'objectif est bien sûr de saturer le marché du travail et d'imposer n'importe quel emploi à n'importe quelles conditions afin de tirer les salaires vers le bas pour ainsi satisfaire les seuls besoins des patrons.


Pour mettre en œuvre sa politique de contrôle et de criminalisation du chômage, le gouvernement renforce régulièrement son arsenal de sanctions à l'égard des chômeur-es. Le décret du 30 mai 2025 sur le nouveau régime de sanctions a été un virage particulièrement brutal et s'étend dorénavant aux franges les ptus précaires de la société comme les allocataires du

RSA

Alors que Parcours Sup permet de verrouiller l'accès aux études supérieures, les salons de recrutement s'enchaînent. Cette année, 120 000 jeunes ont été éjecté-es du parcours universitaire. author: webadmin
title: The Rural Connections Behind Illegal Hunting
content:
Thanks to Wiltshire Hunt Sabs for this guest post, who, alongside Cirencester Illegal Hunt Watch, Bristol Hunt Sabs and Bath Hunt Sabs, have been keeping the pressure on the Beaufort Hunt.


The Duke of Beaufort’s Hunt is one of Britain’s most prominent fox hunts and has been terrorising wildlife across the countryside surrounding the Badminton Estate in Gloucestershire for hundreds of years. But the Beaufort Hunt does not exist in isolation. Behind it lies a wider rural network of landowners, estate managers and property professionals.


One of the most striking examples is Rupert Sturgis, Partner and Head of Knight Frank’s Cirencester office.


Rupert Sturgis, Partner and Head of Knight Frank, Cirencester. Image: Wiltshire Hunt Sabs


Knight Frank’s website describes Sturgis as specialising in the sale of town and country property across Gloucestershire and North Wiltshire.


Screenshot:

Knight Frank


He is also a Field Master of the Beaufort Hunt.


On Saturday we filmed Rupert directing the field riders to surround a covert. This is so foxes become trapped inside, whilst hounds are sent in to kill them. It’s a classic cubbing technique that teaches the new hounds to kill.


Rupert Sturgis directing the field to surround the covert in a classic cubbing formation. Image: Wiltshire Hunt Sabs


Watch the video below


Rupert’s role with the hunt is not recent. In 2015, Horse & Hound described him as an estate agent who was then in his 12th season as a Beaufort Field Master.


Image: Wiltshire Hunt Sabs


The Field describes him as a Beaufort Field Master, quoting him discussing the hunting country where they were openly hunting foxes just last Saturday, and where our drone was shot down in December 2025:

“Field Master Rupert Sturgis recommends the Widleys hedges as part of a run west from Common Wood Farm”

.


Beanie Sturgis laying a trail of cigarette ash. Image: Wiltshire Hunt Sabs


His wife, Beanie Sturgis, is also a Beaufort Field Master. Badminton Horse Trials states that she married Rupert in 2007 and describes her as a Beaufort Field Master, as well as an event organiser, show judge and course designer. Beanie accepted a community resolution in respect of a hate crime committed against a hunt sab in October 2024.


Knight Frank and the Badminton Estate


The connection between Knight Frank and the Badminton Estate goes well beyond Rupert Sturgis. In fact, Knight Frank has been involved with the estate for decades, with senior figures from the firm becoming closely involved in the management structure surrounding Badminton.


In its 2015 Rural Report, Knight Frank stated that it had been involved with the Badminton Estate for 15 years. The report featured Simon Dring, then Badminton’s senior resident agent, who said he had worked at the estate for more than 30 years, including 15 years as senior resident agent. He described working closely with the Duke and his family, as well as coordinating the various specialists and advisers involved with the estate.


Dring retired from the Knight Frank LLP partnership on 31 December 2016, but his relationship with Badminton continued for almost another decade. He remained the estate’s senior resident agent until his retirement from Badminton in late 2025.


Dring once hilariously told us, via deluded hunt supporters, that we couldn’t fly our drone in the ‘Duke’s air space’.


Companies House records show that he was secretary of Swangrove Estates Ltd from 31 March 2000 until 9 March 2026. The company is registered at the Estate Office, Badminton, and its stated business is mixed farming. He was also secretary of Swangrove Holdings Ltd from 31 March 2000 until 9 March 2026, another company registered at the Badminton Estate Office.


Both companies show current officers including members of the Somerset family alongside other directors. The records show the overlap between the people managing the estate and the companies through which its interests are held.


And Dring is not the only former Knight Frank figure with a connection to the Badminton Estate.


Christopher Smith, who was a Knight Frank partner heading its rural consultancy, renewables and energy consultancy, is now listed as a person with significant control of Badminton Hospitality Ltd, with ownership and voting rights of 75% or more. His correspondence address is the Badminton Estate Office.


Alexander (Sandy) Douglas provides another link. He has been a director of Swangrove Estates Ltd since 2000 …

author: Lucas
title: Veganes Wichteln
content:
Veganes Wichteln mit ARIWA geht in die nächste Runde

Danke an über 500 Wichtel beim veganen Wichteln 2025!

Bei der Aktion „Veganes Wichteln 2026 von ARIWA“ senden sich unbekannte Personen Überraschungspakete. Was verschenkt wird, ist dabei komplett offen, unterliegt aber zwei Bedingungen: Der Inhalt muss komplett vegan sein und das Geschenk soll von Herzen kommen.


Es kann gebastelt, gehäkelt, genäht, gebacken werden, du kannst zum Laden um die Ecke gehen und eine Kleinigkeit kaufen – Hauptsache ist, dass du dich ebenfalls über den Inhalt freuen würdest! Deiner Kreativität ist daher keine Grenze gesetzt!


So funktioniert das Vegane Wichteln von ARIWA

1.

Anmelden

: Trage dich im Formular unten mit deiner E-Mail-Adresse ein. Teilnehmen können alle Menschen mit einer Postanschrift in Deutschland.


2.

Bestätigen

: Nach dem Absenden bekommst du sofort einen 6-stelligen Code per E-Mail. Gib ihn direkt im Formular ein – fertig! Kommt keine Mail an, schau im Spam-Ordner nach oder fordere im Formular einen neuen Code an. Solltest du dich vertippt haben, kannst du deine Adresse dort korrigieren.


3.

Adresse erhalten

: Nach dem Anmeldeschluss wird jedem Wichtel per E-Mail die Adresse einer anderen Person zugeteilt – auf magische Weise (und ein bisschen IT-Zauber).


4.

Paket verschicken

: Pack dein Überraschungspaket und schicke es bis spätestens 10. Dezember 2026 los.


5.

Freuen

: Jetzt heißt es abwarten – bald erreicht dein Überraschungspaket die Postadresse deines Wichtels und du bekommst im Gegenzug ein Paket voller Überraschungen.


6.

Danke sagen

: Ist dein Paket angekommen? Über den Link in deiner E-Mail gibst du deinem Wichtel Bescheid und kannst ihm eine kleine Nachricht schicken.


7.

Teilen & verbreiten

: Hilf uns, das vegane Wichteln noch bekannter zu machen! Verteile unseren

Aushang

 oder erzähle deinen Freund*innen auf Social Media davon. Vielen Dank für deine Unterstützung!


Rückblick

Nach über 300 Wichtel-Paketen im Jahr 2023 haben

2024 und 2025 sogar jeweils mehr als 500 Menschen

 beim veganen Wichteln von ARIWA mitgemacht!

Damit hätten wir nicht gerechnet – umso schöner zu sehen, wie viel Freude es euch bereitet, Überraschungspakete zu packen und zu verschicken.


Wir – das Wichtelteam von ARIWA – sagen von Herzen

Danke

 an alle Teilnehmenden. Eure lieben Mails, Dankesworte und guten Wünsche haben uns sehr berührt.


Darum ist klar: Auch 2026 wird es wieder ein veganes Wichteln geben!


Anmeldeschluss: 23. November 2026


Hinweise zum Paket

Was ist vegan?


Veganes enthält keine tierischen Bestandteile wie Milch, Fleisch, Eier, Honig oder auch Bienenwachs, Leder, Wolle. Es ist so hergestellt worden, dass dafür kein Tier leiden musste.


Solltest du dir nicht ganz sicher sein, dann schreib uns unter

wichteln@ariwa.org

.


Wie hoch sollte der Wert des Geschenkes sein?


Der Paketinhalt sollte bei ca. 10 € exklusive Verpackungs- und Versandkosten liegen. Selbstgemachtes ist immer schön, jedoch kein Muss. Wenn du eher nicht zu den Do-it-yourself-Menschen gehörst, freuen sich die Händler*innen bei dir vor Ort.


Können Lebensmittel verschickt werden?

Dies ist möglich, jedoch mit Einschränkungen:


Bitte beachte die jeweils individuell angegebenen Allergien, diese erhältst du direkt mit der Versandadresse.


Bitte verschicke keine Kühlware!


Verpacke die Lebensmittel ordnungsgemäß und am besten luftdicht.


Verzichte bitte gänzlich auf Alkohol! Das Vegane Wichteln steht allen Personen offen und es können auch Kinder unter den Beschenkten sein.


Bitte beschrifte deine Geschenke eindeutig, sodass die beschenkte Person weiß, was sie da gerade genießt. Lege auch gerne das Rezept bei! Wenn du zum Beispiel selbst gebackene Plätzchen verschickst, empfehlen wir, die Zutatenliste beizulegen – für den Fall, dass Allergien bestehen.


Wann solltest du das Paket verschicken?


Spätestens zum 10. Dezember solltest du das Paket versendet haben. Wir erinnern dich daran via E-Mail. Es wäre sehr schade und traurig, wenn eine Person sich auf dein Paket freut und nichts ankommt!


Kann ich mich mit meinem Wichtel austauschen?


Ja! Wenn du bei der Anmeldung zustimmst und dein Wichtelpartner ebenfalls, bekommst du mit der Adresse auch die Mailadresse – so kannst du z.B. nachfragen, ob alles angekommen ist.


Außerdem findest du in deiner Mail einen Link „Paket ist angekommen“. Darüber sagst du der Person, die dich beschenkt hat, Bescheid und kannst ihr eine kleine Dankesnachricht schicken …

title: Dixon Mink Farm in Bluffdale, Utah will be Forced to Close
content:
Dixon Mink Farm at 15028 Pony Express Road in the town of Bluffdale, Utah will be forced to close.

The city council of Bluffdale has eliminated fur farming as a permitted use. Fur farms will be unable to operate in Bluffdale.

The councilperson who pushed for the change said:

“I saw the serious issue the mink farm had on the lives of our residents. As I knocked on doors of our independence area there were so many flies people couldn’t open their door to talk to me. Because of this ordinance change the city can not approve the business license for this or any other mink farm.”

Moreover, Christopher Harshaw and his research assistant Anna are personally responsible for the killing of hundreds of animals per year, sometimes as many as 30-50 in a single day, as noted in Harshaw’s “Euthanasia Log” notebook, which on a previous visit was removed, had its pages photocopied (along with other documents related to animal research) and then put back. His death tally: 323 in 2023 (rats and mice), 575 in 2024 (rats and mice, including one wild mouse caught in a live trap and killed on the premises), and 363 in 2025 (all mice). His method: gassing them to death with co2.


Extensive video was also taken documenting the decrepit conditions of the lab as well as Roberto Refinetti’s animal room full of cages formerly housing squirrels (empty at the time of filming).


As should be clear: the purpose of this action wasn’t to vandalize, nor was it mere opportunism. This was a carefully planned and orchestrated live liberation of mice from Chris Harshaw’s lab. Its only purpose was getting the animals to safety as quickly as possible, therefore no equipment was damaged and no messages left at the scene. The whole operation, from entering the building to exiting with the animals, took ten minutes.


It should also be noted: This action was carried out using a minimum number of tools (none) and a minimum number of personnel (one).


This proves not only that lab raids can still be completed in 2026 but that one person, working alone, can successfully accomplish them.


To Chris Harshaw: Accessing your lab was child’s play, and with the hammer and drill on site it would have been only too easy to decommission every piece of equipment you own. Consider this a warning. In the end you were shown more mercy than the animals you hold captive.


And a word to all you would-be liberators out there: These facilities are not the fortresses you think they are. They are not impregnable. In fact the animal abusers in white coats have become so secure in their belief that no one is watching that they sometimes don’t even bother locking their doors! Use this negligence to your advantage. And while they sleep, go and do your work.


THE LAB RAID IS BACK.


Nine go free…


Another victory for the animals,

author: winter oak
title: Never Accidentally Offer Luxury Recycled Cream Cakes to Portuguese Vegan Punks!
content:
This is the fifth and final chapter from the book 

King of the Squatters

 by jaybo which we are delighted to be able to share on Winter Oak. The whole text can be found as a pdf

here

.


I had enjoyed going for food at the social centre twice weekly. But it became tiresome for me to recognise blatant hierarchies and leaders when their on-line blurb claimed that they were anarchists against leaders, organised along horizontal lines, not vertical, top-down power structures. But my relationship with the social centre was completely destroyed one afternoon, after I had just recycled some expensive, fancy cream cakes.


In front of our house, a fiesta had been happening all weekend, so lots of drunken revellers engulfed our usually quiet home. Our squat had been under siege for the three days, being attacked by young adults who threw stones and came into our building looking for trouble. I had not been sleeping well and was very tired one day as I ate some luxury recycled cream cakes in the city centre. Then the social centre’s leader passed me and stopped to speak. We had only ever seen each other previously at the centre, never in public. I offered yer man a fancy cake, without thinking that they were patently not vegan.


He refused and asked me exactly where our squat was. I innocently told him directions to our home. Then he left to go on a demonstration against workers’ exploitation. That night as I walked home, I was stopped dead in my tracks by fresh graffiti on the bridge just before our squat. In big white letters it simply stated, “vegan limit!!!” I had no doubt that the vegan punk anarchist leader had just sprayed the graffiti as some kind of attempted bullshit intimidation directed at me. Because I had offered to share my hard-earned cakes with him.


I never went back to the social centre after that. I was so angry that I knew if I had returned then I would have certainly made trouble and probably have given the leader an excuse to ban me anyway. I hate egos and authoritarians. However, as always, I tried to turn a negative into a positive. That incident inspired one of my most popular signs for The Whimsical Atrocity Theatre (TWAT): “I only eat vegans”.


The next day, TWAT proudly unveiled its new message to the world. It worked immediately. The show was good. I was a little bit worried that one or more of the social centre vegan punks would pass by, see the sign and beat me up. I was probably safe in my theatre, as I usually had a police escort at one side, looking out for the tourists’ safety. But they knew where I lived.


Some brave souls came and spoke to me during or after my cardboard shenanigans. But things reached dizzying heights for TWAT when an American woman came up to me and asked me how much my signs were. I was absolutely flabbergasted. Someone wanted to buy my recycled carton signs. I replied to her spontaneously that, if she wanted to buy a sign, then she had to tell me how much it was. She put four euros into my hat for “I only eat vegans”. Black permanent marker pen on quality recycled cardboard.


Women were flirting with me almost every day when I performed, but I was caught completely off guard when an extremely attractive, well-dressed young French woman came up to me with her friends, picked up the condoms and said, “OK, let’s go!” She was absolutely serious and in a pathetic response, I replied, “You’re wearing a wedding ring.” She countered with, “It’s only an engagement ring. This is my last chance. Are you coming?” Her friends’ looks assured me that she was absolutely serious. I did not go. One of her friends looked at me as though I must have been insane. One of several potentially delicious sexual opportunities that I missed in life.


As the summer really heated up, it felt as though all of Portugal’s crazy folk were coming out of the woodwork and heading for fun in Lisbon. As I worked one day, a sun-drenched, handsome, young man swaggered up the steps towards me. He wore rags as clothes, had matted, unkempt hair flopping all over his face and had a long stick over his shoulder, with a cloth bundle tied up at the other end. He asked if he could write something on one of my signs. I told him he could, so he picked up “this sign was my bed” and wrote on it, “but I washed it in my jacuzzi first”, which killed me and the audience. Then he shouted for all to hear, “We are homeless because we choose to be.”


Before his departure, he asked me if he could take a condom because …

author: PETA-Team
title: Geheimsache Tierversuche: Neue ZDF-Doku zeigt Tierleid hinter verschlossenen Labortüren
content:
Symbolbild


Die neue „37°“-Dokumentation „Geheimsache Tierversuche – Unter Ausschluss der Öffentlichkeit“ geht der Frage nach, was eigentlich mit Tieren in Versuchslaboren geschieht – und warum die Öffentlichkeit so wenig davon sehen darf.


Am 

29. September 2026 um 22:15 Uhr im ZDF

 sehen die Zuschauer:innen hinter die Kulissen einer Branche, in der Mäuse, Ratten, Hunde, Affen, Kaninchen, Schweine und viele weitere Tiere für Experimente missbraucht werden.


Millionen Tiere leiden für „wissenschaftliche Zwecke“


Nach den offiziellen Zahlen wurden in Deutschland

im Jahr 2024 über drei Millionen Tiere

 für „wissenschaftliche Zwecke“ missbraucht. Einen großen Teil nimmt die Grundlagenforschung ein, in der Tieren zum Beispiel der Schädel aufgebohrt wird, um Elektroden in ihr Gehirn zu setzen. In regulatorischen, gesetzlich vorgeschriebenen Tests werden die Tiere teils vergiftet und getötet.


Solche Experimente finden nicht irgendwo weit entfernt statt, sondern an verschiedenen Forschungseinrichtungen in Deutschland.

Experimente an Affen

, die in der Dokumentation ebenfalls thematisiert werden, sind in der Hälfte der Bundesländer vertreten.


Was passiert in den Versuchslaboren?


Für die Dokumentation hat der Journalist Manfred Karremann mehr als ein Jahr lang versucht, Einblicke in deutsche Tierversuchslabore zu bekommen. Trotz angebotener Anonymität erklärte sich nur eine Einrichtung bereit, ein wenig Einblick zu geben.


Die Dokumentation macht damit ein Problem sichtbar, das Tierschützer:innen seit Jahren kritisieren: Tierversuche finden weitgehend im Verborgenen statt. Sie werden verharmlost und die wenigsten Menschen erfahren, was den Tieren tatsächlich angetan wird. Dabei geht es um Lebewesen, die Angst und Schmerzen empfinden wie wir – und die schlichtweg nicht dazu da sind, dass wir an ihnen experimentieren.


Die Dokumentation zeigt unter anderem Aufnahmen aus einem britischen Labor. Zu sehen sind Hunde,

Affen

, Kaninchen und Ratten, die für sogenannte

Giftigkeitstests

 missbraucht werden. Die Versuche gelten als standardisierte Verfahren und werden nach internationalen Richtlinien durchgeführt – auch in der EU. Tiere müssen dabei beispielsweise Chemikalien einatmen oder bekommen Testsubstanzen über einen Schlauch direkt in den Magen verabreicht.


Jetzt lesen


Forschung und Medizin


Tierversuche in Deutschland: Was wirklich in den Versuchslaboren passiert


In deutschen Tierversuchslaboren werden Affen, Hunde, Katzen, Nagetiere, Fische & Insekten gequält. Erfahren Sie hier mehr über die Versuche!


Jetzt lesen


Tierversuche sind keine gute Wissenschaft


Tierversuche werden oft als „wissenschaftlich notwendig“ gerechtfertigt – doch die Dokumentation zeigt, dass die Wissenschaft längst mit Methoden arbeitet, die ohne Tiermissbrauch auskommen. Expert:innen aus Industrie und Wissenschaft kommen zu Wort und erklären, warum modernste Methoden wie menschliche Zellkulturen oder Organs-on-a-Chip Tierversuchen nicht nur ethisch, sondern auch wissenschaftlich überlegen sind.


Diese Ansätze arbeiten direkt mit menschlichen Zellen und menschlichem Gewebe. Dadurch können sie bei bestimmten Fragestellungen auch Erkenntnisse liefern, die sich besser auf Menschen übertragen lassen.


Jetzt einschalten und hinschauen!


Die „37°“-Dokumentation gibt einen seltenen Einblick in die abgeschottete Welt, in der Tiere in Laboren ihr Leben lang gefangen sind – und zeigt gleichzeitig, warum es längst überfällig ist, dass sich Wissenschaft und Forschung von Tierversuchen abwenden.


„37°: Geheimsache Tierversuche – Unter Ausschluss der Öffentlichkeit“

 läuft am

Dienstag, 29. September 2026, um 22:15 Uhr im ZDF.

 Ab 5:00 Uhr ist die Dokumentation auch über das ZDF-Streaming-Angebot abrufbar.


Jede Unterschrift zählt


PETA fordert von nationalen und internationalen Entscheidungsträger:innen einen strategischen Ausstieg aus Tierversuchen und eine Modernisierung der Forschung. Unterstützen Sie den Research Modernisation Deal und helfen Sie uns, grausame Tierversuche endlich zu beenden.


Jetzt unterschreiben


The post

Geheimsache Tierversuche: Neue ZDF-Doku zeigt Tierleid hinter verschlossenen Labortüren

 appeared first on

PETA Deutschland e.V.

.

title: Nourrir ou trahir. Comment l’élevage intensif saigne la France.
content:
On doit changer de modèle, découvrez comment :

Peu importe qui vous êtes et ce en quoi vous croyez : l’élevage intensif trahit vos valeurs.

Nous mangeons 85 kilos de viande par personne et par an, le double de la moyenne mondiale. Ni accident ni dérive, cette consommation de masse est le produit d’un système dont l’élevage intensif est la pierre angulaire.

Souveraineté alimentaire, santé publique, déforestation, biodiversité, ressource en eau, revenu des agriculteurs, sort des animaux : sur chacun de ces fronts, l’élevage intensif nous trahit. Il nous rend dépendants d’engrais et de soja importés, endette les éleveurs, favorise pandémies et antibiorésistance, nuit à l’environnement et entraîne l’abattage de plus de 3 millions d’animaux chaque jour pour la seule consommation française.

Nous n’avons pas choisi ce modèle. D’autres l’ont choisi pour nous. Ce livre, rédigé par Brigitte Gothière et Sébastien Arsac, cofondateurs de L214, défend une proposition pour reprendre la main ensemble : donnons-nous l’objectif de réduire de moitié le nombre d’animaux tués d’ici 2030. Parce que c’est possible. Parce que c’est vital.

d’animaux abattus chaque jour pour la seule consommation française.

Vous entrez dans un supermarché. Vous prenez un caddie. Vous suivez un itinéraire balisé. Vous voyez ce qui doit être vu, à la hauteur qu'il faut, au prix qu'il faut. Vous croisez la viande partout, les légumineuses presque nulle part. À la sortie, vous avez le sentiment d'avoir choisi.

« On nous a fait croire qu’il fallait choisir son camp : pour les agriculteurs ou pour les animaux, pour le climat ou pour la souveraineté alimentaire. Mais l’élevage intensif ne défend aucun de ces camps, il les renie tous en même temps. C’est ce que ce livre documente, chiffres à l’appui. »

« C’est un livre sur une impasse dont nous devons sortir collectivement. Réduire de moitié le nombre d’animaux tués d’ici 2030 est une nécessité, soutenue par une majorité de Français. Ceux qui croient que l’élevage intensif peut durer se bercent d’illusions. »

Nourrir ou trahir, comment l’élevage intensif saigne la France paru le 30 septembre 2026 aux éditions Payot, disponible au prix de 19 € sur notre boutique en ligne et en librairie.

author: Animal Rising Press
title: Guilty Verdict For King’s Sheep Rescuers In Theft Trial
content:
After a four-day trial at Norwich Crown Court, Rose Patterson, Sarah Foy, and Rosa Sharkey have all been found guilty of theft after the rescue of three lambs from King Charles III’s Sandringham Estate in May 2023. Sentencing to follow today.

Despite the verdict, Animal Rising claims that the rescue and subsequent trial have helped to put a spotlight on the reality behind animal farming in the UK, with over 10 million sheep being slaughtered yearly [1].

The controversial rescue made front-page news across the UK and headlines around the world [2]. It captured the attention of the British public, questioning how we relate to animals in the food system and if it’s a rescue or a theft to take them from farms.

Animal Rising director Rose Patterson, alongside Rosa Sharkey and Sarah Foy, rescued the lambs - Sammy, Sunny and Sooty - before informing police the following day. The women held signs outside Windsor Castle reading “I rescued the King’s sheep” before reporting what they had done to police. They each face up to 7 years' imprisonment.

Earlier this year, Patterson was found not guilty by a jury over another Animal Rising open rescue, after helping to rescue beagle puppies from MBR Acres, a facility breeding animals for testing [3].

Animal Rising director Rose Patterson, one of the three defendants found guilty today, said:

Sammy, Sunny and Sooty remain safe and are now fully grown.

The trial followed a series of open-rescue trials relating to Animal Rising’s rescue of beagles from MBR Acres. In January this year, Animal Rising made history by securing the UK’s first-ever not-guilty verdict in an open-rescue case [4]. The lambs were rescued from Appleton Farm, which forms part of the Sandringham estate.

Defendants Patterson and Foy are available for comment or broadcast interview upon request.

For further information, comment, or to arrange an interview, please email press@animalrising.org or call +44 1225 29 6691

High-Quality Pictures and Videos: https://show.pics.io/animal-rising-breaking-news

All images and videos in this file, on our social media, and website can be used with credit to Animal Rising under ‘fair use’ for the purposes of reporting.

[1] https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/cattle-sheep-and-pig-slaughter

[2] https://www.dailymail.com/news/article-12431619/Animal-Rising-protesters-charged-stealing-Kings-sheep-royal-Sandringham-Estate-driving-away-animals.html

https://www.dailymail.com/news/article-12126009/Will-stop-eco-clowns-Just-Stop-Oil-throw-orange-powder-Animal-Rising-kidnap-lambs.html

[3] https://www.cambsnews.co.uk/peterborough-court-acquittal-animal-rescue-beagles/

[4] https://www.animalrising.org/post/not-guilty-verdict-for-beagle-puppy-rescuers-in-landmark-legal-case

Rose Patterson, 37, is the Director of Animal Rising. An advocate for animals since 2012, she holds an MSc in Animal Welfare Science, Ethics, and Law and previously worked with World Animal Protection before joining Animal Rising in 2020.

Sarah Foy, 26, has been involved in a range of campaigns advocating for a just and sustainable food system that works for animals, farmers, and the planet. She brings a practical, hands-on approach to her advocacy, with real-world experience caring for rescued farm animals at sanctuaries and protesting alongside farmers.

Rosa Sharkey, 26, is a food charity worker. She is passionately committed to reducing the impact of our food system on the climate crisis, community action, and animal rights.

Animal Rising is a nonviolent campaign group working to fundamentally transform our relationship with animals and nature, and build a more sustainable future for animals, people and the planet. Animal Rising is calling on the Government to end factory farming by 2040 and support a transition to a sustainable plant-based food system.

The group has used a variety of civil disobedience and nonviolent direct action tactics, notably blockading McDonald's distribution centres in May 2021, blockading dairy industry sites in September 2022, disrupting the 2023 Grand National, rescuing lambs belonging to King Charles III in May 2023, and carrying out the UK’s largest undercover farm investigation in 2024.

author: Sophie Lemcke
title: So ist es, als Huhn in der Fleischindustrie leben zu müssen
content:
Die Hühnermast ist ein grausames System, das auf maximale Schnelligkeit, Wachstum und Profit ausgelegt ist und mit einem gewaltvollen Tod für die Tiere endet.


Wie fühlt es sich an, als „Masthuhn“ geboren zu werden

, ohne die Möglichkeit, der leidvollen Industrie zu entkommen

?


Der einzige Grund, weshalb die Industrie dich „produziert“ hat: Du sollst so schnell wie möglich so schwer wie möglich werden – und wirst dann getötet.


Du kommst in einem Hühnerschlupfbetrieb mit tausenden anderen Küken zur Welt. Um dich herum piepsen sie verzweifelt. Und auch du suchst nach Nähe und Wärme. Aber da ist keine Mutter, in deren Gefieder du dich kuscheln kannst – und du wirst sie auch niemals kennenlernen.

Noch am ersten Tag deines Lebens wirst du über Förderbänder geschleudert und in eine Kiste gepackt. Dann beginnt die oftmals stundenlange Fahrt zum Mastbetrieb – eingepfercht mit Dutzenden anderen Küken, ohne Wasser, ohne Nahrung.


Foto: Andrew Skowron


Du kommst in einer riesigen Halle an. Hier wirst du die nächsten rund 5 Wochen verbringen – die einzigen Wochen deines Lebens.


Um dich herum Tausende andere Küken. Du teilst dir einen Quadratmeter mit bis zu 23 anderen Tieren. Jetzt seid ihr noch klein, doch das wird sich schnell ändern.


Du wächst. Unnatürlich schnell. Das Futter steht dir Tag und Nacht zur Verfügung – hochkalorisch, proteinreich, entwickelt für maximales Wachstum in kürzester Zeit.


Du hast keinen Platz, um dich natürlich zu bewegen, es gibt nichts zum Erkunden. Keinerlei Möglichkeiten, deine natürlichen Verhaltensweisen auszuleben. Es ist trist und laut. Da ist nur diese Enge.


Die Luft ist stickig. Der Ammoniakgeruch von den Ausscheidungen Tausender Tiere brennt in deinen Augen, in deinen Lungen. Du bekommst Atemwegserkrankungen. Jeder Atemzug tut weh.


Dein Körper wurde durch jahrzehntelange Züchtung so manipuliert, dass du in wenigen Wochen das Gewicht erreichst, für das ein Huhn unter natürlichen Bedingungen Monate bräuchte.


Foto: Andrew Skowron


Deine Brustmuskeln wachsen so schnell und werden so schwer, dass deine Knochen dein Gewicht nicht mehr tragen können. Deine Beine verformen sich. Dein Herz ist zu klein für deinen massiven Körper, es hat Probleme, deine Organe mit ausreichend Blut zu versorgen. Du hast Schmerzen beim Gehen und deine Gelenke sind entzündet.


Um dich herum sind Hühner, die gar nicht mehr aufstehen können. Sie liegen in ihrem eigenen Kot und leiden unter extremen Schmerzen. Sie verdursten und verhungern.


Andere Hühner werden aufgrund der Enge von ihren Artgenossen versehentlich totgetrampelt und erdrückt – ihre Körper verwesen zwischen dir und den tausenden anderen Tieren. Auch du hast keine Chance, den anderen Hühnern auszuweichen.


Dann ist es soweit. Menschen kommen und packen dich. An deinen Beinen, kopfüber, werden du und deine Artgenossen gegriffen und in enge Transportkisten geworfen. Deine ohnehin schon schmerzenden Beine brechen unter der groben Behandlung. Du hast Schmerzen und Todesangst.


Zusammengepfercht, ohne Wasser, ohne Futter, geht es zum Schlachthof. Die Fahrt kann Stunden dauern. Manche Hühner sterben bereits im Transporter – vor Stress, vor Erschöpfung, erdrückt von anderen Tieren.


Foto: Andrew Skowron


Im Schlachthof riechst du Blut. Du hörst die Schreie anderer Hühner. Dann bist du selbst an der Reihe. Unter grausamen Bedingungen wirst du betäubt und getötet. Du bist gerade einmal 35 bis 42 Tage alt geworden.


Es ist unvorstellbar, was Hühner in der Fleischindustrie erleiden müssen.


Die Wahrheit hinter „Hähnchenfleisch“


Wie grausam das kurze Leben von sogenannten Masthühnern ist, haben wir schon mehrfach bei Undercover-Recherchen aufgedeckt, beispielsweise in einem (jetzt ehemaligen) Zuliefererbetrieb der großen Marke Wiesenhof. Hier erfährst du mehr über unsere Aufdeckungen und kannst unsere Petition für strengere Tierschutzvorgaben, -kontrollen und -strafen unterzeichnen:


Jetzt für Hühner unterschreiben 


In Deutschland wird mehr Fleisch von Hühnern konsumiert als produziert – und die Nachfrage ist in den vergangenen Jahren stetig gestiegen. Unterstütze dieses grausame System nicht: Entscheide dich konsequent für pflanzliche Lebensmittel.


In den meisten Supermärkten findest du mittlerweile eine Vielfalt tierfreundlicher Alternativen, die hervorragende Proteinquellen sind – probiere sie aus. Oder koche unsere zahlreichen pflanzlichen Rezepte von Love Veg nach, wie unsere

knusprigen Tofu-Nuggets

.


Erfahre mehr:
